Maxim targets engineering and quality teams shipping production AI features and is available as cloud-hosted SaaS, hybrid (VPC peering), or self-hosted (zero-touch VPC isolation). The company monetizes through tiered SaaS plans and enterprise licenses.

providers.name: Membrane
providers.description: Membrane is an AI-powered platform for building product integrations using natural language. It connects to any API with 282+ pre-built packages and is compatible with AI coding assistants via MCP. There is also a separate open source Membrane API Gateway for REST, SOAP, and GraphQL.

providers.name: Parallel Domain
providers.description: Parallel Domain is a synthetic-data and sensor-simulation platform for physical-AI and autonomy developers. It turns real-world drive and flight logs into photorealistic, simulation-ready digital replicas (PD Replica) and generates deterministic camera, lidar, and radar sensor data at scale (PD Sim), plus self-serve synthetic-data generation through its Data Lab service. The platform is driven through a first-party Python SDK (paralleldomain / pd-sdk) and an app console, integrating with existing autonomy stacks and CI/CD for training, testing, and regulatory validation of perception systems across automotive, trucking, drone, robotics, agriculture, and defense.

providers.name: Auterion
providers.description: Auterion builds the software-defined operating system for autonomous drones and robots. Its open, vendor-independent stack — AuterionOS and the Skynode / Skynode X flight-compute modules — runs across drones from many manufacturers, while Auterion Suite provides cloud fleet management, flight data, and compliance, and Auterion Mission Control is the ground-control planning and flight application. Developers extend vehicles with the on-device Auterion SDK, a C++ app framework built on PX4, MAVLink, and ROS 2. Auterion does not publish a public REST/OpenAPI web API; its developer surface is the on-device SDK plus a set of first-party open-source MAVLink and PX4 libraries on GitHub. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Costanoa Ventures.

providers.name: Latenode
providers.description: Latenode is an enterprise-grade low-code integration and AI automation platform with prebuilt SaaS integrations and native access to top-tier LLMs. It combines the ease of no-code tools with the flexibility of low-code development for building automated workflows. Latenode supports inbound webhooks and JavaScript-based custom logic within scenarios but does not currently publish a public OpenAPI specification for an external REST API.

providers.name: Neuracore
providers.description: Neuracore is an end-to-end cloud platform for robot skill creation. Teams use it to collect teleoperation demonstrations, curate and version datasets, train imitation-learning and reinforcement-learning policies, and deploy them to production robots for real-time inference. The platform is driven by an official Python SDK and command-line interface (pip install neuracore) that stream 14 first-class data modalities to the Neuracore cloud backend at api.neuracore.com, plus a Rust data daemon for high-throughput recording. Founded by Stephen James and backed by Earlybird, Neuracore is used by robotics teams including Anvil Robotics, AIRA, Flexiv and Scale AI.

providers.name: Renovate
providers.description: Renovate is an open source automated dependency update bot maintained by Mend. It scans repositories for references to dependencies across 100+ package managers — npm, pip, poetry, Maven, Gradle, NuGet, Go modules, Cargo, Bundler, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitHub Actions and many more — and opens pull/merge requests that update versions, lockfiles, and digests. Renovate runs as a CLI, Docker container, GitHub App, GitLab Runner, Bitbucket Cloud app, or Azure DevOps integration, supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea, Forgejo, AWS CodeCommit, and Gerrit, and is configured via a renovate.json file with shareable presets, packageRules, automerge, grouping, scheduling, and a Dependency Dashboard. Mend provides a free Community Cloud hosted tier for unlimited public and private repositories and a paid Enterprise Cloud tier with higher concurrency, Merge Confidence Workflows, and support.

providers.name: Telekinesis.ai
providers.description: Telekinesis is a Physical AI company building a unified Python SDK and large-scale "skill library" for industrial robotics and computer vision. Its composable skills span perception (2D/3D detection, segmentation, 6D pose estimation, point clouds), planning, control, reinforcement learning, and Vision-Language-Model agents that orchestrate complete robotics systems. Developers install the official telekinesis-ai SDK from PyPI, authenticate with an API key from platform.telekinesis.ai, and run skills either cloud-hosted or on-premise. The stack includes BabyROS (a lightweight ROS-style pub/sub middleware on Zenoh), a Data Engine for synthetic dataset generation, and NVIDIA Isaac Sim integration for simulation-to-real transfer. Telekinesis targets high-mix manufacturing use cases such as assembly, machine tending, bin picking, CNC loading, and inspection, and is a Techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: DJI
providers.description: DJI (Da-Jiang Innovations) is the world's leading manufacturer of civilian drones, aerial-imaging systems, gimbals, and robotics platforms. Its developer program at developer.dji.com exposes several products for building on DJI hardware: the Cloud API (device management, media, and live streaming for enterprise fleets), the FlightHub 2 API, the Mobile SDK (Android/iOS), the Payload SDK for building custom payloads, the Onboard SDK, the Edge SDK, the Windows SDK, the UX SDK, and the Guidance and RoboMaster SDKs. Developers register an application through a DJI developer account to obtain an App Key, App Secret, and App License that activate SDK and Cloud API access.

providers.name: UnifyApps
providers.description: UnifyApps is an enterprise "AI Operating System" founded in 2023 by Ragy Thomas (founder of Sprinklr) and Pavitar Singh: one platform to build and manage agentic AI solutions, create no-code enterprise applications, automate complex business processes, and replicate data in real time across 1,000+ application integrations, deployable in the cloud or on-premises. Customers expose workflows as REST endpoints (Callable, Webhook, LLM, External API, and Event Stream resources) through the platform's API Manager, and can publish MCP servers whose tools draw on 600+ connectors, custom in-house APIs, and workflows — secured with JWT, OAuth 2.0, Basic, or custom authentication plus rate limiting, quotas, and analytics. UnifyApps has raised $84M+ (Series A led by ICONIQ Growth; $50M Series B led by WestBridge Capital) and is headquartered in New York with offices in Gurugram, Dubai, and Hyderabad.

providers.name: Shell Scripting
providers.description: A collection of APIs and resources for Shell Scripting development, including utilities, documentation, and tools.

providers.name: Mendral
providers.description: Mendral, Inc. is the AI DevOps Engineer — three always-on agents for security, reliability, and performance, plus custom automations for any DevOps work specific to your stack. Built by the team behind Docker and Dagger (founders Sam Alba and Andrea Luzzardi), Mendral installs as a GitHub App and reads your CI/CD logs to review dependency PRs, pin safe package versions, surface exploitable CVEs, diagnose CI failures, fix flaky tests, and cut build times. It integrates with GitHub Actions, AWS, Google Cloud, Datadog, and Sentry, and ships a command-line client for browsing and triaging insights from the terminal or a coding agent. Y Combinator Winter 2026; based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Sea Machines Robotics
providers.description: Sea Machines Robotics builds autonomous command-and-control systems (SM300-SP, SM300-NG) and computer-vision perception (AI-ris) for commercial and defense marine vessels. In September 2025 it announced the SMLink Streaming-API and SMLink Control-API, partner-gated interfaces that stream real-time vessel telemetry to external systems and let approved third parties command SM300 autonomy functions from their own mission software. These interfaces are embedded, vessel-side product features, not a self-service public developer platform; access is arranged through Sea Machines sales.

providers.name: Heex Technologies
providers.description: Heex Technologies builds the Smart-Data Platform, an event-based data management solution for autonomous systems, robotics, and ADAS/AD vehicles. Instead of moving raw big data off fleets, Heex lets engineering teams define Smart Events with pre-set triggers so software agents capture only the most relevant, context-rich data ("Smart-Data") directly at the edge or in the cloud. The platform spans a Heex Agent/SDK deployed on robots and vehicles (Ubuntu x86_64/ARM, ROS/ROS2), a Heex CLI for operating the SDK and Heex Cloud, and a web platform for triggers, events, recordings, and fleet monitoring. It is used across AMRs, industrial robots, smart mobility, and off-road autonomy, with customers and partners including NVIDIA, Siemens, RATP, Vinci, Stanley Robotics, Apex.AI and Helm.AI. Backed by Techstars, Google for Startups, and AWS Activate.

providers.name: Ushur
providers.description: Ushur is an agentic AI platform for customer experience automation (CXA) in regulated industries, including healthcare, insurance, and financial services. Enterprises use Ushur Studio, AI Agents, the Invisible App, intelligent document automation, and the platform's REST APIs and prebuilt integrations to automate end-to-end member, patient, and policyholder journeys across SMS, email, voice, and web channels, with HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, and PCI DSS compliance built in.

providers.name: BMC Software
providers.description: BMC Software is an enterprise software company providing automation, service management, and mainframe solutions for large organizations. Its flagship products include Control-M for application and data workflow orchestration, the BMC AMI portfolio (Automated Mainframe Intelligence) for DevOps, operations, storage, security, and data protection, and BMC Helix for IT service and operations management. BMC exposes programmatic access primarily through the Control-M Automation API (a REST API with Jobs-as-Code), an official Python client (ctm-python-client), a command-line interface (ctm), and a VS Code extension, all maintained under the github.com/controlm organization. Approximately 80% of the Forbes Global 100 rely on BMC technology across financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications, and the public sector.

providers.name: Comulate
providers.description: Comulate is an accounting automation and revenue intelligence platform built for large insurance brokers. It captures carrier statement data across spreadsheets, PDFs, and email, then automatically reconciles direct-bill and carrier-payables transactions against policies to eliminate manual back-office accounting work. Its Revenue Intelligence layer adds commission forecasting, variance tracking, and missing-commission detection. Comulate is delivered as a hosted application at app.comulate.com with native connectors to broker management systems including Epic, BenefitPoint, AMS360, Microsoft Dynamics, and Salesforce. The company was surfaced as a Bond Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: Echelon AI
providers.description: Echelon AI is an AI-workforce platform that automates ServiceNow platform delivery and maintenance, acting as an AI teammate that writes stories, builds catalog items, flows and apps, runs CMDB audits and migrations, and generates Automated Test Framework (ATF) tests — delivering working artifacts live in a customer's instance in hours rather than the traditional multi-month systems integrator timeline. It is a ServiceNow Registered Build and Consulting/ Implementation partner covering ITSM, CMDB, HRSD, CSM, ITOM, SecOps and 30+ modules, connects to development or sub-production instances via OAuth 2.0, logs every action for audit, and is sold as a consumption-based credit model with Starter, Growth and Enterprise tiers. It is a Bain Capital Ventures portfolio company in the ai-apps sector. Echelon AI publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, commercial and security surface.

providers.name: Bubble Lab
providers.description: Bubble Lab is an open-core, agentic workflow automation platform built for developers. Its open-source (Apache-2.0) TypeScript engine lets you compose AI agents and integrations as typed, composable units called "Bubbles" — service bubbles (Slack, Gmail, PostgreSQL, Google Sheets, Airtable, ElevenLabs, Resend, and more) and tool bubbles (web scraping, research agents, SQL, LinkedIn, Reddit, YouTube) — then stitches them into production-grade "BubbleFlow" pipelines with end-to-end type safety, built-in logging, tracing, and step-level observability. Workflows are fully runnable, self-hostable, and exportable to your own backend, or authored visually in the hosted Bubble Studio. Scaffold a project in seconds with the create-bubblelab-app CLI. Backed by Y Combinator (W26).

providers.name: Ansys
providers.description: Ansys is a global engineering simulation company (now part of Synopsys) with a deep portfolio spanning structures (Mechanical, LS-DYNA, Motion), fluids (Fluent, CFX, Rocky), electronics (HFSS, Maxwell, SIwave, Icepak), semiconductors (RedHawk, Totem), optics, photonics, materials (Granta), 3D design (Discovery, SpaceClaim), embedded software (SCADE), and systems (optiSLang, Twin Builder). Ansys also runs Ansys Cloud for burst HPC and offers Ansys Apps in the Cloud. The primary public developer surface is PyAnsys — an open-source family of 45+ Python packages on GitHub (ansys/pyansys metapackage) that wrap individual Ansys products as Pythonic interfaces. There is no public web REST API portal; programmatic access is licensed per product and driven through PyAnsys, ACT (Ansys Customization Toolkit), product scripting (MAPDL, Fluent TUI/Scheme), and Ansys Cloud.

providers.name: IFTTT
providers.description: IFTTT (If This Then That) is a consumer and prosumer automation platform that connects more than 750 apps, devices, and services through conditional Applets that chain triggers to actions. The IFTTT Maker Webhooks service exposes a public HTTP API that lets developers fire triggers and execute Applets from any internet-connected device using a personal Webhooks key for authentication, with both form-encoded and JSON payload variants supported.

providers.name: Savant Labs
providers.description: Savant Labs is an agentic AI platform for business analytics, finance, and data automation. It turns AI conversations into governed, audit-ready agents that automate regulated finance workflows such as month-end close, reconciliations, tax automation, and financial consolidation, with human review and audit-ready evidence. The no-code platform combines data preparation, blending, cleansing, automation, and a Vision Agent that extracts data from PDFs and images, connecting to ERPs (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), data warehouses, BI tools, and spreadsheets through hundreds of pre-built connectors. Savant Labs is SOC 2 Type II certified with GDPR and HIPAA support, and is used by teams at Dell Technologies, ConocoPhillips, and Rover. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta.

providers.name: APIwiz
providers.description: APIwiz is a federated API management platform that streamlines the complete API lifecycle from design through monetization. The low-code platform provides centralized control for organizations managing APIs across multiple cloud environments, with federated gateway control, automated governance, security pipeline, compliance monitoring, and API marketplace capabilities. Trusted by 25K+ managed APIs and 10B+ API volume. Gartner Magic Quadrant Honorable Mention (2023).

providers.name: Dependabot.yml
providers.description: GitHub Dependabot configuration file defining automated dependency update schedules, package ecosystems to monitor, grouping, cooldown, and review assignment rules.

providers.name: Black Ore Technologies
providers.description: Black Ore Technologies is an Austin, Texas AI company building AI infrastructure for tax and financial services. Founded in 2022 by Eyal Shinar (previously founder of the fintech unicorn Fundbox) and Pavel Kapovski, the company emerged from stealth in November 2023 with $60 million in funding led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Oak HC/FT. Its flagship product, Tax Autopilot, combines proprietary AI with federal and state tax codes to autonomously execute the full lifecycle of complex tax returns for Certified Public Accountants and accounting firms, spanning document ingestion, intelligent extraction, return preparation, workpaper generation, and tax software integration (UltraTax, Lacerte, ProConnect). The platform covers 1040 individual returns plus 1041, 1065, and Schedule K-1/K-3 automation, and is used by 40% of the top 20 leading firms. Black Ore does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time; its authentication is handled by an Auth0-hosted OpenID Connect tenant at auth.blackore.ai.

providers.name: Strateos
providers.description: Strateos operates a robotic cloud laboratory for the life sciences, delivering Cloud Lab Automation-as-a-Service so scientists can design, run, and analyze wet-lab experiments remotely and programmatically. Originally founded as Transcriptic, Strateos couples high-throughput robotic lab automation with the Autoprotocol standard and a JSON:API-based web API, letting researchers submit protocols, launch runs, manage projects, inventory, and datasets, and pull results into downstream ML and data-engineering pipelines. It is backed by DCVC and Lux Capital.

providers.name: ABB Robotics
providers.description: ABB Robotics is the robotics and discrete-automation business of ABB Ltd, the Swiss-Swedish multinational headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland. ABB was formed in 1988 from the merger of ASEA (Sweden) and Brown, Boveri & Cie (Switzerland), with ASEA's IRB 6 (1974) considered the world's first microprocessor-controlled industrial robot. ABB Robotics manufactures a broad portfolio of articulated industrial robots, collaborative robots (GoFa, SWIFTI, YuMi), delta robots (FlexPicker / IRB 360), painting and welding robots, and autonomous mobile robots, paired with the OmniCore family of controllers running RobotWare 7 and the RAPID programming language. The developer surface is anchored by Robot Web Services (RWS) — a RESTful HTTP/HTTPS API for IO, RAPID, motion, file service, controller, e-log, subscriptions over WebSockets, and user authentication — plus the PC SDK (.NET) for native controller applications and the RobotStudio SDK (.NET 10 / RobotStudio 2026) for building Add-Ins and SmartComponents. RobotStudio Cloud extends offline programming and simulation into a collaborative browser surface. ABB also boosts RobotStudio with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for AI-driven simulation. The company sells robots, controllers, software licenses, and PowerPac add-ons; RobotStudio Basic is free, RobotStudio Premium is sold by annual subscription via local sales.

providers.name: Apkudo
providers.description: Apkudo is a Baltimore, Maryland based company operating the Device Passport Platform for the connected device supply chain, combining software, AI and advanced robotics to capture trusted data at every stage of a device's life. The platform spans Launch (device certification and testing), Trade In (consumer trade-in and diagnostics), Recover (enterprise IT asset recovery), Process (automated functional and cosmetic grading) and Monetize (liquidation and resale routing), and is built on Device Passport, Device AI and DeviceOS. Apkudo sells a Full Automation Line, a Standalone Automation Unit and a Diagnostic SDK that partners embed into consumer and retail applications; integrations with customer systems are delivered privately under commercial agreement rather than through a public developer program.

providers.name: Aside
providers.description: Aside is an AI-powered browser from a Y Combinator (Fall 2025) startup that runs an autonomous browser agent to complete real work across the logged-in websites you already use — email, dashboards, internal tools, documents, and spreadsheets — without relying on per-service API integrations. It pairs browsing history used as local memory with the first password manager designed for AI agents (hardware-backed encryption, audit logging), keeps data local-first and end-to-end encrypted, and gates sensitive actions like payments and messages behind human approval. For developers, Aside ships a command-line interface, a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and a browser-automation REPL so other agents and coding tools can drive the browser, plus bring-your-own-key support for OpenAI and Anthropic models.

providers.name: Facets
providers.description: Facets is a platform engineering and infrastructure automation platform that unifies provisioning, deployment, and configuration into a single declarative model for governed, secure, and self-serve cloud operations. The Facets Control Plane exposes a REST API for managing blueprints, environments, releases, resources, and integrations across the platform.

providers.name: Transport Canada
providers.description: Transport Canada (Transports Canada) is the federal department that regulates aviation, marine, rail and road transportation in Canada under the Aeronautics Act and the Canadian Aviation Regulations. In travel it is the safety-and-security regulator rather than a participant in distribution — it certifies air operators, registers aircraft on the Canadian Civil Aircraft Register, licenses pilots and drone operators, runs the Civil Aviation Daily Occurrence Reporting System (CADORS) and the Air Cargo Security program, and publishes the Canadian airports layer. It sits entirely outside the GDS/NDC distribution chain; airline economic licensing, all-in fare advertising and the Air Passenger Protection Regulations belong to the separate Canadian Transportation Agency. Its API posture is thin but genuinely open — no developer portal exists at tc.canada.ca, developer./developers./docs. subdomains do not resolve, and no OpenAPI is published anywhere. What does exist is real and ungated: a self-describing JSON/XML Vehicle Recalls Database API at data.tc.gc.ca, an ArcGIS REST and OGC WMS service for Canadian airports with air navigation services, and bulk CSV/XML extracts of CADORS, the Air Cargo Security members list and the vessel registers, all indexed through the Treasury-Board-operated open.canada.ca CKAN Action API under the Open Government Licence – Canada. No key, no account, no accreditation, no contract.

providers.name: Black Ore
providers.description: Black Ore is an enterprise AI company building Tax Autopilot, an AI-native platform that automates tax preparation and review for accounting firms and financial-services professionals. Its models ingest source documents, then classify and extract data using machine learning and computer vision, compute individual (1040) and pass-through (1041/1065, K-1/K-3) returns, generate workpapers, and route results through CPA-supervised quality review, pushing prepared data into existing tax software such as CCH Axcess, Drake, Lacerte, ProSystem fx, and UltraTax. Founded in 2022 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Oak HC/FT, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Khosla Ventures.

providers.name: Instance
providers.description: Instance (Instance Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (Summer 2026) company building a verification layer for robot learning. Their platform ingests raw robot rollouts and episode footage from any robot or camera angle and automatically judges whether a task was completed successfully, returning a verdict with supporting evidence and a detailed subtask breakdown. The company positions itself as the ground-truth / success-detection layer that lets robotics teams trust their training data and train policies faster, and reports its verifier reaching higher accuracy than frontier vision-language models at a fraction of the latency across 10,000+ human-labeled episodes on 7 robot platforms. Founded by MIT computer scientists with backgrounds at SpaceX, AWS, and NASA JPL. Today the product is exposed as a hosted demo (submit videos or capture a live rollout for verification); there is no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Jitterbit
providers.description: Jitterbit is a modern enterprise iPaaS platform infused with AI for API integrations. The Jitterbit Developer Portal provides resources for creating connectors, plugins, templates, and recipes to extend the Jitterbit Harmony platform.

providers.name: Clicks
providers.description: Clicks (Clicks Health) is an AI-native operations company that deploys AI agents to run complete healthcare back-office workflows. Its agents handle revenue cycle management (eligibility and insurance verification, prior authorization, claim status checking, denials management, and patient refunds), patient access, and other repetitive tasks by working inside a customer's existing EHR, practice-management, and payer systems either through APIs or the same screens staff use. Clicks integrates with major health IT platforms including Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, NextGen Healthcare, and MEDITECH, and states it is SOC 2 Type II audited and HIPAA compliant with end-to-end encryption for PHI. Founded in 2025, headquartered in Switzerland, and backed by Y Combinator (F2025).

providers.name: Trilobio
providers.description: Trilobio builds whole-lab automation for genetic engineering, synthetic biology, and life-science research — affordable robotics "built by biologists, for biologists." The platform pairs the Trilobot (a self-calibrating, tool-changing lab robot with 16 deck slots), interchangeable gripper/pipette tools, and Trilobio OS (no-code, GUI-driven protocol design with automatic sample layout, error checking, an automated lab notebook, and LIMS). For developers, Trilobio exposes T-code — the command language of Trilobots — through the open-source Python `tcode-api` package, which drives a Trilobot fleet via a local T-code Servicer and integrates third-party lab devices. Founded in 2021 in San Francisco by Roya Amini-Naieni and Maximilian Schommer; backed by Initialized Capital, Argon Ventures, and Lowercarbon Capital.

providers.name: DeepMind
providers.description: Google DeepMind is an artificial intelligence research laboratory and product organization behind the Gemini and Gemma foundation model families, the AlphaFold protein-structure prediction system, WeatherNext atmospheric forecasting, and Gemini Robotics. Founded in London and now part of Google, DeepMind combines frontier AI research with public and developer-facing model deployment. Its models are exposed to developers through the Google AI / Gemini API and Google AI Studio, while its research tooling ships as first-party open-source JAX libraries (Haiku, Optax, Chex, dm-control, and more) on GitHub and PyPI. Originally an independent startup backed by early investors including Founders Fund before its acquisition by Google.

providers.name: Boston Dynamics
providers.description: Boston Dynamics, a Hyundai Motor Group subsidiary, designs advanced mobile robots including Spot (agile quadruped for dynamic sensing and industrial inspection), Atlas (electric humanoid for manufacturing), Stretch (warehouse case-handling robot), and the Orbit enterprise fleet management platform. Boston Dynamics publishes a public, open-source Spot SDK (Python and C++) on GitHub built on gRPC and Protocol Buffers for developing applications and payloads for Spot; Atlas and Stretch are enterprise products without public APIs.

providers.name: Trope
providers.description: Trope is an AI-native platform that helps ERP implementation partners deliver successful implementations faster, deploying AI agents across discovery, requirements, fit-gap analysis, data migration, approval workflows, UAT scripts, training guides, documentation, and go-live readiness — built for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central consultancies and other implementation teams. Trope also maintains Trope CUA, an open-source MCP-native computer-use agent for background desktop automation on Windows and macOS. Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Amboras
providers.description: Amboras is an AI-native e-commerce platform - positioned as "the AI-native Shopify" - that puts an entire online store on autopilot. Merchants build or rebuild a storefront by talking to AI in natural language, and Amboras then autonomously generates design, copy, and product imagery, runs generative A/B tests, adjusts pricing and offers, and reads first-party analytics to continuously optimize conversion rate, retention, and average order value. It includes integrated checkout via Stripe and PayPal and first-party session, funnel, and revenue tracking with no third-party pixels. Founded in 2025 in San Francisco by Imad and Amin Mokadem, Amboras is a Y Combinator Spring 2026 (P26) company. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation - this record captures its public web and product surface only.

providers.name: Continuous Delivery Foundation
providers.description: The Continuous Delivery Foundation (CDF) is a Linux Foundation project that hosts vendor-neutral open source projects for continuous integration, continuous delivery, and DevOps. It is the home of CDEvents, Jenkins, Spinnaker, Screwdriver, Ortelius, JayeX, and was previously the home of Tekton (now a CNCF graduated project) and other CD-focused tooling.

providers.name: Klang Games
providers.description: Klang Games is an entertainment and game development studio headquartered in Berlin, founded in 2013 by three Icelandic co-founders — Mundi Vondi (CEO), Oddur Snær Magnússon (CTO) and Ívar Emilsson (CCO) — several of whom came out of CCP and EVE Online. Its flagship product is SEED, a persistent large-scale MMO society simulator built on Google Cloud, backed by investors including Animoca Brands, Supercell, LEGO Ventures, Anthos Capital, Kingway Capital and Northzone. Klang publishes no developer platform: there is no API documentation, no SDKs and no partner program. The only publicly discoverable machine interface is the OpenID Connect provider behind SEED player accounts, captured in this repo from its discovery documents.

providers.name: EliseAI
providers.description: EliseAI is an agentic AI platform that automates communications and operations for the housing and healthcare industries. For property management it offers LeasingAI, ResidentAI, EliseCRM, VoiceAI, AI-guided tours, and automation for maintenance, renewals, move-in, delinquency, lease audits and fee transparency across SMS, email, chat and voice channels. For healthcare, its HealthAI automates patient scheduling, intake and communication with HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Elise integrates with leading PMS, CRM, EHR and RCM systems. API and integration access is provisioned through the EliseAI developer portal; the company does not publish a self-serve public OpenAPI. This profile was surfaced as a venture portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: RamAIn
providers.description: RamAIn builds AI agents that automate any UI task with natural language. A Y Combinator (W26) company backed by General Catalyst and Nexus Venture Partners, RamAIn operates web portals, desktop apps, and legacy systems the way a human does — reading screens and interacting with UI elements — then compiles those workflows into reusable, self-healing automations that can be published and managed as APIs. It targets high-friction, document-heavy back-office work across mortgage, finance, healthcare, and insurance.

providers.name: Sweep
providers.description: Sweep is the agentic layer for enterprise systems. By connecting to platforms like Salesforce, Snowflake, ServiceNow, and HubSpot, Sweep reads live metadata and gives AI agents the context they need to understand, plan, and govern changes safely across complex systems. It unifies discovery, design, and build into one continuous workflow — auto-generating living documentation of every flow, field, and rule; visualizing end-to-end business processes; running metadata agents that audit and optimize org configuration; and shipping Salesforce automations, lead routing, alerts, and deduplication without custom code. Sweep also publishes an official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects Salesforce context to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. Sweep is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Homebrew, and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Furhat Robotics
providers.description: Furhat Robotics builds the Furhat social robot, a customizable robotic platform with a back-projected, animated digital face and multi-language voice synthesis designed for natural, multi-party human-robot conversation. Developers build interactions using the Kotlin Skill API and the Furhat SDK (with a Virtual Furhat for desktop development), stream live data through the Realtime API over WebSocket, and rapidly prototype LLM-driven characters with the FurhatAI Creator. A deprecated REST Remote API with an official Python client is also available. Furhat is widely used across academic research, clinical training, mental health, hospitality, and automotive human-machine interaction.

providers.name: Avision
providers.description: Avision is airspace infrastructure for drone and Advanced Air Mobility operations. The platform delivers FAA airspace services — LAANC flight authorizations, B4UFLY airspace awareness, TFRs, NOTAMs, and advisory information — alongside UTM / U-space coordination and prioritization for safely integrating uncrewed aircraft into national airspace. Avision serves commercial Part 107 pilots, recreational (Section 44809) flyers, public-safety and first-responder agencies, airports, and critical-infrastructure operators through web and mobile apps, with a flexible REST API integration offered to enterprise customers and drone manufacturers. The company holds an FAA LOA for BVLOS operations and has completed a UTM production rollout in Switzerland.

providers.name: INFINIT
providers.description: INFINIT is an AI application for Web3 financial execution that lets anyone research, create, and execute DeFi and trading strategies through AI agents. Its Prompt-to-DeFi experience turns natural-language intents into agent-powered, one-workflow on-chain strategies, and its AI-managed trading vault marketplace lets independent strategy managers deploy non-custodial vaults that depositors access through a single workflow. For developers, INFINIT publishes the open-source INFINIT Library and INFINIT CLI — a TypeScript action framework and command-line tool for programmatically deploying and interacting with DeFi protocols including Aave v3, Uniswap v3, Pendle, and INIT Capital, distributed as npm packages under the @infinit-xyz scope. Backed by Electric Capital and EQT Ventures.

providers.name: Aescape
providers.description: Aescape is a New York City lifestyle-robotics company, founded in 2017 by Eric Litman, that builds a fully automated AI-powered robotic massage platform. Its table uses sensors and computer vision to map over one million 3D data points of a person's body, then drives heated robotic arms through massage techniques at a user-selected pressure, duration and focus area, with sessions booked and controlled through a mobile/web app. Sessions run 15 to 60 minutes and the tables are deployed in Equinox clubs, Four Seasons, Marriott and Ritz-Carlton properties, spas and corporate wellness sites across North America, alongside an Aescape One home product. Aescape publishes no public developer API: its consumer app is served by a private AWS API Gateway host (api.aescape.com) and its developer documentation site (developer.aescape.com) is gated behind HTTP Basic auth. The one machine-readable, anonymously reachable contract Aescape does publish is the OpenID Connect discovery document for its Zitadel identity tenant.

providers.name: BDD (Behavior-Driven Development)
providers.description: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) is a software development methodology that combines test-driven development with domain-driven design, encouraging collaboration between developers, QA, and business stakeholders through human-readable test scenarios. The BDD ecosystem includes frameworks, tools, and data providers that enable teams to write specifications in Gherkin syntax (Given-When-Then) and automate those scenarios as executable tests across APIs, UIs, and microservices.

providers.name: Operator Framework
providers.description: The Operator Framework is a CNCF incubating toolkit for building and managing Kubernetes Operators. It includes the Operator SDK for scaffolding and building operators using Go, Ansible, or Helm, the Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM) for installing and managing operators on clusters, and OperatorHub for discovering and sharing operators. The framework codifies operational knowledge into software.

providers.name: Jeeva AI
providers.description: Jeeva AI builds, deploys, and governs autonomous digital workers — AI agents that perceive, reason, act, and remember context across business systems. Workers are deployed with natural-language (no-code) descriptions and automate workflows across revenue, IT, customer service, operations, finance, security, and HR. The platform serves 36,000+ active users, runs production digital workers, and is backed by Sapphire Ventures following a $9M raise. Jeeva AI does not currently publish a public API reference or OpenAPI definition; enrichment here is identity, trust, and security posture.

providers.name: Sintra
providers.description: Sintra is a no-code AI-employees platform that gives small businesses a team of role-based digital workers. It ships 12 specialized AI helpers — such as Soshie (social media), Cassie (customer support), Seomi (SEO), Buddy, and Vizzy (meeting notetaker) — that handle social media, inbox, content, customer support, SEO, and sales and business operations. Users chat with helpers, schedule recurring background tasks, build custom helpers with the Helper Builder, and connect tools like Facebook, Instagram, Gmail, Google Calendar, Outlook, Google Drive, Notion, and Strava through consumer OAuth integrations. Sintra is a portfolio company of Earlybird Venture Capital. As of this profile Sintra publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or API reference — it is an end-user low-code product rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Wenrix
providers.description: Wenrix is an AI infrastructure company for the travel industry, providing embedded AI that helps Online Travel Agencies (OTAs) and Travel Management Companies (TMCs) drive revenue and operational efficiency from search through post-trip servicing. Founded in 2017 and backed by Insight Partners, Wenrix processes roughly $12 billion in annual air volume across 60+ global OTAs and TMCs. Its platform is delivered as three API-first products: FareSight, a predictive price-assurance engine that optimizes pricing across EDIFACT, NDC, GDS, aggregators, and low-cost carriers at both search and post-booking stages; FlexEngine, a flight-flexibility solution offering short- and long-term flexibility, refund guarantees, and price-lock through a single API; and DeepFlow, a post-booking servicing automation layer that automates cancellations, refunds, and changes at 93%+ automation rates and is available as either an API or an MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server. Wenrix operates from offices in Tel Aviv, New York, and Barcelona.

providers.name: iGent
providers.description: iGent AI is a UK-based artificial intelligence company (Altrincham, Cheshire) building Maestro, an autonomous AI software-engineering agent. Maestro pairs adaptive autonomy with an ensemble of frontier AI models to plan, generate, test, and refine code across large multi-file codebases inside secure cloud sandboxes, letting developers start from scratch, upload existing code, or clone a repository. Founded by Sean Ward (CEO) and Martin Szummer (CTO), iGent AI is backed by HV Capital, XTX Markets Ventures, Twinpath VC, 10x Founders, and Dhyan VC. The product publishes developer documentation, a quick-start guide, integrations, skills, and a credits-based billing model. iGent was surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network; it does not currently publish a first-party public REST API.

providers.name: CircuitHub
providers.description: CircuitHub is an on-demand electronics manufacturing platform that provides rapid, low-cost turnkey PCB (printed circuit board) assembly for hardware and robotics teams. Engineers upload their CAD and BOM files (Altium, EAGLE, KiCAD) to an automated web application that reconciles the bill of materials against 35,000+ stocked common parts, generates an instant quote, previews a virtual build, and manufactures small prototype-to-production batches in the USA — with 81% of full turnkey orders shipping within three days and real-time quality metrics for transparency. CircuitHub has delivered over 1.5 million boards and placed 87 million parts for more than 20,000 engineers. The company operates a web application rather than a public developer API; user authentication is handled through an Auth0-hosted OpenID Connect tenant.

providers.name: Cast Corporation
providers.description: Cast Corporation (Cast.app) is an AI-agent platform that automates customer success and post-sales revenue operations for B2B SaaS and technology companies. Its autonomous "digital CSM" agents deliver personalized business reviews, grounded answers, onboarding, usage adoption, churn reduction, renewal influence, and referral workflows across email, in-app, and chat in 17 languages. Cast positions itself as an autopilot layer over an existing stack, connecting natively to 60+ systems including Salesforce, HubSpot, Gainsight, Totango, and data warehouses, with customers such as Pure Storage, HPE, and Aruba Networks. Backed by Techstars. Cast does not currently publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its identity, security posture, and public developer-adjacent surface.

providers.name: Neo.Tax
providers.description: Neo.Tax is an AI-powered tax automation platform that helps enterprises and their accounting teams generate audit-ready R&D tax credit studies, software capitalization (ASC 350-40), and R&D capitalization (IRC Section 174) documentation. The platform ingests engineering and financial data from tools like Jira, GitHub, payroll systems, and Workday and uses large language models and agentic AI to qualify projects under IRC Section 41, eliminating the manual surveys and interviews that traditionally drive R&D tax credit work. Neo.Tax is backed by GV and Uncork Capital and delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS product; it operates a customer application, a help center, a public status page, and a trust center (SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, GDPR) but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: UBIO Automation Cloud
providers.description: UBIO (ubio.ai, formerly ub.io) is a London-based, Techstars-backed web automation company. Its Automation Cloud platform runs automation scripts as jobs through a REST API, automating end-to-end website flows such as flight and hotel booking, broadband signup, insurance quotes, and job applications. Developers create jobs with inputs, receive outputs and lifecycle events, and handle deferred inputs and 3-D Secure through official JavaScript/TypeScript client libraries, with the ubio Automation Protocol defining typed input/output schemas for more than 50 automation domains.

providers.name: Alkira
providers.description: Alkira delivers Network Infrastructure as a Service (NaaS) through its Cloud Services Exchange, letting enterprises build, deploy, and manage a global multi-cloud network from a unified portal without provisioning physical hardware. The platform connects clouds, sites, remote users, and SaaS through Cloud Exchange Points (CXPs) with built-in segmentation, routing, integrated firewall/security services (Palo Alto, Fortinet, Check Point, Cisco, Zscaler, Infoblox, F5), and full-stack visibility. Everything provisioned in the portal is driven by the Alkira Portal REST API and exposed as infrastructure-as-code via an official Terraform provider, a Go client library, and a published Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents.

providers.name: Habitat Lab
providers.description: Habitat Lab is Meta AI Research's embodied AI simulation platform. It provides documentation, quickstart code, and tools for training and evaluating AI agents in photorealistic 3D environments, with Habitat 2.0 focusing on household rearrangement tasks. Habitat Lab is delivered as a Python research library; it does not currently expose a public HTTP API.

providers.name: Newton
providers.description: Newton is a Linux Foundation open source physics engine, contributed by Disney Research, NVIDIA, and Google DeepMind. Built on NVIDIA Warp and integrating MuJoCo Warp as a backend, Newton targets roboticists and simulation researchers, providing GPU-accelerated, differentiable, OpenUSD-compatible physics simulation for AI training, robotics, gaming, and scientific research.

providers.name: Zeroqode
providers.description: Zeroqode is a leading no-code development platform and Bubble agency that provides app templates, plugins, courses, and automation tools for building scalable applications without coding. It offers 800+ plugins for Bubble.io, the Air Native mobile app conversion service, and Framer plugins. Zeroqode helps founders and developers build apps 10x faster using no-code and AI tooling.

providers.name: Gecko Robotics
providers.description: Gecko Robotics is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania based AI and robotics company that inspects and manages critical physical infrastructure. Its wall-climbing, aerial and submersible robots capture full-coverage ultrasonic, visual and other sensor readings from boilers, pressure vessels, tanks, pipelines, ship hulls and decks, which are fused with facility records and operational data inside Cantilever, the company's AI-powered operating platform for the built world. Cantilever quantifies corrosion rates, predicts remaining asset life and prioritizes capital and maintenance decisions for customers across defense, power, oil and gas, steel, pulp and paper, mining and advanced manufacturing. Cantilever is delivered as a closed, authenticated enterprise SaaS at cantilever.app; Gecko Robotics publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or self-serve API program, and integrations are arranged through the company directly.

providers.name: XAG
providers.description: XAG (Guangzhou, China) is an agricultural technology company building autonomous farming solutions: agricultural drones (P150 Max, P150, P100 Pro, P60), R100/R200 agricultural ground rovers, the APC2 AutoPilot console, and smart-farm IoT devices. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. XAG operates a Chinese-language developer Open Platform (open.xa.com) that integrates application management, device data authorization, secure data communication, and message subscription, providing APIs for second-party development on XAG products; public API documentation is still largely unpublished.

providers.name: Double Robotics
providers.description: Double Robotics builds telepresence robots for hybrid work and education, best known for the self-driving Double 3 videoconferencing robot and the earlier iPad-based Double 2. Its developer program spans three surfaces: the Double 3 SDK (a local command-and-event API exposed over a Unix domain socket on the robot, covering base movement, navigation, PTZ cameras, depth sensors, WebRTC calling, and standby/sidebar apps), iOS SDKs for the Double 2 (Basic Control and Camera Kit), and a Fleet REST API for programmatic access to fleet-management data such as robots, users, call logs, and visitor passes. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC-portfolio discovery and enriched against the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: Energy Robotics
providers.description: Energy Robotics GmbH, now trading as Korial, is a Darmstadt, Germany enterprise AI platform (spun out of TU Darmstadt robotics research) for fully autonomous industrial operations. It is hardware-agnostic, unifying mixed-vendor robots, legged and tracked ground robots, drones, fixed cameras, and field sensors into a single governed AI operating layer that turns live telemetry into verified insight and orchestrated action across oil & gas, chemicals, power & utilities, and critical infrastructure. The platform spans four modules: Kore (the AI core with LLM, agentic workflows, embedded AI skills, and fleet/device supervision), Connect (an integration backbone exposing bidirectional governed APIs into ERP, EAM, SCADA, historians and ICS/OT systems), Recreate (digital twins and mission simulation), and Sustain (support, onboarding, and managed mission execution). Korial reports 1,000,000+ autonomous inspections, 100+ global deployments, and named customers including Shell, bp, Repsol, Petrobras, Pluspetrol, Chevron, E.ON, Evonik, BASF, and Merck. Rebranded from Energy Robotics GmbH on 4 May 2026.

providers.name: Botrista
providers.description: Botrista, Inc. is a San Francisco based beverage-automation company founded in 2017 that builds the DrinkBot robotic beverage dispenser and the CloudBar cloud platform behind it. The DrinkBot automates craft beverages — infused teas, flavored lemonades, iced coffees and mocktails — dispensing a drink in roughly twenty seconds from a touchscreen order, and every unit is internet connected so it pulls recipes, reports consumption, tracks ingredient levels and pushes maintenance alerts back to Botrista. CloudBar is the operator-facing web application used by restaurant, campus dining, convenience and theme-park operators to manage recipes, inventory replenishment and sales/menu performance analytics across a fleet of machines, alongside a separate Botrista Data Portal. Botrista sells beverage automation as a service rather than as a developer platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract, and POS integrations are handled case-by-case through its commercial team.

providers.name: SIMULIA (Dassault Systemes)
providers.description: SIMULIA is Dassault Systemes' multidisciplinary simulation portfolio for evaluating product performance, reliability, and safety before physical prototyping. The product family includes Abaqus (nonlinear FEA), CST Studio Suite (electromagnetics), Isight (process automation and design optimization), fe-safe (durability), Tosca (topology and shape optimization), and additional structural, CFD, multibody, and vibro-acoustics solvers, integrated on the 3DEXPERIENCE platform. Programmatic access is delivered through scripting interfaces (Python for Abaqus, Visual Basic / macros for CST, Java/JavaScript for Isight) rather than a public web API.

providers.name: Lecturio
providers.description: Lecturio is a medical and nursing education technology company headquartered in Leipzig, Germany (Lecturio GmbH), serving more than 500,000 learners and educators across 175+ countries. The platform combines video lectures, concept pages, spaced-repetition quizzes, and AI-tutored question banks covering 20+ preclinical and clinical subjects, with exam preparation for USMLE, NBME, COMLEX, MCAT, PANCE, NCLEX-RN, and international licensure exams such as the Saudi SNLE. Alongside the direct-to-student Lecturio Medical and Lecturio Nursing products, the company sells institutional platforms to medical schools, nursing schools, hospitals, and residency programs under the Healer (clinical reasoning), SimTutor (simulation authoring), and SIMTICS (procedural simulation) brands. Lecturio publishes no public developer API or developer portal; its public machine-readable surface consists of an RFC 9116 security.txt, a self-managed vulnerability disclosure policy, and a Rank Math generated llms.txt.

providers.name: Common Sense Machines
providers.description: Common Sense Machines (CSM) builds 3D world models with image-to-3D and 3D world simulation APIs aimed at games, robotics, and synthetic data. The CSM Cube product family released a single-click model pipeline with mesh-parts-based topology in early 2026. API access is bundled with mid-tier and enterprise CSM subscription plans.

providers.name: Dronecode Foundation
providers.description: The Dronecode Foundation is a vendor-neutral Linux Foundation project for open source drone projects. It hosts PX4 autopilot flight control software and MAVLink communication protocol used worldwide for unmanned aerial vehicles, providing a complete open source platform for drone development.

providers.name: Open 3D Foundation
providers.description: The Open 3D Foundation is a Linux Foundation project supporting the Open 3D Engine (O3DE), an open source, real-time 3D engine for building games, simulations, and other 3D applications. With Microsoft as a premier member, it provides a modular, cross-platform engine with advanced rendering capabilities.

providers.name: Tofu
providers.description: Tofu (tofuhq.com) is an agentic go-to-market (GTM) platform that automates always-on, integrated marketing and sales campaigns inside a team's existing GTM stack, helping revenue teams ship integrated campaigns dramatically faster. It targets outbound prospecting, lead nurturing, event follow-up, sales acceleration, stalled-deal re-engagement, and customer expansion, and integrates with major CRM and sales tools including Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, and Outreach. Tofu is a hosted SaaS product backed by Index Ventures; it consumes third-party APIs rather than publishing a public developer API, and advertises SOC 2 compliance. No public OpenAPI, SDK, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Wonder Workshop
providers.description: Wonder Workshop (GitHub org "playi", originally Play-i) is an educational technology company that makes the Dash, Dot, and Cue programmable robots and the Make Wonder K-8 coding and robotics learning platform, used by more than 40,000 schools across 65 countries. Its developer surface is a set of official SDKs that give granular realtime control of the physical robots' sensors and actuators over Bluetooth Low Energy: WonderPy (Python, on PyPI), @wonderworkshop/wwjs (JavaScript, on npm), and an iOS/Android robot framework shipped in the playground sample-app repository. There is no HTTP/cloud REST API, OAuth, or webhook surface; integration happens locally over BLE. Backed by GV.

providers.name: Augmentus
providers.description: Augmentus is a no-code adaptive robotics company (founded 2019, offices in Singapore and Pflugerville, Texas) that turns industrial robots into AI-driven automation systems programmable without code or a teach pendant. Its platform pairs 3D scanning and computer vision with AI motion planning to auto-generate robot toolpaths for welding, surface finishing, spraying, sandblasting, sanding, and material removal across ABB, FANUC, KUKA, Yaskawa, Kawasaki, Universal Robots, and Techman arms — cutting process automation from weeks to minutes. Sold as Standard (CAD-based toolpaths) and Pro (vision-guided) tiers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of sierra-ventures; profiled here from public sources. Augmentus ships a desktop/on-prem product rather than a public web API, so this profile is identity-and-presence oriented.

providers.name: Motics Technologies
providers.description: Motics Technologies (trading as Motics / Motics Health) is a UK-based healthcare AI automation platform providing AI agents for clinics, hospitals, and care homes. Its five agents — Scribe (clinical notes, letters, discharge summaries), Phone (24/7 AI receptionist and appointment booking), Email (patient communications and inbox triage), Billing (insurance claims and revenue cycle management), and Audit (clinic-wide documentation review for CQC/HCPC readiness) — help clinicians save 2+ hours per day on administrative work. Motics serves NHS trusts, private clinics, care homes, and telehealth providers, integrating with practice management systems including Cliniko, Meddbase, and Nookal, and states NHS Digital, HCPC, GMC, CQC, GDPR, and ISO 27001 compliance. The company is a Techstars portfolio company. No public developer API, SDK, or API reference is published at this time.

providers.name: Strawberry
providers.description: Strawberry is an agentic web browser for macOS with AI companions that work inside it: you describe an outcome and a companion operates the open web on your behalf — logged in as you, across many tabs — to research, extract data, fill forms, draft messages, and run multi-step work end to end ("Do hours of work in minutes"). Companions are persistent AI teammates you brief once; Routines run work on a schedule; Skills save a workflow to re-run in one line; Integrations let companions act across apps you are already signed into (Gmail, Google Sheets, Notion, Slack, Stripe, and more). It keeps a human in control, asking approval before consequential actions. Distributed as a desktop app, metered in credits. Backed by EQT Ventures and General Catalyst. Strawberry publishes no public REST/OpenAPI developer API as of this profiling; its surface is the consumer app plus web documentation, a security program, and machine-readable llms.txt and security.txt.

providers.name: AVAP BRUNIX
providers.description: AVAP BRUNIX is an AI-powered API development platform that serves as a copilot for developers, integrating artificial intelligence directly into the core of the AVAP framework to enhance efficiency and productivity in API development, testing, and management.

providers.name: Flyby Robotics
providers.description: Flyby Robotics is an American manufacturer of open-architecture, NDAA-compliant medium-lift drones built as a platform for physical and edge AI. Its F-11 series (F-11T, F-11S, F-11H) pairs onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX GPU compute (up to 314 TOPS) and an open ArduPilot/CubePilot flight controller with a developer-facing C++ SDK, so engineers can register custom payloads, stream video over GStreamer, and programmatically control the aircraft. The company ships the Flyby SDK (flyby-sdk-release) through GitHub and documents it at docs.flybydev.com, targeting ISR, photogrammetry, public-safety, research, and drone-delivery use cases. Flyby Robotics raised a $4M pre-seed backed by investors including MaC Venture Capital, Gaingels, and Anthemis Group. This profile captures Flyby's developer surface as it exists today: an on-board SDK and docs rather than a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Huginn
providers.description: Huginn is an open-source system for building agents that perform automated tasks online. Self-hosted agents can monitor the web, send and receive events, and trigger workflows. Each Huginn instance exposes a JSON-based HTTP interface (the Web Requests API) that lets external systems trigger scenarios and post events into the platform.

providers.name: Magical
providers.description: Magical is an AI-agent platform that automates repetitive administrative and operational workflows without requiring API integrations, instead driving the same web applications and databases a human worker would use. Originally known for its cross-application autofill and text-automation product, Magical has focused on healthcare operations, deploying specialized AI agents for patient access, revenue cycle management, prior authorizations, referrals, benefits verification, records requests, revenue integrity, and payment posting across EHR and payer systems such as Epic, Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, ModMed, Availity, and major insurers. Agents can be deployed individually or combined into autonomous suites, with the company reporting high task accuracy and multi-week deployment timelines. Magical is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Greylock, and SV Angel. Notably, Magical operates through user-interface automation ("no APIs or integrations are required") rather than by exposing a public developer API.

providers.name: Genspark
providers.description: Genspark is an all-in-one AI workspace and autonomous "Super Agent" platform that plans and executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf. It bundles a suite of AI agent tools — deep research, AI slides, AI sheets, AI docs, AI chat, a "Call For Me" voice agent, and a built-in AI browser — into a single natural-language workspace, alongside companion products such as Genspark Claw, Speakly, GenClipboard, and GenTerminal and native iOS and Android apps. For developers and agents, Genspark operates a hosted, remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at /api/mcp that exposes its tools, resources, and prompts over HTTP, gated by OAuth 2.1 (authorization_code with PKCE, refresh tokens, and dynamic client registration). Genspark is backed by Emergence Capital.

providers.name: Locus Robotics
providers.description: Locus Robotics is a warehouse-automation company that pairs autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) with an intelligent orchestration platform. Its robot line — Locus Array (Robots-to-Goods), Locus Origin, and Locus Vector — works alongside the LocusONE platform and the LocusHub business-intelligence engine to raise pick/putaway rates and reduce labor across distribution and fulfillment operations. LocusONE integrates with warehouse management systems (WMS) and ERP platforms through APIs delivered via the Locus Global Alliance Network partner program; the company also maintains 100+ open-source ROS robotics repositories on GitHub. There is no public self-serve developer portal or published API specification — integration is arranged through partners and direct engagement.

providers.name: RapidClaims
providers.description: RapidClaims is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) company building autonomous AI agents for medical coding and claims. Its platform automates medical coding (RapidCode), value-based-care coding and risk adjustment (RapidVBC), denial management and revenue recovery (RapidRecovery), and a unified revenue cycle platform (RapidRCM) for FQHCs, community health centers, ACOs, physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals, and management services organizations. The company emphasizes a healthcare-grade security and compliance posture (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, 256-bit encryption). RapidClaims is backed by Accel and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Vecna Robotics
providers.description: Vecna Robotics is a Waltham, Massachusetts material-handling automation company, spun out of Vecna Technologies in 2018, that builds autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) — autonomous forklifts, pallet trucks, tuggers, conveyor and lifter platforms — together with Pivotal, its end-to-end orchestration software suite for warehouse and manufacturing operations. Pivotal spans Orchestration (real-time task allocation and routing), Autonomous Navigation (3D lidar/vision sensor fusion), Insights (analytics and KPI dashboards), Integrations (WMS / MES / ERP, barcode scanning, on-robot and remote tablet UIs, call buttons, smart I/O) and the Pivotal Command Center, a 24/7 human-in-the-loop teleoperation and remote monitoring service. Vecna sells the fleet as Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) alongside the CaseFlow case-picking solution, and markets "flexible API integrations" into existing WMS/WES environments — but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract as of this profiling pass. The only anonymous machine-readable surface found is the OpenID Connect discovery document served by its Salesforce Experience Cloud partner portal.

providers.name: Quilter
providers.description: Quilter is a physics-driven AI platform that automates printed circuit board (PCB) placement and routing. Using reinforcement learning, it converts a schematic into multiple fabrication-ready layout candidates in hours instead of weeks, validating each against physical constraints through Physics Rule Checks (impedance control, differential pairs, power nets, bypass capacitors, keepouts, and stackup rules). Quilter supports Altium, Cadence Allegro, Siemens Xpedition, KiCAD, and OrCAD formats and handles boards of roughly 100-1,000 components with 2,000-5,000 pins to route. It is delivered as a hosted web application (app.quilter.ai) with a startup program and a free tier; there is no public developer API, SDK, or CLI surface at this time.

providers.name: Cartwheel
providers.description: Cartwheel is a generative motion platform for games, film & TV, advertising, and robotics. It gives creators a new way to animate 3D characters — turning ordinary video into clean, usable character motion (video-to-motion), and posing and rendering characters as images in any visual style. Cartwheel is delivered as a hosted web studio (studio.getcartwheel.com) with exportable animation formats for downstream 3D, game, film, and social pipelines. The product is in private beta and is backed by Accel, Craft Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. At this time Cartwheel exposes no public developer/REST API; this profile captures its public web, documentation, and security surface.

providers.name: Champ Ai
providers.description: Champ AI is an AI operations platform that automates complex, multi-step enterprise back-office workflows through autonomous agents that browse, read, call, and act on behalf of operations teams. Positioned as an AI-native replacement for traditional business process outsourcing (BPO), Champ combines browser automation across legacy portals and internal tools, document intelligence, outbound voice AI, and SOP-to-agent conversion with process mining and more than 100 integrations. The platform targets regulated, operations-heavy verticals such as healthcare and professional employer organizations (PEO), claiming 95%+ accuracy on complex standard operating procedures and 4-10x ROI on operational spend. Founded by Jagannath Putrevu, Ted Cheng, and Peter Lin (early Instacart operators), Champ AI emerged from stealth in May 2026 with an $8.5M seed round led by Redpoint Ventures with participation from defy.vc and SV Angel. This profile was surfaced as a Redpoint Ventures portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; Champ AI does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Interplay Learning
providers.description: Interplay Learning is an Austin, Texas edtech company delivering always-on, immersive skilled trades training through online video courses, 3D simulations, and VR for HVAC, plumbing, electrical, facilities maintenance, and solar. Its SkillMill platform has trained more than 500,000 workers to be job-ready, pairing hands-on simulations with custom learning paths, certification prep, and skill assessments. For employers, Interplay exposes an enterprise data-integration API plus SSO and LMS integrations so training data can flow into an organization's own systems; it publishes no public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI. Backed by Sierra Ventures. This profile was enriched from the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Khalifa University
providers.description: Khalifa University of Science and Technology is a research-intensive university in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, ranked #202 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates colleges of Engineering and Physical Sciences, Computing and Mathematical Sciences, and Medicine and Health Sciences, along with multiple research centers. No central public, documented developer or API program was found; student and administrative systems (KU Connect portal, Banner registration, e-Learn, library discovery) are gated behind institutional authentication. The only confirmed public code footprint is the GitHub organization of its Center for Autonomous Robotic Systems (KUCARS), which publishes open-source robotics research repositories rather than a managed, documented API.

providers.name: Rezo
providers.description: Rezo.ai is an enterprise customer-experience (CX) company building a unified, agentic-AI contact-center platform. Founded in 2018 in Noida, India by Dr. Rashi Gupta and Dr. Manish Gupta, Rezo automates and augments customer interactions across voice, chat, email, and social channels with AI voice agents, speech and sentiment analytics, real-time agent assist, and robotic process automation, supporting 30+ languages. Its Agentic AI Suite spans customer support, sales, and marketing use cases for enterprises across banking, telecom, e-commerce, and other verticals, with product surfaces including the "Central Data Hub" (my.rezo.ai) and the "Autonomous Conversation Matrix" (az-converse.rezo.ai). Rezo operates offices in India, the USA, and the UAE, and holds ISO 27701:2019 with GDPR compliance. Rezo does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures its public identity, trust/compliance posture, and vulnerability disclosure program.

providers.name: Robocurve
providers.description: Robocurve is a San Francisco Public Benefit Corporation (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building open-source tools and independent benchmarks to help society understand what AI and robots can actually do in the physical world. Its flagship framework, Inspect Robots ("the Inspect AI for robotics"), runs any vision-language-action policy on any embodiment against any benchmark with full trace logs and live Rerun visualization, and integrates with ROS, Isaac Lab, and LeRobot. World Evals is its curated catalog of physical-world benchmarks (KitchenBench, DataCenterBench). Everything ships MIT-licensed as Python packages with a command-line interface rather than a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Briefcase
providers.description: Briefcase is an AI-native accounting and bookkeeping automation platform for UK accounting firms and businesses. Founded in 2024 in London by Reuben Steenkamp and Ján Stehlík, and backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, Entrepreneur First and Tiny, Briefcase describes itself as building the world's first AI autopilot for accounting firms. The product uses multimodal AI and agentic workflows to automate the most tedious parts of accounting: extracting data from invoices, receipts and bank statements, categorising transactions against a firm's chart of accounts, handling VAT (with embedded HMRC legislation for standard, reverse-charge and zero-rated VAT), automating prepayments and expense claims, and driving month-end and financial close. It publishes results into Xero and QuickBooks. Briefcase is delivered as a cloud SaaS application (app.briefcase.so); it is a consumer of accounting APIs rather than a public API producer, and at the time of this profile it publishes no developer/API documentation, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Helsing
providers.description: Helsing SE is a Munich-based European defense AI company founded in March 2021 by Torsten Reil, Gundbert Scherf, and Niklas Köhler. Helsing builds AI software and autonomous weapons systems for European and allied militaries — reconnaissance-strike software (Altra), electronic-warfare AI (Cirra), an AI fighter pilot (Centaur), loitering-munition strike drones (HF-1 and HX-2), an autonomous combat aircraft (CA-1 Europa), and underwater autonomy (Lura acoustic processing, SG-1 Fathom long-endurance underwater drones). The company is sales-led and government-restricted; there is no public REST API or developer portal. This profile documents the publicly visible product surfaces and partnerships rather than endpoint shapes. Funding totals roughly €1.37B across four rounds, with a $1.2B Series E at an $18B valuation reportedly being finalized as of May 2026. Daniel Ek's Prima Materia is the largest shareholder. Public partnerships include Saab (Gripen E integration of Centaur, including the 2025 Project Beyond combat trial), Airbus, Rheinmetall, the Bundeswehr, and the Eurofighter Typhoon EK programme.

providers.name: Nori
providers.description: Nori (Nori Robotics) is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) hard-tech company in San Francisco building affordable bimanual humanoid home robots — the NORI L2, a sub-$1,300 wheeled robot with dual Z-axis lift arms that autonomously handles household chores like loading dishes, making beds, food prep, and cleaning, with multiple units able to collaborate on coordinated tasks. Beyond the hardware, Nori publishes a developer surface: the @nori/sdk robot-local teleoperation SDK connects to a robot over WebRTC to stream video and telemetry and drive it from the browser in ~20 lines, with all safety mechanisms (clamping, watchdog, E-STOP, motor torque lifecycle) enforced on the robot's control daemon. The SDK targets the nori-protocol v1 wire format (NDJSON over a WebRTC data channel to the daemon on port 7777), is Apache-2.0 licensed, and is distributed to a small set of collaborating developers as a tarball rather than on public npm.

providers.name: Fullseam
providers.description: FullSeam builds AI agents for corporate accounting and finance operations teams, automating the manual work that happens outside traditional accounting software. Its agents handle accounts receivable (following up on payments, generating requested documentation, and entering invoices into customer AP portals), accounts payable (extracting invoices from multiple sources, matching them against purchase orders and contracts, chasing vendors for missing information, and categorizing expenses before posting to the general ledger), cash application, and reconciliation. FullSeam integrates with existing systems including QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Sage, Bill, Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, and PandaDoc rather than requiring a platform migration, flagging exceptions with full context for human review and maintaining audit logs for compliance. Founded by the team behind TaxProper (acquired by Opendoor), FullSeam is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company.

providers.name: Imubit
providers.description: Imubit is a Houston-based industrial AI company behind the Optimizing Brain, the process industry's first Closed Loop AI Optimization (AIO) solution powered by deep reinforcement learning. Its cloud-based platform learns a dynamic model from a plant's own historian and DCS data, then writes optimal setpoints back through existing control-system infrastructure to continuously optimize throughput, yield, energy use and emissions. Imubit reports 100+ closed-loop applications deployed across refining, oil and gas, chemicals, petrochemicals and polymers, cement and building materials, and mining, minerals and metals, and is trusted by 7 of the 10 largest U.S. refiners. Imubit publishes no public developer API; its GitHub organization ships open-source Python libraries for pulling data from industrial historians (OSIsoft PI, Aspen IP21) and supporting infrastructure.

providers.name: Shoreline
providers.description: Shoreline is an incident automation platform that enables operators to build automated remediation for recurring incidents.

providers.name: TraceAir
providers.description: TraceAir is a construction site intelligence platform for homebuilders and land developers, combining drone photogrammetry and LiDAR scans with cloud analytics to track sitework progress, verify earthwork cut/fill quantities, generate lot layouts and yield estimates, and document builds with 360-degree interior scans across the full project lifecycle from land acquisition to handover. The company publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; the platform is accessed through its web application.

providers.name: Basata
providers.description: Basata is a Phoenix-based healthcare AI company building the operational layer for American medical practices. Its AI agents automate back-office administrative work — processing patient referrals, answering phone calls 24/7, and managing faxes and patient communications — while integrating with existing EHR systems so clinical staff can focus on patient care instead of paperwork. Founded in 2024 by Kaled Alhanafi (CEO, formerly Lyft and Cruise), Chetan Patel (co-founder and president, formerly Medtronic), and Vivin Paliath (co-founder and CTO), Basata raised a $21M Series A led by Basis Set Ventures with Cowboy Ventures and PHX Ventures participating (~$24.5M total). The platform is marketed as fully HIPAA-compliant and the company publishes a SOC 2 attestation. Basata does not currently expose a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: DataSnipper
providers.description: DataSnipper is an AI-powered, agentic productivity platform built specifically for audit, tax, and finance teams. It automates repetitive testing and analysis work - extracting, matching, and analyzing data across documents and systems - while keeping human professionals in control of final decisions. Capabilities include AI Agents for end-to-end workflows (revenue testing, tests of detail, royalty calculations), Excel Agents that run analysis directly inside spreadsheets, and document intelligence that collects and cross-references evidence. The platform serves external audit, internal audit, tax, financial control, government audit, and advisory teams, with a security-first posture (no training on customer data, encryption, and 24-hour document deletion). Backed by Index Ventures and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Aris Machina
providers.description: Aris Machina builds AI-powered industrial software for advanced manufacturing, describing its mission as delivering "industrial superintelligence" that unifies design, production, and operations through AI agents and a shared semantic knowledge model. Its products include Protos, an AI co-engineer for R&D teams that accelerates design validation and simulation; Gemba, shopfloor operational agents that provide real-time equipment diagnostics; and the Ontology Toolkit, a knowledge-integration layer that bridges data across MES, ERP, and PLM systems. Aris Machina serves batteries, biopharma, robotics, defense, and aerospace, and is backed by Earlybird. The company operates from Stockholm, Bangalore, and California. This profile was surfaced as an Earlybird portfolio company and enriched from public web sources; Aris Machina does not currently publish a public developer API surface, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: Maxima
providers.description: Maxima is an AI-native accounting and financial-close automation platform for enterprise finance teams.
