Its AI agents automate the core work of the accounting close — journal entries, cash coding, payroll entries, bank and balance-sheet reconciliations, flux (variance) analysis, and fixed-asset depreciation — while connecting natively to the systems finance teams already use (the company advertises 150+ integrations across ERPs, banks, and payroll providers). Maxima is an early-stage, enterprise-focused company backed by Kleiner Perkins. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this pass the company runs a corporate marketing site and a gated web application (app.maximahq.com) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Yaskawa / Motoman
providers.description: Yaskawa Electric Corporation is a Kitakyushu, Japan industrial automation company and the world's largest manufacturer of AC servo motors and motion controllers, with major business segments in motion control (AC servo motors, SERVOPACK amplifiers, machine controllers), AC drives / inverters, industrial robotics (under the Motoman brand), and systems engineering. Yaskawa's Motoman robotics division supplies articulated, SCARA, delta, collaborative, and mini robots used across automotive, EV, semiconductor, electronics, food, biomedical, and logistics manufacturing, alongside its Sigma-X servo family and GA / U1000 industrial AC drives. The company exposes a developer surface through the Yaskawa Motoman Developer Portal at developer.motoman.com and the Yaskawa-Global GitHub organization, including YMConnect (a modern PC-side communication library for C++ 17 and C#), MotoPlus SDK (on-controller C code for deterministic motion, I/O, jobs, and alarms), MotoROS2 (a native ROS 2 / micro-ROS node running on DX200, YRC1000, and YRC1000micro controllers), MotoCom SDK (legacy Windows communication SDK), the Smart Pendant SDK (Java extensions for the Smart Pendant teach interface), and YIP (Yaskawa Innovation Plus) packages and Smart Packager tooling. The catalog is SDK- and protocol-driven rather than HTTP/REST — there are no public OpenAPI specifications, so this profile captures the SDK, ROS, GitHub, and developer-portal surface without generated OpenAPI artifacts.

providers.name: Genesis AI
providers.description: Genesis AI is a physical-AI company building a universal robotics foundation model and a full-stack platform for general-purpose robots. Founded in 2024 by Zhou Xian and Théophile Gervet, it emerged from stealth in July 2025 with $105M in seed funding from Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, HSG, Eric Schmidt, and Xavier Niel. Its stack spans the GENE vision-language-action foundation model (GENE-26.5), the Eno general-purpose robot, and Genesis World, a multi-physics simulation platform that generates synthetic training data and is developed in the open as the `genesis-world` Python package. The company is pre-product with customer deployments targeted for the end of 2026; its primary public developer surface today is the open-source Genesis simulation stack on PyPI, GitHub, and Read the Docs rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Notable
providers.description: Notable is an intelligent-automation company purpose-built for healthcare, applying AI agents to administrative and operational workflows across patient access, revenue cycle management, care operations, and contact-center automation. Its platform pairs a library of prebuilt AI Agents with Flow Builder, a low-code interface for designing, training, and deploying automations, and Sidekick, a natural-language assistant for staff. Deployed at more than 1,000 healthcare locations and used by health systems including Intermountain Healthcare and the Medical University of South Carolina, Notable is backed by Greylock and ICONIQ Capital. This profile has been enriched from the company's public trust, security, and developer surfaces.

providers.name: Exotec
providers.description: Exotec is a French warehouse automation manufacturer and integrator, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Croix, France, that builds the Skypod robotic automated storage and retrieval system (AS/RS) and the Deepsky warehouse execution system (WES) that orchestrates it. Skypod combines autonomous three-dimensional mobile robots, modular racking, picking workstations and inbound exchangers into an all-in-one goods-to-person system; Deepsky is the software layer that coordinates the robots, stations and third-party equipment and connects the installation to a customer's WMS or WCS over a RESTful web-services interface. Exotec reports more than 10,000 robots deployed across over 200 customer sites for more than 50 brands including Decathlon, Renault Group, DSV, Carrefour, Gap and Uniqlo, serving apparel, general merchandise, aftermarket parts, grocery, third-party logistics and healthcare fulfillment. The Deepsky WMS integration interface is delivered as customer-specific documentation under a commercial deployment rather than a public developer program, so Exotec publishes no open developer portal, API reference or SDK. It does publish an llms.txt at its web root and holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification and SOC 2 Type 2 compliance.

providers.name: Ambarella
providers.description: Ambarella (NASDAQ: AMBA) is a fabless semiconductor company designing low-power system-on-chip (SoC) processors for edge AI and computer vision. Its CVflow architecture accelerates deep neural networks on-device for intelligent cameras, automotive ADAS and autonomous driving, robotics, security, and industrial applications. Ambarella does not publish a public HTTP/REST API; developers engage through the Cooper Developer Platform, the CVflow SDK and toolchain (compiler, debugger, Caffe/TensorFlow support), the Model Garden on HuggingFace, Agentic Blueprints, and an Apache-2.0 set of on-device Agent Skills for Cooper Foundry. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Matrix Partners and enriched with the provider's real public developer, security, and agent surfaces.

providers.name: Sumary
providers.description: Sumary is a Denmark-based fintech building an AI-native workflow engine for finance and accounting teams. Its platform layers autonomous accounting agents, anomaly detection, and on-demand reporting over a company's existing accounting systems — automating reconciliations and variance explanations, validating transactions to catch errors and potential fraud, and generating management reports, margin analyses, and cost breakdowns for bookkeepers, controllers, CFOs, and finance leaders. The company raised a $4.2M (27M DKK) pre-seed round led by byFounders with participation from Partech and Tenity. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's web, trust, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Ntopology
providers.description: nTop (formerly nTopology) is a computational design software platform for engineering teams building complex, high-performance products. Its parametric, field-driven modeling engine combines geometry, simulation data, and manufacturing constraints so engineers can move from requirements to production-ready designs in a fraction of the traditional time. nTop is used across aerospace and defense, automotive, medical, and industrial energy sectors for lightweighting, lattice and implicit modeling, thermal and structural optimization, and additive manufacturing. nTop also ships nTop Core, a first-party developer library (C++, .NET, and Python) for working with implicit bodies exported from nTop. The company is headquartered in New York City and is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and DCVC.

providers.name: Mech-Mind Robotics
providers.description: Mech-Mind Robotics provides industrial 3D cameras (the Mech-Eye industrial 3D camera and laser profiler line) together with software suites — Mech-Vision machine-vision software, Mech-Viz robot-programming software, and the Mech-DLK deep-learning toolkit — that give industrial robots embodied AI and 3D vision. Typical applications include bin picking, depalletizing, machine tending, piece picking, and item picking; the company reports 3000+ deployed applications for 1000+ clients worldwide. The developer surface is the Mech-Eye SDK (a C++ core with Python and C# bindings), ROS and ROS2 interfaces, and the Mech-DLK SDK, all published under the MechMindRobotics GitHub organization; there is no public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Mona Ai
providers.description: Mona AI GmbH (mona-ai.de) is a German AI recruiting-automation company backed by Earlybird. Its platform combines AI agents and digital avatars to automate recruiting and HR processes for staffing agencies and enterprises: 24/7 candidate outreach, automated pre-qualification and candidate-profile generation, and "digital branch" structures — built to be fully GDPR- and EU-AI-Act-compliant. Products include MONA Recruiting, MONA Recruiting Light, MONA Agents, MONA Digital Branch, MONA Consulting and MONA ARS, an autonomous prompt-driven recruiting system that sources, screens, schedules and reports automatically. The website is Wix-hosted and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint plus an llms.txt for AI-agent access; the recruiting product itself runs behind a login and does not publish a public developer API, SDK or OpenAPI.

providers.name: BrainCo
providers.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

providers.name: Chimelabs Holdings PTY LTD
providers.description: Chime Labs (Chimelabs Holdings PTY LTD) builds an AI voice receptionist and call-automation platform purpose-built for Australian trades and service businesses — plumbers, electricians, HVAC, locksmiths, pest control, cleaners and other on-the-tools operators. The AI answers missed inbound calls 24/7, qualifies and captures job details in natural Australian English, books work into scheduling and field-service systems (ServiceM8, Simpro, ServiceTitan, AroFlo, Fergus, Acuity Scheduling and Google Calendar), runs outbound calls, and turns quote calls into sent quotes automatically. Founded in 2025 in Sydney, Australia by Alexis Griveau (CEO) and Mathew Pretel and backed by 500 Global. The company operates a customer-facing SaaS product at platform.chimelabs.ai; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: General Intuition
providers.description: General Intuition is a frontier AI lab building large action foundation models that can perceive, predict, and act across space and time in both virtual and physical environments. Spun out of the gaming clip platform Medal, the company trains its spatial-temporal reasoning models on billions of action-labeled gameplay clips - recordings of exactly which buttons a player pressed and when - to teach AI agents how to move through and reason about the world. Its Mira world model powers applications across games, simulation, and robotics. Founded in 2025 and based in New York City, General Intuition has raised $454M total, including a $320M Series A at a $2.3B valuation, and is onboarding first partners to a commercial API ahead of a broader developer release.

providers.name: Infera
providers.description: Infera is an AI-native laboratory automation platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts plain-English descriptions of experiments into validated, instrument-ready runs across the lab instruments a team already owns. It compiles protocols into vendor-specific scripts for liquid handlers, plate readers, mass spectrometers, thermocyclers and centrifuges (Opentrons, Hamilton, Tecan and others), limits AI to initial drafts while keeping downstream steps deterministic and fully checkable, supports both automated and manual bench procedures, and maintains an end-to-end audit trail of protocols and runs. Founded in San Francisco by Troy Zhang and Chloe Sow.

providers.name: Anzen
providers.description: Anzen Technologies builds AI-powered market access software for commercial insurance agencies. Its flagship product, Anzen Pro, automates the commercial insurance quoting workflow: intelligent market matching predicts which carriers are most likely to respond to a submission based on historical quoting data, automated submission routing delivers each submission to a carrier's preferred channel (email, portal, or form), and submission intake extracts data from ACORDs, emails, and PDFs to generate branded client proposals in seconds. Anzen reports recovering roughly 80% of the time agency teams spend on administrative tasks and serves 200+ agencies while reducing errors-and-omissions exposure. The company holds a SOC 2 Type II attestation and anchors its security program on the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. Backed by a16z. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs are published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: DoNotPay
providers.description: DoNotPay is an AI-powered consumer advocacy platform, founded in 2015 by Joshua Browder and marketed as the "robot lawyer." It offers a web-based consumer product with 100+ AI-assisted tools that help people cancel subscriptions and free trials, dispute parking tickets and traffic violations, file chargebacks and refunds, negotiate and lower bills, find unclaimed money, fight robocalls, generate virtual cards for safe trial signups, and automate customer-service interactions. DoNotPay is a direct consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; it is tracked here as an API Evangelist company profile.

providers.name: Zone & Company
providers.description: Zone & Co (Zone & Company) is a NetSuite-native financial operations software vendor whose SuiteApp suite automates the back office across five product families - Quote to Cash (ZoneBilling billing and revenue recognition, ZonePayments Stripe integration), Procure to Pay (ZoneProcure, ZoneCapture, ZoneApprovals), Treasury (ZoneLiquidity cash forecasting, ZoneReconcile), Payroll Management (ZonePayroll, Employee Portal), and Record to Report (ZoneReporting on Power BI, Data Warehouse, ZoneExtract, Solution 7). The products are delivered as native Oracle NetSuite SuiteApps distributed through the SuiteApp Marketplace rather than as a standalone public developer API. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Ambi Robotics
providers.description: Ambi Robotics is a Berkeley, California AI robotics company building parcel-sortation and induction robots for ecommerce, postal, and logistics workflows. Founded in 2018 as Ambidextrous Laboratories — a spin-out of UC Berkeley's Dex-Net Project led by Ken Goldberg — by Jeff Mahler (CTO), Stephen McKinley, David Gealy, and Matt Matl, with Jim Liefer (ex-Walmart, ex-UPS) as CEO. Its flagship products are AmbiSort A-Series (sort-to-sack small parcel sorting), AmbiSort B-Series (sort-to-gaylord parcel induction for middle-mile and reverse logistics), AmbiStack (mixed-case stacking for inbound and outbound), and AmbiVision (3D dimensioning, OCR, defect detection, and visual quality inspection). All robots run AmbiOS, the company's cloud-native "operating system for physical intelligence," comprising the AI Skill Suite (Sort, Stack, Kit, Pack, Induct apps), the PRIME-1 foundation model trained on millions of real-world operations, AmbiVision perception, AmbiAccess fleet management dashboard with heat maps and remote support, and a Sim2Real training pipeline that compresses model training by up to 10,000x. Ambi Robotics' primary commercial deployment is a $23 million expansion with Pitney Bowes, with AmbiSort A-Series and B-Series systems deployed across Pitney Bowes ecommerce hubs in the US (including the Stockton, CA hub that nearly doubled local-direct-delivery throughput in the 2021 peak holiday season, and middle-mile B-Series systems that sorted more than 3 million parcels within four months of deployment). Ambi Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for AmbiOS, AmbiSort, AmbiStack, or PRIME-1; integration with customer WMS/WES systems is performed by Ambi's solutions team. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (Ray, trimesh, FCL, EIPScanner, tinygltf, rapier, jszmq, CVXPYgen, mongoose-delete) and internal CI/CD workflow utilities — no published API spec, SDK package, or developer documentation.

providers.name: TMRW Life Sciences *
providers.description: TMRW Life Sciences is a medical technology company that builds the world's first and only FDA-cleared automated platform for the safe management and storage of frozen eggs and embryos used in IVF and fertility treatment. Its cryo-storage hardware combines robotic specimen handling with digital tracking, chain-of-custody monitoring, and real-time visibility for fertility clinics and their patients, replacing manual, paper-based handling of irreplaceable reproductive tissue. Deployed at clinic networks including CCRM Fertility, Pinnacle Fertility, RFC, and IVIRMA North America. TMRW is a private company backed by GV (Google Ventures). It publishes a Security & Trust program (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27018) but does not expose a public developer portal, API, or specification surface.

providers.name: Baseframe
providers.description: BaseFrame (baseframe.co) is a Y Combinator (W26) startup building an AI workflow discovery platform for teams and small businesses. Its privacy-first desktop application analyzes historical work patterns across email, documents, Slack, calendar, browser activity, and files using on-device local models to identify high-value, repetitive tasks and recommend concrete AI automations, then helps users set them up in the tools they already use. BaseFrame publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time; it is a consumer/desktop product with SaaS integrations (Gmail, Slack, HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Office 365, Jira). Founded in 2025 by Anshul Paul and Vaibhav Agrawal.

providers.name: Flowscope
providers.description: Flowscope is an AI-native process-automation firm (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that deploys agents to observe how a business actually runs, map and redesign its workflows, then ship the automation into production on top of existing systems in days rather than months. It positions itself as the AI team for mid-market operating businesses that do not have one, selling services-as-software with outcome-aligned pricing rather than a self-serve developer API. Founded in 2025 in San Francisco by Samuel Mirpuri (ex-McKinsey QuantumBlack) and Javier Leguina (founding engineer, ModelML), Flowscope runs forward-deployed agents that shadow employees, baseline the process, redesign the work, and write back into legacy systems of record while a human core keeps judgment and accountability in the loop.

providers.name: Ordana
providers.description: Ordana provides AI agents that run wholesale order-desk operations for distributors, reading every order across email, fax, PDF, EDI, voice, SMS and chat, resolving exceptions, communicating with retailers, and closing orders directly into the customer's ERP. Four agents cover the surface: Desk (end-to-end order automation), Voice (inbound/outbound phone ordering), Predict (cart prediction and AOV optimization), and Chat (text/SMS ordering). Ordana sits as an intelligence layer on top of existing ERP and commerce systems via pre-built connectors, and exposes its capabilities through a gated REST API, Webhooks, an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over HTTP/SSE with OAuth 2.0, and the A2A agent-to-agent protocol. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Mosaic Manufacturing
providers.description: Mosaic Manufacturing is a Toronto-based additive manufacturing company building automated, high-volume FFF 3D printing systems for factory-floor production of end-use polymer parts. Its flagship Array platform combines integrated robotics, intelligent scheduling software, and high-performance fused-filament-fabrication printers so manufacturers can cut part costs and run true production at scale. Mosaic also makes the Palette line of multi-material hardware and Canvas (canvas3d.io), a cloud/web software platform for file preparation, color/slice, print scheduling, and fleet management. As of this enrichment pass Mosaic publishes no public product API or OpenAPI-described developer surface; its developer-facing presence is the open-source MosaicManufacturing GitHub organization (3MF tooling, slicer post-processing, and firmware) plus a hosted support/knowledge-base portal.

providers.name: Crux OCM
providers.description: CruxOCM builds AI-powered automation software for industrial control-room operations in the energy-infrastructure sector. Its Industrial Automation Hub (IAH) delivers closed-loop automation on top of existing SCADA and DCS systems to increase pipeline throughput, cut operating and energy costs, and improve safety without replacing installed control infrastructure. The product family includes pipeBOT, gatherBOT, draBOT, maxOPT, leanOPT, and powerOPT, supported by a Deployment Manager, Log Analyser, and real-time Status Dashboard. Founded by control-room engineers and operators (CEO Vicki Knott, co-founder Roger Shirt) and headquartered in Calgary, Alberta, the company raised a $17M Series A led by Microsoft's M12 and serves midstream operators including ONEOK, Delek US, Enbridge, HF Sinclair, and Alliance Pipeline. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Vector.ai
providers.description: Vector.ai, now operating as Raft (raft.ai), is an AI-powered logistics automation platform for freight forwarders, customs brokers, and trade finance teams. The Raft Intelligence Engine layers organization data, contextual LLMs, orchestration, and specialized governed agents to automate document processing, invoice matching, data extraction, and exception handling across supply chain operations, reporting 20M+ tasks completed by AI agents and 5M+ shipments processed annually. Raft publishes no public developer API; the platform is an enterprise application that integrates with customers' TMS and ERP systems.

providers.name: Nurix
providers.description: Nurix AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform for sales and customer support, delivering AI voice and chat agents that qualify leads, resolve support issues, and automate back-office operations across voice, chat, and messaging channels. Its products include NuPlay (customer-facing conversational AI agents) and NuStack (a workflow automation engine), backed by a library of 400+ pre-built integrations spanning CRM, contact-center (CCaaS), e-commerce/order-management, messaging, and scheduling systems. Nurix is backed by General Catalyst. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API surface — engagement is via sales/demo and pre-built connectors rather than self-serve API keys or developer documentation.

providers.name: Ridecell
providers.description: Ridecell is an AI-powered asset intelligence and orchestration platform for automotive leasing, fleet, and finance companies. Its five intelligence modules (Client, Spend, Supplier, Asset, and Operational Intelligence) and the "Maya" AI agent monitor fleets, flag invoice overcharges, track garage/supplier performance, optimize vehicle remarketing and residual value, and resolve idle-vehicle inefficiencies. The platform processes 12M+ events daily across 500K+ assets, 100+ connected systems, and 14+ countries. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Ridecell does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK; this profile captures its public information, security, and compliance surfaces.

providers.name: Built Robotics
providers.description: Built Robotics is a San Francisco robotics company, founded in 2016 by Noah Ready-Campbell and Andrew Liang, that turns conventional heavy construction equipment into AI-powered autonomous robots. Its Exosystem retrofit kit converts excavators and other earthmoving machines into self-operating robots for trenching, foundation excavation and pad grading, while the RPD 35 and RPS 25 autonomous pile drivers install foundations for utility-scale solar farms. Machines are supervised from the Everest command center, and field deployment is run through its Built Solar Technologies (built.solar) division. The company reports $114M raised and 25+ commercial deployments across the United States and Australia. Built Robotics publishes no public developer API, SDK or machine-readable API contract; its only public developer artifact is the open-source rsplan Reeds-Shepp path-planning library on PyPI and GitHub.

providers.name: Lato
providers.description: Lato (LATO Labs) is a San Francisco company building an agent-native research and simulation platform for investors. Its agents source and conduct hundreds of voice interviews with verified domain experts and customers in any language, each returned with a recording, transcript and thematic analysis, then combine those interviews with thousands of documents from public sources and a fund's own proprietary knowledge into a single commercial study. The study becomes a live simulation of the market that analysts can question and run scenarios against to predict where a market is headed. Investors use Lato for commercial due diligence, expert interviews, market sizing, competitive mapping, customer interviews, pricing studies, deal sourcing, inbound screening and portfolio value creation, compressing research that traditionally costs hundreds of thousands of dollars and takes weeks into hours. The product integrates with the tools investment teams already run on, including Outlook, SharePoint, Gmail, Google Drive, Slack, Teams, Excel, Affinity, Attio, Harmonic and Granola. Lato was founded by Tymek Staniszewski (CEO) and Tien Chu (CTO), is backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026), and builds on Anthropic, OpenAI and ElevenLabs. As of this profile Lato publishes no public developer API, documentation or SDKs; the company surface is captured here for discovery and the repository will be re-enriched when a developer program appears.

providers.name: Zebra Technologies
providers.description: Zebra Technologies is a global leader in barcode printing, RFID, mobile computing, and machine vision solutions for manufacturing, warehousing, healthcare, and retail. The Zebra Developer Portal and TechDocs expose cloud REST APIs for printing, device management, barcode generation, RFID IoT connectivity, asset tracking, and label design, enabling integration of Zebra hardware into enterprise workflows and manufacturing operations systems.

providers.name: Wiselayer
providers.description: WiseLayer is an AI-powered accounting automation platform that provides named "digital workers" (AI agents) for finance and accounting teams, automating tasks such as accruals, vendor communications, payroll accounting, bank reconciliations, depreciation and amortization, lease accounting, and prepaid expenses. The platform emphasizes transparent, explainable AI ("AI that shows its work") with natural-language interaction, automated email digests, and 300+ integrations into ERPs, billing, procure-to-pay, and HRIS systems. WiseLayer was acquired by BlackLine (NASDAQ: BL) and its product is now offered as Verity Accruals by BlackLine. WiseLayer was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners. The company operates a SaaS application at app.wiselayer.com and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Intrinsic
providers.description: Intrinsic is a Mountain View, California industrial robotics software company spun out of Alphabet's X "moonshot factory" and led by CEO Wendy Tan White. Its mission is to make industrial robots radically easier to program, use, and innovate with so that automation is accessible to a much broader range of businesses. Intrinsic's flagship product is Intrinsic Flowstate, an all-in-one web-based developer environment for designing, building, simulating, and deploying production-grade robotics solutions, paired with Intrinsic Intelligence — a portfolio of AI-powered capabilities including pose estimation, motion planning, grasp planning, and sensor-guided control — and IntrinsicOS, a robot operating system that spans cloud to edge. Developers extend Flowstate by writing Skills and Services in Python and C++ via the open-source Intrinsic SDK (Apache-2.0), or compose them visually via behavior trees in the Flowstate Process Editor. The platform integrates deeply with ROS through Intrinsic's 2022 acquisition of Open Source Robotics Corporation (OSRC) — the commercial arm of Open Robotics — while ROS, Gazebo, and Open-RMF stewardship remain with the independent OSRF non-profit. Flowstate is currently in a gated beta / trusted-tester program; production access is granted to enterprise customers, systems integrators, and participants in programs such as the AI for Industry Challenge. Pricing is not publicly disclosed and there is no self-service developer signup.

providers.name: Hyperganic
providers.description: Hyperganic is a Munich- and Singapore-based deep-tech software company building algorithmic engineering technology for additive manufacturing (3D printing). Its flagship product, HyDesign, is a browser-based application for creating, customizing, and optimizing 3D-printed latticed parts, combining implicit (meshless) modeling with validated materials and cloud simulation. Capabilities include lattice grading, TPMS structures, shell/offset and emboss/skin editing, image modulation, meshless linear-elastic simulation, topology optimization, and Lattice Boltzmann CFD. It serves lightweighting, thermal management, metamaterials, mass customization, tooling, and bioengineering use cases across aerospace, automotive, and sports. Backed by HV Capital. Hyperganic does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: LocBox Labs
providers.description: LocBox Labs is associated with Hownd, Inc. (formerly FetchRev), a Tempe, Arizona automated promotions and local-merchant marketing platform that helps restaurants, health and beauty businesses, family entertainment centers, and retail merchants generate new and repeat customers. The platform runs automated marketing across web popups, email drip campaigns, social media, a MyHownd consumer mobile app, buy-now buttons, and guest-WiFi capture on a pay-per-visit billing model. The merchant application runs at app.locbox.com. This provider was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface could be found on the provider's public properties.

providers.name: Neara
providers.description: Neara is a physics-enabled digital twin platform for electric utilities and network operators. It builds a single, physics-accurate 3D model of a utility's entire network from LiDAR, GIS, and imagery, then runs engineering-grade simulations across vegetation management, wildfire and flood mitigation, severe-weather response, clearance and conductor-clash analysis, pole utilization and FEA, asset inspection and lifecycle management, and transmission and distribution network design. Utilities use Neara to plan, harden, and operate their grids at scale — forecasting and backcasting resilience, prioritizing risk, and optimizing capital spend across millions of assets. Founded in Australia, Neara operates regionally across ANZ, the USA, and Europe.

providers.name: Optimyzee
providers.description: Optimyzee is an AI-powered ad management platform that structures and optimizes Google Ads search campaigns in minutes, acting like a senior PPC specialist. It analyzes a website and its keywords to generate an optimized campaign structure, keyword plans, and responsive search ad copy, then validates ads against Google Ads standards in real time to improve click-through rate, conversion rate, and Quality Score while lowering cost-per-click. It targets business owners, marketing agencies, and individual marketers. Backed by 500 Global and Triple S Ventures, it is a consumer-facing SaaS product with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Pixc
providers.description: Pixc is an ecommerce enablement company that builds Shopify apps automating the visual busywork of running an online store — product photo resizing and AI framing, background removal and retouching, AI-generated alt text for SEO, AI lifestyle imagery, and automated visual merchandising of collections. Founded in 2014 and backed by 500 Global, Pixc also runs a professional bulk product photo-editing service (pay-per-image credits with an optional Pixc Member subscription) and serves 32,000+ Shopify merchants. Pixc is an app developer and photo-editing service; it exposes no public developer API.

providers.name: Wishup
providers.description: Wishup is a remote-work outsourcing platform that matches businesses with pre-vetted virtual assistants, bookkeepers, and automation specialists, typically onboarding a trained professional within 60 minutes. Its managed talent handles inbox and calendar management, CRM and social-media work, bookkeeping, project management, and AI-driven workflow automation across industries such as healthcare, e-commerce, real estate, startups, nonprofits, and legal services. Wishup runs a client-facing Employee Management App for task tracking and real-time feedback, but publishes no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Colibri
providers.description: ColibrITD (Colibri) is a French quantum-computing deep-tech company founded in 2019 in Paris by Dr. Laurent Guiraud and Hacene Goudjil, with a mission to make quantum computing accessible to any enterprise. It develops quantum software for scientific and industrial applications, including QUICK (a quantum multiphysics simulation platform), QUICK-PDE (a Qiskit function for solving partial differential equations), the H-DES hybrid differential-equation solver, and MPQP (Multi-Platform Quantum Programming) - an open-source Python library for building quantum circuits and executing them across IBM Qiskit, Eviden myQLM, Google Cirq, AWS Braket, and Microsoft Azure Quantum backends. ColibrITD serves the semiconductors, finance, defense, aerospace, automotive, and energy industries. Its primary developer surface is the MPQP Python SDK (PyPI + GitHub) and its documentation, rather than a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Agency Ai
providers.description: Agency (agency.inc) is an agentic AI company building autonomous customer success agents for B2B SaaS. Founded in 2024 by Elias Torres and Luke Van Seters (previously of Drift), Agency raised a $20M Series A led by Menlo Ventures with Sequoia, Felicis, Snowflake Ventures, and Databricks Ventures. Its flagship product, Kai, is a superintelligent AI co-worker that runs the long tail of the customer book most companies leave untouched — drawing signal from email, Slack, support tickets, and product usage to monitor accounts, catch churn signals early, and run personalized onboarding, adoption, expansion, and renewal outreach through customer-success Playbooks. Agency is a SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, GDPR-aligned application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Riff
providers.description: Riff is an Oslo, Norway based enterprise software company building AI agents for supply chain, procurement, planning, and logistics operations. Its agents automate repetitive back-office work such as chasing supplier order confirmations, updating order and delivery status, matching invoices, and monitoring deliveries, while keeping actions deterministic, auditable, and team-controlled rather than purely generative. Riff integrates non-disruptively with existing ERP systems including SAP, Oracle, Infor, and Microsoft, is EU-based with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 aligned and GDPR compliant data handling, and was founded by veterans of Cognite. The company raised a $16M Series A backed by Northzone and other investors. Riff has no public developer or API program at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Shield AI
providers.description: Shield AI builds autonomous defense systems anchored by Hivemind, an AI-powered autonomy stack that pilots aircraft and robotic platforms without GPS or communications. Hardware products include the V-BAT vertical-takeoff ISR aircraft, the Nova quadcopter, and the announced X-BAT AI-piloted VTOL fighter. Hivemind itself is delivered as a layered platform: EdgeOS (real-time C++ autonomy middleware), Pilot (autonomy behavior catalog), Forge (autonomy factory for build, sim, and test), and Commander (C2 and fleet integration). In 2025 Shield AI introduced Hivemind Enterprise, a partner-facing SDK for building, evaluating, testing, and deploying mission autonomy on customer platforms. There is no public, self-service API; access to Hivemind SDKs and developer tooling is gated through partnership and is subject to U.S. export controls (ITAR/EAR).

providers.name: Machinations
providers.description: Machinations is a visual platform for designing, simulating, and balancing game economies, tokenomics, and other complex systems. Studios and designers model resource flows as interactive node-and-connection diagrams, run Monte-Carlo simulations to predict outcomes, and balance economies before a single line of production code is written. The product spans Design, Predict, and Balance modules plus an AI Builder that generates runnable diagrams from natural-language descriptions and a spreadsheet integration. It is used by studios such as Amazon Games, Hasbro, and Zynga and taught at MIT, NYU, and Berkeley. Machinations is a Seedcamp portfolio company; at the time of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: NEURA Robotics
providers.description: NEURA Robotics is a German deep-tech company building cognitive and humanoid robots for industry, business, and everyday life. It develops robots such as the 4NE-1 humanoid and the MAiRA, MiPA, LARA, and MAV cognitive cobots, powered by its proprietary AI system AURA. Its Neuraverse ecosystem is a connected platform and app marketplace that links robots, developers, and partners so AI models, applications, and hardware come together to make the robots smarter. NEURA Robotics is backed by HV Capital. As of this profile the company exposes no public, documented developer API: neuraverse.com is a gated single-page application portal, and no OpenAPI, developer documentation, or well-known discovery endpoints are published on its public surface.

providers.name: Resolve Systems
providers.description: Resolve Systems (resolve.io) is an enterprise IT automation and AIOps platform that helps IT and operations teams automate incident resolution, service-desk workflows, and cross-domain remediation at scale. Its "Agentic Resolution Fabric" combines a Knowledge Agent (contextual answers across chat, portals, and collaboration tools), an Automation Agent (autonomous cross-domain workflows that remediate, configure, and orchestrate IT processes in real time), and Agent Assist (enriched diagnostics, related incidents, and next-best actions). Product lines include Resolve Actions, Actions Pro, Actions Express, and Barista, spanning IT process automation (ITPA), robotic process automation, and agentic service management. The company positions itself around cutting manual tickets by up to 90% and reports large aggregate customer savings. Resolve is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. This profile was enriched from public web sources; Resolve does not appear to publish a public, self-service developer API, OpenAPI definition, or open developer portal — integration and automation are delivered through the platform's connectors and customer-gated documentation.

providers.name: Jaipur Robotics
providers.description: Jaipur Robotics is a Manno, Switzerland based deep-tech company building advanced computer vision and deep learning solutions for the waste-to-energy sector. Its product, Jaipur Intelligence, applies patent-pending image recognition to plant bunkers and truck unloading bays to detect oversized and dangerous items, map the calorific value (LHV) of incoming waste in real time, and track crane operations — helping operators cut emissions, improve waste mixing and combustion stability, and minimize unplanned shutdowns. The company operates a gated customer application at app.jaipurrobotics.com and is backed by Techstars, Innosuisse, Venture Kick, CSEM and others. It currently publishes a marketing site and a customer login only; there is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Praxis AI (Vortexify)
providers.description: Praxis AI is a Y Combinator (Fall 2024) company that now operates as Vortexify (vortexify.ai). Vortexify is an AI-native platform that generates operational software directly from a company's data: teams connect data sources through 20+ prebuilt connectors (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, BigQuery, Redshift, Snowflake, NetSuite, Oracle, S3, Azure Blob, Google Sheets/Drive, SharePoint and more), describe requirements in plain English, and AI agents plan, code, test and deploy backend logic plus custom frontends with no infrastructure to manage. The platform emphasizes building complete apps on operational data rather than just dashboards, with built-in scheduling, serverless compute execution, role-based access control, audit logs, sandboxed environments, token-based authentication, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Praxis AI was founded by Aditya Tewari (ex-Palantir) and Ransika Liyanage (ex-Tesla, GM, Deloitte), originally focused on manufacturing-specific AI agents for predicting and preventing machine failures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator. Vortexify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: 1X Technologies
providers.description: 1X Technologies is a humanoid robotics company headquartered in Palo Alto, California with vertically integrated manufacturing at the NEO Factory in Hayward. Its product line includes EVE (an earlier wheeled-base humanoid used for commercial pilots) and NEO, the company's bipedal consumer humanoid marketed as the "world's first consumer-ready humanoid robot for the home," with NEO Beta and NEO Gamma development variants and a consumer pre-order program. 1X is an OpenAI portfolio company and collaborates with NVIDIA on training-data generation and on-board model execution. The company maintains a public GitHub organization (github.com/1x-technologies) with 24 repositories, most notably 1xgpt — a world-modeling challenge for humanoid robots — alongside Halodi robot URDF models, ROS2 examples for the EVE robot, and robotics infrastructure tools. 1X does not publish a public hosted API or developer SDK; engagement is via product purchase, research challenges, and open-source code.

providers.name: Brain
providers.description: Brain Co. builds agent-native operating systems for institutions across the public and private sectors. Its Atlas platform powers GovOS — permitting, licensing, claims, and casework for government agencies at national scale — and InsuranceOS for underwriting, claims, authorization, and insurance operations, with an emphasis on sovereign-grade security and vendor neutrality. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the company was cofounded by Elad Gil, Jared Kushner, and Luis Videgaray, with a team drawn from Google, DeepMind, NVIDIA, Palantir, and Tesla. Brain Co. does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definitions; this profile tracks its public web surface (news, trust center, privacy and terms) pending any future developer program.

providers.name: Motional
providers.description: Motional is a Boston-headquartered autonomous-vehicle company formed as a joint venture between Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv. Its core product is an all-electric IONIQ 5 robotaxi built on a Hyundai E-GMP platform with Motional's full Level 4 autonomous driving stack and a sensor suite including lidar, radar, and cameras. Motional operates commercial robotaxi service in Las Vegas in partnership with Uber, Uber Eats, and Lyft, with additional operations in Boston, Pittsburgh, Santa Monica, Singapore, and Seoul. The company's most influential developer artifact is nuScenes, the open large-scale multimodal autonomous-driving dataset originally released by nuTonomy (a Motional predecessor), now a de facto benchmark for 3D perception research. Motional also publishes the nuscenes-devkit Python library and AVCDL cybersecurity development lifecycle materials on GitHub. Motional does not publish a traditional public developer API; the developer surface is research-dataset access plus open-source devkits.

providers.name: Sphero
providers.description: Sphero designs programmable robots and STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and math) learning tools for K-12 education. Its product line spans indi, Mini, Snap, BOLT+, littleBits, RVR+ and Blueprint robots, paired with standards-aligned curriculum (NGSS, CSTA, ISTE) delivered through Sphero Central. For developers and educators, Sphero publishes a public robot-control SDK (sdk.sphero.com) that programs Sphero RVR+ / RVR robots from development boards — Raspberry Pi, micro:bit and Arduino — using Python, Node.js/TypeScript and C++. Sphero exposes robot-control SDKs and a locally-run Node.js RESTful interface rather than a hosted public web API. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist as part of the APIs.io network.

providers.name: Standard Practice
providers.description: Standard Practice builds voice AI for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) teams. Its AI agents place and handle outbound phone calls to insurance payers to automate administrative work — claim status follow-up, benefits verification, prior authorization, and EDI enrollment — so billing teams can scale collections and get paid more, faster. The platform is delivered as a private, login-gated web application. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and Wing Venture Capital and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Waymo
providers.description: Waymo is the autonomous driving subsidiary of Alphabet, originally spun out of the Google Self-Driving Car Project. The company develops the Waymo Driver, a full Level 4 autonomous driving stack combining custom lidar, radar, and camera sensors with proprietary perception, prediction, and planning models. Waymo One operates a commercial robotaxi service in Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Austin, and other expanding US markets, with announced launches in Tokyo and London. The company has logged tens of millions of rider-only miles and reports significantly fewer serious-injury crashes than human-driven benchmarks. Waymo does not publish a traditional public developer API. Its primary developer-facing artifacts are the Waymo Open Dataset, the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, the Waymax JAX-based driving simulator, and a robust research publication catalogue spanning perception, behaviour prediction, planning, simulation, and end-to-end driving. Consumer access is through the Waymo One mobile app.

providers.name: MoonLake AI
providers.description: Moonlake AI Inc. is a San Francisco based company building world models and simulation infrastructure for embodied AI. Its platform turns an image, video, or text description into physically accurate, simulation-ready 3D models of the world — assets shipped with baked-in physics and articulation (joints, ranges, drive limits) that export directly to USD, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, and MuJoCo. Teams generate sim environments and digital twins in hours instead of weeks via a hosted generation API. Moonlake is backed by Threshold (formerly DFJ), AIX Ventures, and NVIDIA's venture arm, and was named to the CB Insights AI 100 in 2026.

providers.name: Nabu
providers.description: Nabu is an AI-powered customs clearance platform that automates international trade compliance end to end. It collects shipment data from emails, PDFs, Excel files, databases, and TMS records via API, EDI, SFTP, or email, prepares complete compliant customs files, and generates pre-filled import/export declarations ready for submission in standard customs software. Nabu targets customs brokers and declaration teams, offering autonomous processing, workload flexibility to absorb staffing gaps, and full auditability across multiple regions and local regulatory regimes. Backed by Techstars. No public developer API, documentation, or SDKs are published at this time.

providers.name: Posha
providers.description: Posha (formerly Nymble) is a consumer robotics company that makes an autonomous countertop kitchen robot which cooks fresh, home-style meals from raw ingredients across 1,000+ recipes. The device combines robotics, computer-vision cameras, automated heat, timing and stirring control, and culinary AI, paired with an iOS/Android companion app for real-time monitoring and recipe control. Backed by Accel, Posha is a consumer hardware and appliance product with a companion mobile app; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with real, verifiable public properties.

providers.name: CircuitLab
providers.description: CircuitLab, Inc. is an in-browser schematic capture and circuit simulation platform that lets engineers, students, educators, and hobbyists design and analyze analog and digital electronics systems before building a physical prototype. Running entirely in the browser with no installation, it offers schematic capture, mixed-signal SPICE-style simulation (DC, AC, transient, frequency-domain), custom device models and symbols, expression-based parameters, and shareable, exportable documentation. CircuitLab also publishes an electronics curriculum (CircuitLab Academy, the Ultimate Electronics textbook), community forums, and an electronics Q&A. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Y Combinator. At the time of this enrichment pass CircuitLab publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API description, so this profile captures its public web identity only.

providers.name: Ctrl
providers.description: Ctrl (Ctrl, Inc., a Delaware corporation) is an AI-powered workspace for revenue and sales teams that consolidates the tools and data a rep needs — CRM, email, calendar, and messaging — into a single actionable view. Founded in 2021 by Omri Sagzan and Aviv Nahum and based in Tel Aviv and London, Ctrl automates the manual work of updating records across apps such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Slack, and helps teams codify and replicate their winning sales playbooks. The company raised a $9M seed round led by LocalGlobe and Earlybird in 2023 and was acquired by Sana Labs in October 2024. Ctrl is a UI/workspace product surfaced as an Earlybird portfolio company; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Prized
providers.description: Prized is an AI-powered platform that lets non-technical operations, support, and finance teams build, deploy, and share secure internal tools without engineering. Users describe a workflow in natural language (or bring their own coding agent such as Claude Code) and Prized builds real software on company data that is pre-connected and scoped, with least-privilege database access per tool, credential isolation, outbound-traffic proxying, and an audit trail on every access. Tools deploy behind corporate authentication and connect to 20+ services including Salesforce, Postgres, Slack, Stripe, and Notion. Prized is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) company founded by Hudson Griffith and Marinos Eliades, both formerly of Gander (YC F24, acquired by Archer Aviation). Added to the API Evangelist network via the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Zatanna
providers.description: Zatanna is a Y Combinator (W2026) startup based in San Francisco that creates APIs for software that doesn't have any. It reverse-engineers the back ends of web-based cloud and on-prem software — ERPs (SAP), PMS/POS systems, insurance portals, and marketplaces — by observing real workflows, reconstructing the underlying request sequences, and hosting them as clean, callable APIs. Rather than relying on slow browser automation or computer-use agents, Zatanna gives AI agents faster, cheaper, and more reliable integrations, with a reliability layer that handles session management, authentication, and change detection. The agent-facing surface is a hosted, OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at api.zatanna.ai.

providers.name: SVT Robotics
providers.description: SVT Robotics builds the SOFTBOT Platform, a software integration and orchestration foundation for warehouse automation and the supply chain. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia, the company lets enterprises connect industrial systems, robotics, AMRs, and warehouse management software through standardized, prebuilt SOFTBOT Connectors — reducing integration complexity and enabling real-time visibility, faster automation deployments, and a resilient data backbone for automation and AI. Customers include DHL Supply Chain, Barrett Distribution Centers, and the Hagen Group. The provider operates a developer documentation hub for the SOFTBOT integration API (docs.svtrobotics.com, currently password-protected) and a public status page; no public OpenAPI, SDK, or open API surface was discoverable at enrichment time.

providers.name: Aeva
providers.description: Aeva Technologies is a Mountain View, California sensing and perception company that builds 4D LiDAR based on proprietary Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) technology, measuring instant velocity in addition to 3D position for every point in a scene. Its product line spans Atlas and Atlas Ultra long-range automotive-grade sensors, the Omni wide-view short-range sensor, and Eve 1 precision laser speed sensors for factory automation, serving autonomous vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, security, and physical-AI markets. Aeva is a hardware and perception-software provider rather than a web-API company: its developer surface is open-source software on the aevainc GitHub org (the AevaScenes Python SDK and Doppler ICP), the AevaScenes dataset, and product SDK/EULA-gated software delivered with its sensors. No public REST or web API is published.

providers.name: Dominion Dynamics
providers.description: Dominion Dynamics Inc. is a Canadian defence-technology company (Kanata/Ottawa, Ontario) building the autonomy stack for the Arctic and other extreme, infrastructure-constrained operating environments. It develops integrated autonomy, edge sensing, communications, and command-and-control systems for defence, security, and critical infrastructure. Its AuraNet platform is a peer-to-peer sensor mesh that fuses EO/IR/SAR imagery, SIGINT/EW/RF signals, telemetry, and structured reporting into a unified local intelligence stream that interoperates with existing allied C2 architectures, and its Aurion product is an open-source government procurement intelligence platform built on Canadian federal open data. Founded by Anduril alum Eliot Pence, the company raised a $139M CAD Series A (2026) led by Georgian. This profile currently has no public developer/API surface; the entry captures the company identity, security.txt, and llms.txt the company publishes.

providers.name: Universal Robots
providers.description: Universal Robots is a Danish collaborative-robot (cobot) manufacturer headquartered in Odense, Denmark, founded in 2005 by Esben Østergaard, Kasper Støy, and Kristian Kassow, and acquired by Teradyne in 2015 for USD 285 million. Universal Robots is the market leader in cobots, with more than 100,000 units sold worldwide and a 40–50% share of the global collaborative-robot market. The company ships two product generations — the e-Series (UR3e, UR7e, UR12e, UR16e) and the newer high-payload UR series (UR8 Long, UR15, UR18, UR20, UR30) — running the PolyScope 5 teach-pendant software stack and the next-generation PolyScope X platform. Universal Robots is unusual among industrial-robot vendors in publishing an extensive open developer surface: the C++ Universal_Robots_Client_Library, the Universal_Robots_ROS_Driver and Universal_Robots_ROS2_Driver, the RTDE Python Client Library, the Universal_Robots_Isaac_Driver for NVIDIA Isaac, the URCap SDK (PolyScope 5 Java) and PolyScopeX URCap SDK (TypeScript/HTML), and the URScript language. The wire-level protocols — Real-Time Data Exchange (RTDE), Dashboard Server, Primary/Secondary Client Interface, Reverse/Trajectory interfaces, XML-RPC, and the Tool Communication forwarder — are all documented and externally addressable over TCP, making UR cobots first-class citizens in third-party automation stacks, ROS/ROS 2, MoveIt, Isaac Sim, and the UR+ ecosystem (500+ certified end-effectors, vision systems, and URCap software extensions on universal-robots.com/plus). Universal Robots does not publish a public HTTP/REST API or OpenAPI specification — all programmatic access is via the documented socket protocols and SDKs.

providers.name: Walter
providers.description: Walter is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI employee for the manufacturing back office. Founded in 2026 by Nikolas Keller (CEO) and Lukas Postulka (CTO), Walter logs into the enterprise systems a company already runs on — SAP, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Teams, Outlook and Gmail — the way a new hire would, and takes over manual paperwork: reading sales orders and purchase orders from emails and PDFs, capturing and validating the data, cross-checking it against the ERP, ordering from suppliers and catching pricing errors before they ship. It uses a purpose-built document-understanding model (rather than legacy template OCR) that supports 270+ languages and reaches 90%+ accuracy after minimal training, cutting an order that used to take 15 minutes down to about one. Walter requires no integration project and no rip-and-replace, operating the same screens the team already uses. It is an early-stage company with no public API, developer program, SDKs or documentation; this profile captures its public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Praxis Labs
providers.description: Praxis Labs is an AI-powered leadership and human-skills learning platform, surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and acquired by Torch. Its flagship product, Pivotal Practice, uses immersive simulations, personalized AI coaching, and role-play scenarios to build critical management capabilities such as difficult conversations and performance discussions, with behavior-change tracking and ROI analytics. The learning application runs at practice.praxislabs.co behind login and integrates with HR/L&D systems including Workday, Docebo, and Degreed. Praxis Labs is SOC 2 Type 2 certified. No public API, developer portal, or SDK was found during enrichment; this remains a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Context.ai *
providers.description: Context (context.ai) is a unified enterprise AI platform for building, deploying, and improving AI agents at scale. The product is organized into modular components: a Workspace for authoring agent workflows in plain English, an Engine with 800+ connectors and IdP-brokered identity, Unify as a knowledge/institutional-context repository, and Evals for rubric-based quality scoring. It is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, or open weights) and offers hosted, VPC, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment. The company originated as a GV (Google Ventures) and Theory Ventures backed product-analytics-for-LLMs startup and now operates as an enterprise agent platform used by teams including Qualcomm, Stripe, and Palantir. This repo carries no public developer/API surface: the provider publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation, so most machine-readable artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: Intuition Robotics
providers.description: Intuition Robotics is a Tel Aviv-based AI company (with offices in the United States, Japan, and Greece) building social companion technology for older adults. Its flagship product, ElliQ, is an AI care companion robot that proactively engages users through natural conversation, body language, lights, and sound, powered by a proprietary "Relationship Orchestrator" cognitive-AI platform and multiple large language models to support health, wellness, cognitive engagement, and reducing loneliness. Intuition Robotics publishes no first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the ElliQ product store (elliq.com, on Shopify) does expose an agent-commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), including a published llms.txt and a UCP shopping MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search and checkout. Backed by Bloomberg Beta among other investors.

providers.name: Beyond Math
providers.description: BeyondMath is an AI company that has built what it calls the world's first foundational AI model of physics. Its Generative Physics Engine runs full-fidelity, engineering-grade simulations covering fluid, thermal, and structural analysis directly from uploaded geometry, without pre-meshing or preprocessing, and returns results up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD/FEA solvers while generalizing across unseen geometries without retraining. The platform lets engineering teams explore thousands of design variations in minutes rather than months across automotive, aerospace, energy, defense, semiconductor, construction, telecommunications, and electronics. Founded by Alan Patterson (CEO) and Darren Garvey (CTO), the company raised an $18.5M seed round and partners with NVIDIA and AWS. Access is gated behind a waitlist for the Generative Physics Studio; on-premise and private-cloud enterprise deployment is offered. No public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI is published at this time.

providers.name: Freedom Robotics
providers.description: Freedom Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics infrastructure company founded in 2017 that builds mission-critical software to help robotics companies build, operate, support, and scale heterogeneous robot fleets. Its cloud platform — sometimes referred to as Mission Control — provides device and fleet management, remote teleoperation (Pilot), live data streaming, smart alerts and notifications, fleet maps and heatmaps, deployment and service management, remote development, and analytics across cobots, industrial robots, AMRs, drones, and custom hardware. The platform is robot- and OS-agnostic, installs on a device in seconds via a single-line Freedom Agent installer, and integrates with ROS, ROS 2, Python, microcontrollers, Protobuf, Docker, and the cloud offerings of AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Freedom exposes a public REST API at api.freedomrobotics.ai covering accounts, devices, alerts, statistics, uploads, tokens, users, user groups, and zones, plus a Python SDK (freedomrobotics.link) with Link, MicroLink, message, log, image, and command-callback primitives for programmatic control and telemetry of large numbers of robots. The company has raised approximately $17M in venture funding and operates on a per-robot subscription model (publicly cited at roughly $300 per robot per month) with custom enterprise plans negotiated through sales.

providers.name: Qventus
providers.description: Qventus is a healthcare technology company that provides an AI-powered automation platform for hospital operations. Its "AI teammates" combine machine learning, generative AI, and behavioral science to streamline care-coordination workflows across surgical growth and operating-room utilization, perioperative and pre-admission-testing coordination, inpatient capacity and discharge planning, and care-gap and coding automation. Qventus sells to health systems and hospitals as a B2B SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Mayfield, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Tutor Intelligence
providers.description: Tutor Intelligence builds AI-powered robotic workers for industrial and logistics operations, delivered as robots-as-a-service. Its flagship Cassie palletizing robot handles material-handling tasks — palletizing, depalletizing, and case picking — in warehouses and factories without facility retrofits, and a humanoid robot, Sonny, is slated for late 2026. The company pairs on-robot autonomy with a human-in-the-loop teleoperation and data model, priced per robot-hour with no long-term contracts, and is backed by Union Square Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is published as of this profiling; the company's public GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and open-source forks rather than a first-party product API.

providers.name: Capstan Medical
providers.description: Capstan Medical is a Santa Cruz, California medical device company founded in 2020 out of the Occam Labs incubator by Dan Wallace, with Maggie Nixon as CEO. The company is developing a surgical robotics platform for structural heart disease, merging robotic catheter navigation with next-generation transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve implants so heart valves can be repaired or replaced without open heart surgery. In 2025 Capstan completed what it describes as the world's first robotic catheter mitral valve replacements in humans, and it raised a $110M Series C led by Eclipse with participation from Intuitive Ventures and Yu Galaxy, bringing total funding past $150M ahead of a second-generation system planned for 2026. Capstan is pre-commercial and regulated medical device focused: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Convey
providers.description: Convey is an enterprise AI platform for building and running autonomous "digital teammates" — AI workers that non-technical operators train by describing a workflow or sharing their screen, after which the teammate runs business processes end to end across existing enterprise systems (Salesforce, NetSuite, ad operations, reporting) with role-based access, isolated agent identities, dedicated credentials, audit logs, and escalation to a human on high-stakes decisions. Founded by former DoorDash and project44 engineers, Convey raised a $38M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in June 2026 (with Khosla Ventures and Pear VC) and reports 1.1M+ hours of work completed for customers including NBCUniversal, TelevisaUnivision, Unity, and Samsara. The platform is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. Convey is an enterprise, contact-sales product with no public developer API or documentation surface as of this profile.

providers.name: Fintor
providers.description: Fintor is an enterprise software company that provides an agentic AI workforce for mortgage lending operations. Its purpose-built, autonomous AI agents execute mortgage workflows end to end - from application through closing - with human-in-the-loop oversight, integrating with existing loan origination systems (LOS), CRMs, and contact centers rather than replacing them. Product modules include a Loan Officer Assistant (document intake, borrower communication, gap analysis), a Processor Assistant (third-party orders, condition tracking, disclosures), Predictive Conditioning, a Closing Agent, and a Manager Assistant for forecasting and reporting. Fintor ships pre-built connectors for Encompass, Salesforce, Five9, Polly, and Blend, exposes documented API integrations, and is SOC 2 Type II certified with encryption, RBAC, approval chains, and audit logging.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: ReadyAPI
providers.description: ReadyAPI is SmartBear's enterprise-grade automated API testing platform. It unifies functional, security, performance, and virtualization testing for REST, SOAP, GraphQL, Kafka, JDBC, and JMS APIs. ReadyAPI is delivered as a desktop and CI/CD tool rather than as a public REST API, integrating with Jenkins, Azure DevOps, Git, and other automation platforms via TestEngine.

providers.name: Roborock
providers.description: Roborock is a global consumer robotics company best known for its robot vacuum and mop cleaners, wet/dry wash-and-fill floor washers, and connected home-cleaning appliances controlled through the Roborock mobile app. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Beijing, the company was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. Roborock operates a private cloud that backs its consumer mobile app but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program. It does operate a public Trust Center documenting the security and privacy design of its IoT products, including TÜV Rheinland EN 303 645 and UL Diamond IoT Security certifications.

providers.name: SiMa
providers.description: SiMa.ai is a Silicon Valley machine-learning semiconductor company building a co-optimized hardware and software platform for physical AI at the edge. Its MLSoC (Machine Learning System-on-Chip) family — including the Modalix line delivering roughly 50 TOPS under 10 watts in multiple form factors — targets drones, robotics, automotive, industrial, retail, government, and healthcare. The developer experience centers on the Palette software suite and an agentic development environment that compiles and deploys computer-vision and multimodal models onto SiMa silicon, backed by a Developer Center, a model browser, a Hugging Face model hub (simaai), and a community forum. SiMa.ai ships downloadable SDK/CLI tooling and evaluation hardware (Modalix DevKit) rather than a hosted public HTTP API.

providers.name: RealPact
providers.description: RealPact is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-native operating system for real estate brokerages. Its voice-enabled AI agents automate the operational work behind every deal: the Deed Agent retrieves county deed records and flags encumbrances, the Tax & Vision Agent uses computer vision to extract tax assessments and property details, the Property Agent consolidates ownership and property information, and the Transaction Agent auto-fills contracts, manages disclosures, coordinates signatures, and tracks compliance deadlines. The company aims to compress transaction workflows from hours to minutes for brokerages, with early customers including Four Seasons Sotheby's International Realty and Black House Real Estate. Backed by Y Combinator and the LeapYear Fund, RealPact currently operates a customer-facing application and marketing site but publishes no public API, SDK, or developer program as of this profiling.

providers.name: Hilbert's AI
providers.description: Hilbert's AI is an AI-native growth infrastructure platform for B2C companies, backed by a16z. It unifies fragmented product, marketing, and finance data into a single source of truth and layers agentic automation on top through four intelligence stages: Detect (anomalies, churn signals, and behavioral shifts), Reason (ML/deep-learning root-cause analysis and forecasting), Act (autonomous growth interventions such as churn plays and channel adjustments), and Optimize (continuous budget and strategy tuning). A natural-language interface lets growth, product, and finance teams collapse months-long decision cycles into minutes without writing code or navigating dashboards. Hilbert connects to existing data and paid-media stacks via prebuilt integrations (Meta, Google, Pinterest, Snapchat, Reddit, Google Analytics 4, Triple Whale, Klaviyo, Braze) and is SOC 2 certified. The product is delivered as a hosted application; there is no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Applied Intuition
providers.description: Applied Intuition builds physical AI software and systems for intelligent machines, helping customers develop, test, validate, deploy, and operate autonomy and vehicle intelligence across automotive, defense, trucking, mining, construction, and agriculture. Its product lines include a Self-Driving System (a unified autonomy stack for land, air, and sea), Vehicle OS (an operating system for intelligent machines), and Tools for Vehicle Intelligence covering simulation, validation, data, training, and evaluation workflows. The company operates as a private enterprise vendor and does not currently publish a public developer API or self-service portal; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and machine-readable llms.txt.

providers.name: Zomma
providers.description: Zomma (Zomma Labs) is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building AI agents that automate repetitive back-office operations for investment firms — hedge funds, asset managers, and fintech companies. Rather than integrating through traditional APIs, its computer-use agents perceive and operate existing portals, desktop applications, and PDFs the way a human would (clicking, reading, typing) to handle reconciliation, client onboarding, KYC, and investor reporting, with human approval required before any submission. Zomma also markets a developer-facing computer-use API ("plug Hermes, Claude, or your own agent into our API") that is currently waitlist / pre-general availability with no public specification, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: Formic
providers.description: Formic is a Chicago, Illinois-based Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) company founded in 2020 by Saman Farid that delivers full-service industrial automation to American manufacturers on a pay-per-hour, fixed monthly subscription model with no capital expenditure. Formic specializes in end-of-line manufacturing operations — palletizing, case packing, and robotic pallet wrapping — and pairs deployed robots with a 24/7 remote monitoring, support, and field-service operation. The company's software stack includes Formic Core, an embedded operating system that abstracts motion, vision, sensing, and real-time coordination across heterogeneous industrial robot hardware (Fanuc, ABB, Kuka, Doosan) behind unified control interfaces; Formic Cortex; the Colony 2.0 fleet dashboard; FAST configuration tools; and Formic Production Intelligence (FPI), a manufacturer-facing analytics surface. Formic has raised more than $86M across rounds led by Lux Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and other investors, and works through a network of 100+ system-integrator partners with 500+ systems deployed. Formic's revenue model is the RaaS subscription itself; there is no public developer API, no published SDKs, and no public customer-portal API documentation. Formic Core's "unified APIs" are internal abstractions used by Formic engineers and integrator partners to drive robot hardware — they are not exposed to manufacturers or third-party developers.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: AMP Robotics
providers.description: AMP Robotics (operating as AMP Sortation) is an artificial-intelligence company for the waste and recycling industry that designs, builds, and operates advanced, cost-competitive facilities to process single-stream recycling and municipal solid waste. Its Smart Sortation technology suite combines computer vision (real-time material characterization), high-speed air-jet sortation (Jet and MicroJet), and robotic-arm sortation (Delta) to raise material-recovery rates, cut contamination, and extend landfill life. The flagship AMP ONE platform delivers fully automated, facility-scale sortation processing from 10K to 1M+ tons annually for waste haulers, material-recovery facilities, and municipalities. AMP Robotics is a Google Ventures (GV) portfolio company. No public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; this profile is maintained for network discovery and identity.

providers.name: Beewise
