providers.description: Beewise is an agricultural technology company building the BeeHome, an AI- and robotics-enabled beehive that autonomously monitors, cares for, and protects honeybee colonies to reduce colony loss and deliver reliable pollination. Founded to address bee colony collapse, Beewise combines computer vision, robotics, and cloud software to detect pests and disease, regulate hive climate, and dispatch precision pollination for growers. The company serves growers with guaranteed pollination services, beekeepers with technology-enhanced hive management, and property owners through its Bees for Buildings program. Beewise is a venture-backed company (Insight Partners portfolio) surfaced into the API Evangelist network; it operates a customer grower portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Bright Machines
providers.description: Bright Machines is a San Francisco-based software-defined manufacturing company founded in 2018 by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan that builds a full-stack intelligent automation platform for electronics and AI-infrastructure assembly. Its Microfactory pairs modular Bright Robotic Cells with Brightware, a platform operating system that orchestrates hardware, runs a machine-vision "Smart Skills" perception stack, and provides manufacturing-execution services for work orders, material management and real-time production KPIs. Bright Data, the company's data layer, unifies component, process and enterprise-system data through secure APIs and auditable data flows, and Bright Designer turns product CAD into assembly-ready digital twins using NVIDIA Omniverse on Microsoft Azure. The company has raised roughly $279M from Eclipse, BlackRock, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Jabil and others. All platform and data interfaces are delivered to customers under commercial engagement; Bright Machines publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: buynomics
providers.description: Buynomics is a Cologne, Germany-based software company providing an AI-powered Revenue Growth Management (RGM) platform for consumer goods, retail, telecom, and consumer software companies. Its proprietary "Virtual Shoppers AI" runs agent-based simulations of consumer purchasing behavior so commercial teams can optimize pricing, promotions, price pack architecture (product mix), and trade terms before going to market — capturing cross- effects, cannibalization, and competitive response. The platform's Decision Guide generates prescriptive recommendations from thousands of evaluated scenarios. Buynomics is used by brands including Unilever, Nestle, L'Oreal, Danone, General Mills, Vodafone, and Ferrero, and is backed by Insight Partners and Seedcamp. The product is delivered as a web application; no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is published at this time.

providers.name: Carbon Robotics
providers.description: Carbon Robotics is a Seattle-based physical-AI and agricultural robotics company building autonomous systems that help farmers cut costs and reduce chemical use. Its flagship LaserWeeder G2 uses computer vision and high-power lasers to eliminate weeds without herbicides, and its Carbon Autonomy product adds remote-supervised autonomy to compatible John Deere tractors. The underlying Carbon AI Large Plant Model is trained on 150 million labeled plants across 15 countries and 100+ crops. Carbon Robotics operates a customer grower cloud portal and Starlink-connected fleet control, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal as of this profiling.

providers.name: Datumate
providers.description: Datumate is a construction technology company whose cloud-native SaaS platform, DatuBIM, turns drone imagery, laser-scanning, and site data into real-time progress tracking, deviation detection, automated reporting, and actionable analytics for heavy civil infrastructure projects. It serves asset owners, general contractors, and engineering and consulting firms across roads, highways, rail, bridges, and earthworks, giving multi-site visibility from design validation through construction to final inspection. The company reports 125+ active customers, thousands of managed sites, and tens of thousands of processed drone flights. Datumate has Israeli engineering roots (Technion) with leadership based in Miami, Florida, and is backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Drag Bot
providers.description: drag&bot is a web-based industrial robotics software platform for the intuitive setup, programming, and operation of industrial robots without prior robotics or coding skills. Founded in Stuttgart in 2016 and acquired by KEBA in 2021, it lets production workers assemble robot programs by dragging and dropping reusable Function Blocks. The platform is built on ROS (Robot Operating System), making it vendor-neutral across robot brands such as KUKA, ABB, Universal Robots, FANUC, Denso, Kinova, and Aubo, as well as a wide range of grippers and peripheral tools. Developers extend the platform with Python/JSON Function Blocks and ROS-based Components (hardware drivers), and integrate with factory equipment over Modbus TCP/IP and MQTT. drag&bot has been integrated into KEBA's Kemro X automation platform. Its programmatic surface is exposed as ROS services, topics, and messages rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Gamma Technologies
providers.description: Gamma Technologies develops GT-SUITE, the multi-physics system simulation software used by engineers to model, simulate, and optimize complex systems across automotive, HVACR, aerospace, industrial machinery, and shipbuilding. GT-SUITE combines 0D/1D/3D physics-based modeling, prebuilt model libraries, digital-twin workflows, and native AI tooling (GT Intelligence Studio and a Machine Learning Assistant). The company is a desktop/engineering CAE vendor rather than an API-first provider and publishes no public REST API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and enriched with the identity and domain-security signals that are publicly available.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Kodiak AI
providers.description: Kodiak AI, Inc. (formerly Kodiak Robotics) is a Mountain View, California company building the Kodiak Driver, an AI-powered ground autonomy system for driverless trucking and defense vehicles. Founded in April 2018 by Don Burnette, Kodiak develops a purpose-built autonomous driving stack — sensor pods, 4D radar, sparse maps, and fallback systems — that integrates into third-party driving platforms rather than shipping a vehicle of its own. The company runs commercial driverless freight lanes in Texas, Oklahoma, Ohio and Indiana with partners including Atlas Energy Solutions, Maersk, Martin Brower, Roehl Transport, JB Hunt and Werner, and it adapts the same driver to defense and industrial missions with General Dynamics Land Systems, Textron Systems and the US Army. Kodiak raised a $125M Series B in 2021 with Lightspeed Venture Partners, Battery Ventures, CRV, SIP Global Partners and others participating, and became a public company through a business combination with Ares Acquisition Corporation II. Kodiak publishes a corporate web presence, a news/RSS feed and an llms.txt for agents, but does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Kodiak AI
providers.description: Kodiak AI, Inc. (formerly Kodiak Robotics) is a Mountain View, California company founded in 2018 that builds AI-powered ground autonomy — the "Kodiak Driver" — for long-haul freight trucking and for off-road, industrial, and defense ground vehicles. The company sells a turnkey driver-as-a-product to fleet operators rather than a public developer API: its surface is a corporate website, a news/press feed, a safety report, and investor-relations material. Kodiak has run driverless operations for partners including Atlas Energy, Roehl Transport, Martin Brower, Tyson Foods, and West Fraser, and works with Bosch, NVIDIA, and General Dynamics Land Systems on hardware and defense autonomy. It reports more than 2.6 million autonomous miles and 7,000+ delivered loads. No public API, SDK, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition has been found; the company does publish an llms.txt for AI crawlers.

providers.name: Loft Dynamics
providers.description: Loft Dynamics is a Swiss aviation technology company (founded 2016, headquartered in Dübendorf, Switzerland with a North American office in Santa Monica) that builds virtual reality flight simulation training devices (FSTDs) for helicopters, fixed-wing aircraft, and eVTOLs. Its simulators combine full-scale replica cockpits, dynamic motion platforms, 360-degree VR visuals, and advanced pose tracking, and were the first VR aircraft simulators to earn EASA and FAA qualification. Products include VR simulators for the Airbus H145, Airbus H125, and Robinson R22 helicopters, with Boeing 737 and eVTOL platforms in development. Customers include Alaska Airlines, the FAA, Airbus Helicopters, the LAPD, and Marshall University. The company operates the LoftHUB customer platform but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Miso Robotics
providers.description: Miso Robotics is a Pasadena, California kitchen-automation company that builds AI-powered robotics and restaurant operations software for commercial food service. Its flagship product, Flippy, is an autonomous fry station that uses computer vision and NVIDIA-accelerated motion planning to identify food items, detect doneness and run up to 100 baskets per hour on existing commercial fryers from Frymaster, Henny Penny and Pitco. Miso also ships Zippy (built on the acquired Zignyl platform), a real-time digital shift manager for forecasting, scheduling, task management, incentives and payroll that connects to restaurant point-of-sale systems. Customers include White Castle, Jack in the Box, CaliBurger and Auntie Anne's. Miso publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract and no SDKs; its integrations are delivered as private partner connections (Toast, PAR and other POS vendors) arranged through sales, and its public GitHub organization carries ROS/robotics and cloud-infrastructure forks used internally rather than a client-facing API surface.

providers.name: Skyryse
providers.description: Skyryse is an El Segundo, California aviation technology company founded in 2016 by Mark Groden and Mitch Adler that builds SkyOS, a universal operating system for flight. SkyOS is a retrofittable hardware and software stack that replaces complex mechanical flight controls with a triply redundant, software-driven system, letting a pilot fly an airplane or helicopter with a single control stick and touchscreens. The platform delivers simplified flight controls, inherent stability, automated maneuvers, emergency autorotation, automated zero-visibility landing, envelope protection, and optionally piloted capability. Skyryse also produces Skyryse One, a SkyOS-powered production helicopter, and Skylar, a universal AI flight assistant. Customers and partners span the U.S. military, law enforcement, Cal Fire, emergency medical services, disaster response, and private operators. In February 2026 the company raised over $300 million in Series C funding at a $1.15 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Autopilot and Fidelity Investments. Skyryse operates as a certified-avionics and aircraft manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Polsia
providers.description: Polsia is an autonomous AI business-management platform marketed as "AI that runs your company while you sleep." It deploys a set of specialized AI agents — business planning, competitor research, social media, ads, email outreach, customer support, code generation, finance, and deployment — coordinated by an orchestrator to run a company's daily operations on recurring schedules for a monthly subscription plus a share of revenue generated on the platform. Founded by Ben Sera and backed by True Ventures and Sound Ventures (raised $30M at a $250M valuation in 2026), Polsia is a hosted consumer/SMB SaaS product and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Clone
providers.description: Clone Robotics develops musculoskeletal, intelligent humanoid androids and robotic hands built on Myofiber, its artificial-muscle technology pioneered in 2021, driven by water-based hydraulics and biomimetic joints. Its flagship Clone Alpha is a full-body biomimetic humanoid with synthetic organs; the Clone Hand is its foundational dexterous-manipulation platform. The developer surface is a first-party Python client (clone_client) exposing a high-level gRPC (proto3) API to directly control the Clone Robot over the local network — actuating muscles via impulses/pulses/pressures, driving pinch and hydra valves, managing the water-pump pressure source, streaming IMU/pose/joint telemetry, and configuring cameras. There is no public HTTP/REST API or hosted endpoint; control is LAN-scoped gRPC discovered over zeroconf/mDNS by robot name or IP. Co-founded 2021 by Dhanush Radhakrishna and Lukasz Kozlik.

providers.name: Expedock
providers.description: Expedock is a digital business process outsourcing (BPO) and document-automation company for the logistics and freight-forwarding industry. It pairs AI-powered document automation products (FCL/LCL accounts-payable automation, monthly statement automation, and commercial invoice and packing-list data entry) with tech-enabled remote teams supported by operations managers and QA specialists. Freight forwarders, 3PLs, and supply-chain operators use Expedock to digitize shipping documents, automate back-office workflows, and scale operations without scaling headcount. Customers include Maersk, Gebrueder Weiss, and large shippers such as Nike, Adidas, Coca-Cola, and Shell. Expedock is backed by Insight Partners. The company operates a Digital BPO offering and document-automation product suite; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: Hesai Technology
providers.description: Hesai Technology is a global leader in 3D LiDAR perception, designing and manufacturing high-performance lidar sensors for autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, and industrial automation. Its sensors are deployed by major automotive OEMs and autonomous-vehicle companies across more than 40 countries. Hesai does not expose a public REST/HTTP API; its developer surface is source-distributed C++ SDKs, ROS and ROS2 drivers, and integration plugins (including an NVIDIA DriveWorks plugin) published on the HesaiTechnology GitHub organization, alongside a developer portal and downloadable firmware, manuals, and tools. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Hesai's public developer resources.

providers.name: Modular Robotics
providers.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot. The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

providers.name: True Anomaly
providers.description: True Anomaly is a defense-technology company building spacecraft, software, and payloads for space superiority. Its products include Jackal, a multirole space-superiority platform positioned as a tactical fighter-interceptor for contested orbital environments, and Mosaic, an autonomy software platform that transforms commander intent into autonomous action. The company serves U.S. government and allied defense customers from facilities in Centennial and Colorado Springs, Colorado; Long Beach, California; and Washington, DC. True Anomaly publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its only machine-readable public surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-disclosure contact.

providers.name: Hub
providers.description: Hub (Hub.xyz) is a distributed physical-AI data infrastructure company that creates, annotates, and curates custom real-world datasets — egocentric first-person video, image, video, and audio — used to train AI and robotics models. Data is sourced through a global network of 500,000+ retail contributors and verified small and medium businesses across 150+ countries and 100+ languages. Hub offers both off-the-shelf labeled datasets and bespoke, custom-scoped data collection projects quoted within hours, delivered through a fully managed pipeline that couples automation with human-in-the-loop validation for frontier AI labs and Fortune 500 companies.

providers.name: Phaidra
providers.description: Phaidra builds AI agents for autonomous data center and industrial operations, using reinforcement learning to control cooling, power, and workloads in mission-critical facilities. Its products include Phaidra Prism, an LLM for data center operations that helps technicians identify, prioritize, and resolve infrastructure issues, and Phaidra Factory, self-learning AI agents that continuously monitor and optimize thermal reliability, energy efficiency, and IT capacity to maximize tokens per watt across AI factories. Phaidra is an enterprise vendor with no public API or developer program; this profile captures its public security, compliance, and web posture. Backed by Index Ventures.

providers.name: Xenex Disinfection Services
providers.description: Xenex Disinfection Services is a San Antonio, Texas-based medical technology company founded in 2008 by Johns Hopkins-trained epidemiologists Dr. Mark Stibich and Dr. Julie Stachowiak. Its LightStrike+ pulsed-xenon UV robot is the first FDA-authorized whole-room microbial reduction device, used by hospitals to destroy pathogens like C. difficile on surfaces; the portfolio also includes the LightStrike6 robot, the Deactivate handheld LED unit, and the TrackMate digital cleaning-event tracking system with a client portal at dms.xenex.com. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, but the company does publish an llms.txt company profile on its website.

providers.name: Pointee
providers.description: Pointee is an agentic automation platform for enterprise business process automation, guiding organizations through the full automation journey from discovery to running AI at scale. Its Process Discovery maps how work actually runs to surface automation potential and ROI, Workflow Automation orchestrates people, bots, and AI agents in unified workflows, and Guardian Agents continuously monitor automation to detect quality drops, automate incident response, and prevent cost overruns and security threats. Pointee also offers a dedicated offering to maximize existing RPA investments. The product is operated by Pointee Interactive s.r.o. (Liberec, Czech Republic) and is a portfolio company of Earlybird; customers include KBC, Intel, Deloitte, AXA, Microsoft, and Mutual of Omaha.

providers.name: Ray Browser
providers.description: Ray Browser is an AI-powered web browser that learns a user's interests and browsing habits to personalize their internet experience. It ships a built-in agent that can run web searches and automate tasks, a curated daily Discover feed, and Ray Studio for building custom tools and dashboards without writing code. The product is currently in public beta with a free Starter plan that grants weekly credits for its AI features. Ray Browser is a consumer product; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: Roby
providers.description: Roby (Imageous, Inc.) is a Seattle-based building-management software company whose HVAC automation product connects room and space calendars with a building's BMS (building management system) to automatically switch HVAC to an unoccupied/energy-saving mode when spaces are not in use, delivering measured energy savings and extended equipment lifetime for K-12, higher-education, and office facilities without added staff effort. Roby is deployed through building system integrators (ATS, Climatec, Syserco, ABM Systems, Oprizon, NSF-E) and also offers Receptionist and Helpdesk workplace applications. The product uses Auth0-managed authentication with token-based, SSL-only API access, but does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ruma Care
providers.description: Ruma Care is a healthcare software company that streamlines the prior authorization process for biologic and infusion medications in infusion clinics. Its AI-powered platform pulls patient and insurance data from electronic health records (EHRs) to identify payer requirements, auto-populates payer-specific prior authorization forms with clinical data, flags missing documentation, and then manages insurer communication and follow-up until an authorization is approved. Built by former infusion clinic staff, Ruma Care consolidates the manual portal, fax, and paper workflows behind buy-and-bill and infusion services into a single platform to reduce denials and accelerate patient access to biologics. Ruma Care is a Y Combinator-backed company. As of this profile the company exposes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Sanctuary AI
providers.description: Sanctuary AI is a Vancouver, British Columbia humanoid robotics company on a mission to create and deploy industrial-grade general-purpose humanoid robots to help address growing labor challenges. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for dull, dirty, and dangerous work in automotive, manufacturing, and logistics environments. Phoenix is driven by Carbon, Sanctuary AI's proprietary AI control system that mimics human cognitive subsystems — memory, sight, sound, and touch — to translate natural-language tasks into dexterous physical actions. The company is vertically integrated, designing everything from motors and actuators through to generative AI algorithms in-house. Co-founded by James Wells (CEO) and Olivia Norton (CTO/CPO), Sanctuary AI has a private GitHub organization with no public repositories, no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, and no published OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications. The commercial model is hardware sales and enterprise deployments; Carbon is a proprietary on-board system and there is no public developer surface.

providers.name: AI Build
providers.description: AI Build (Aibuild) is a London and Silicon Valley based software company, founded in 2015, that is transforming additive manufacturing with agentic AI. Its flagship Aibuild OS is an autonomous engineering platform whose computer-use AI operates CAD, CAE, and CAM software the way a human engineer would, carrying work from design intent through to manufacturing-ready output. Aibuild CAM provides toolpathing for large-format and robotic 3D printing, CNC machining, mould design, and analysis, while Aibuild FETS delivers finite element thermomechanical simulation. The company is a portfolio company of Seedcamp and SuperSeed and appears in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Applied Intuition
providers.description: Applied Intuition builds physical AI software and simulation infrastructure for autonomous systems across automotive, defense, trucking, mining, construction, and agriculture. Its end-to-end stack spans a Self-Driving System (SDS), a Vehicle OS, and tools for vehicle intelligence, letting teams develop, simulate, test, validate, and deploy autonomy at scale. Applied Intuition sells enterprise autonomy software to OEMs and defense programs; it does not publish a public developer REST/GraphQL API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures the company identity plus its public web, security, and open-source surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Care GP
providers.description: Care GP is a Sydney-based healthcare technology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building a suite of AI agents that automate the administrative and operational work of Australian general practice clinics. Its products include Samantha (medical document allocation that files inbound emails, faxes, and scans), Veronica (24/7 inbound and outbound phone and booking management), and a Billing beta for billing and debt-collection automation. Care GP states it is ISO 27001 certified with onshore Australian data storage, multi-factor authentication, and encryption, and reports serving 400+ clinic operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a customer web application (agent.caregp.com.au) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Lila Sciences
providers.description: Lila Sciences is an AI company founded in 2023 that is building what it calls Scientific Superintelligence: an autonomous system that runs the scientific method end to end by generating hypotheses, designing experiments, executing them in physical AI Science Factories (autonomous robotic laboratory networks), and learning from the resulting experimental data. Rather than training on internet text, Lila trains a scientific reasoning model on experimental data, coupling it to scalable verifiers and instruments such as molecular dynamics simulators, protein structure predictors, quantum chemistry solvers, and gene editors, then optimizing the policy with reinforcement learning. The company packages this as two commercial offerings: Catalyst, positioned as an operating system for science that accelerates an organization's existing research, and Creation, a partnership model for generating new discoveries, launching products, and founding new companies. Lila works across therapeutics (mRNA, proteins, antibodies, cell therapies, small molecules), advanced materials, chemicals, energy and environment, oil and gas, aerospace and defense, and biotech. It has raised roughly $550M ($200M seed announced March 2025 and a $350M Series A closed in October 2025) from investors including General Catalyst and NVIDIA, at a reported valuation above $1.3B, and collaborates with NVIDIA on the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit. Lila operates from Cambridge MA, San Francisco CA, and London UK. As of this profile Lila publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this entry is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Presso
providers.description: Presso is a garment-care automation company (operated by parent LaundrySucks.io Inc.) that builds robotic, AI-driven systems for dry cleaning and laundry businesses. Its flagship AirTouch product is a compact, plug-and-play unit that runs on a standard 110V outlet and combines automatic fabric recognition, built-in non-toxic cleaning formulas, and smart temperature control to deliver same-day wash, fold, and dry cleaning under one roof. Presso positions itself around faster, greener, and gentler garment care without compressors, boilers, or skilled labor. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Presso publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface — it is a hardware/robotics and equipment business, not an API provider.

providers.name: Unitree Robotics
providers.description: Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou, China-based high-performance robot manufacturer founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing. The company is a global pioneer in the commercial quadruped (robot dog) market and has expanded into bipedal humanoid robots. Its product line includes the Go1, Go2, and Go2-W quadrupeds for consumers, education, and research; the industrial-grade B1 and B2 quadrupeds for inspection, patrol, and logistics; the H1 full-size humanoid; the G1 humanoid for research and developer experimentation; the R1 humanoid; and the Z1 robotic arm. Unitree also produces in-house components including the L1/L2 LiDAR, hand-grade actuators, and dexterous hands (Dex1-1). Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

providers.name: Cobalt AI
providers.description: Cobalt AI (formerly Cobalt Robotics) is a San Francisco based physical security automation company whose Cobalt Monitoring Intelligence platform uses AI handlers to investigate security events across access control systems and video feeds, determine root cause, and trigger automated responses so security teams focus on genuine threats instead of alarm triage. Its offerings include the Cobalt Command Center remote monitoring service and an indoor autonomous security robot, with integrations spanning LenelS2, Genetec, Avigilon, Brivo, Eagle Eye Networks, Milestone, Okta, ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Slack. The company was founded in 2016, backed early by Bloomberg Beta and Sequoia, and acquired in 2024 by Dean Drako, who rebranded it to Cobalt AI.

providers.name: General Intuition
providers.description: General Intuition is a frontier AI lab, founded in 2025 and spun out of Medal, building spatial-temporal world and action models that learn to perceive, anticipate, and act in space and time. Rather than training primarily on the archive of human language, its systems learn from gameplay data, teaching machines to play, dream within compressed simulacra of reality, and improvise within the unfolding dynamics of the world. The company is developing a commercial API for gaming, simulation, and robotics partners, with broader access planned through 2026. General Intuition is backed by Khosla Ventures, which led both its $133.7M seed round (October 2025) and its $320M Series A at a $2.3B valuation (2026).

providers.name: Kodiak Robotics
providers.description: Kodiak Robotics, which now operates publicly as Kodiak AI, is an autonomous vehicle company founded in April 2018 by CEO Don Burnette and headquartered in California with a Texas operations center. Its flagship product is the Kodiak Driver, an AI-driven autonomy system that pairs onboard artificial intelligence with modular, swappable sensor hardware and offboard services so that a single driverless stack can be carried across different vehicle platforms. The company sells into three markets — long-haul trucking, defense, and industrial ground transportation — and positions driverless operation as a safety improvement, citing that more than 85% of U.S. truck crashes are caused by human error. Kodiak reports more than 2.6 million autonomous miles driven and over 7,000 loads delivered. Kodiak publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs; enrichment probes of kodiak.ai found no /.well-known/ discovery documents and no api/docs/developer subdomains. It does publish an llms.txt, an RSS news feed, and a corporate safety report, so this profile is maintained as a company record rather than an API producer profile.

providers.name: Numos
providers.description: Numos is an AI agent platform that automates accounting and financial planning & analysis (FP&A) workflows for finance teams. It layers above existing ERPs with "zero disruption to your current architecture" and learns a company's accounting policies and entity structures to run strategic FP&A and variance analysis, continuous month-end close, accounts payable orchestration, and accounts receivable / revenue recognition. Numos is headquartered in San Mateo, California and is backed by General Catalyst. Its product is delivered as a hosted web application (app.numosai.com); the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced from the General Catalyst portfolio and enriched from Numos's public web surface.

providers.name: TRIDITIVE
providers.description: TRIDITIVE is an automated additive manufacturing company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Meres, Asturias, Spain, with offices in Hartford, Connecticut and London. It builds the AMCELL family of automated industrial 3D printing machines (Amcell 1300, 4300, 8300, Bulkam), the Traced traceability system, and the EVAM Software platform for additive manufacturing workflow management, digital warehousing, and on-demand production of polymer and metal parts. A Techstars portfolio company, TRIDITIVE publishes no public API, developer portal, or client SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Udacity
providers.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

providers.name: World Golf Tour
providers.description: World Golf Tour (WGT Golf), operated by World Golf Tour, LLC out of San Francisco, is a free-to-play online golf simulation launched in 2008 that recreates more than twenty real championship courses like Pebble Beach, St Andrews, and Bethpage Black using photorealistic imagery, played by over 15 million players on web, iOS, and Android, with virtual equipment from Callaway, Titleist, and TaylorMade and integrations with SkyTrak launch monitors. The company is a Battery Ventures portfolio company and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Cenos
providers.description: CENOS is an engineering simulation software company founded in 2017 in Riga, Latvia, that packages academically proven open-source solvers (Salome, GetDP, and Elmer FEM) into focused, affordable desktop applications for practical engineers. Its products cover electromagnetic and thermal simulation use cases including induction heating, radio-frequency antenna design, wireless charging, electromagnetic stirring of liquid metals, and busbar heating, promising faster product development and lower cost than traditional CAE suites. CENOS is a subscription desktop product with CAD import, one-click PDF reports, and live expert support; it does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform. Backed by 500 Global, Startup Wise Guys, and Capitalia.

providers.name: Dusty Robotics
providers.description: Dusty Robotics is a construction-technology company building automated layout robotics for the building trades. Its flagship product, the FieldPrinter, is a mobile robot that prints digital BIM models and design drawings directly onto the jobsite floor at full scale, laying out walls, penetrations, and other design intent so field teams build to plan with far less manual measurement and rework. The FieldPrinter platform ingests drawings from tools like Autodesk Revit and AutoCAD via native plugins, translating the digital model into precise physical markings on the deck. Dusty Robotics is headquartered in Mountain View, California and is backed by investors including Canaan Partners. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its published surfaces are the product site, a partner program, a support center, and the Dusty Academy training resource.

providers.name: Instruct
providers.description: Instruct ("AI that works for you") is an AI automation platform that lets non-technical users delegate repetitive work across their connected applications. Users describe a task in natural language and Instruct's AI pulls context from one integrated app, acts on it in another, and can turn any successful one-off task into a recurring scheduled workflow, spanning use cases across education, recruiting, sales, and operations. It is a hosted end-user application with a free plan and Google/email sign-up. As of this profile Instruct does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. Instruct is backed by Creandum.

providers.name: Kingsware
providers.description: Kingsware (Zhuhai Kingsware Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd. / 珠海金智维人工智能股份有限公司) is a leading Chinese enterprise AI and RPA solutions provider that builds "AI digital employees" and enterprise-grade agent platforms by fusing large language models, AI algorithms, and robotic process automation with vertical industry workflows. Its core products are the K-APA intelligent process automation (RPA) platform and the Ki-Agent enterprise agent platform (built around a "Supervised Agent" model with task planning, tool calling, multi-agent collaboration, and result verification), exposed through the Kingsware AI Open Platform (ai.kingsware.cn). The company serves finance, government, manufacturing, energy, telecom, education, HR, and finance/operations use cases; it has been recognized by IDC as the number-one China RPA+AI solution vendor by market share, counts all six major state-owned banks and 1,300+ enterprise/government customers, has deployed over 1.8 million AI digital employees, and is a national-level "little giant" (专精特新) enterprise. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Overview
providers.description: Overview (overview.ai) builds AI-powered machine vision systems for manufacturing quality control. Its edge-computing platform runs vision transformer models directly on smart cameras with on-device NVIDIA GPUs to perform automated defect detection, assembly verification, and real-time inspection without cloud dependency. Overview serves connector, semiconductor, packaging, automotive, pharmaceutical, aerospace, renewable energy, food, and textile manufacturers, and integrates with factory-floor systems (PLCs, ERPs, SCADA) over MQTT and digital I/O rather than a public REST API. Backed by GV and Homebrew. Profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pallet
providers.description: Pallet builds an AI-powered logistics workforce: autonomous AI agents that automate supply chain operations for freight brokerages, freight forwarders, FTL and LTL carriers, warehouses, and shippers. Its agents handle end-to-end workflows from quoting through order entry, track-and-trace, billing, and customer service, integrating with existing TMS, WMS, email, and legacy applications. The Atlas product surfaces revenue opportunities across freight operations. Pallet is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Robco
providers.description: RobCo is a Munich- and Austin-based industrial robotics company building software-defined, modular robotic automation delivered as Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) with zero upfront capital expenditure. Its modular robot arms (up to 8 axes, 40 kg payload, 2.5 m reach, 0.1 mm repeatability), the Alfie autonomous robot, the RobFlow no-code programming platform, RobCo Studio configuration and simulation tooling, and the RobVision AI vision system let manufacturers automate machine tending, palletizing, materials handling, and finishing tasks. RobCo serves manufacturing, food and beverage, logistics, automotive, wood, and defense customers, and is backed by Lightspeed, Sequoia Capital, Lingotto, Kindred Capital, and Promus Ventures.

providers.name: Sunday Robotics
providers.description: Sunday Robotics is a consumer robotics company building Memo, an autonomous home robot that handles household chores such as clearing dishes, loading the dishwasher, pulling espresso shots, and folding laundry. The robot is trained on human demonstrations captured with the company's proprietary Skill Capture Glove and runs on the ACT family of robot foundation models. Founded as a physical-AI company and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Sunday is pre-launch with a beta program opening in late 2026. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this record captures its public web and security surface only.

providers.name: swivl
providers.description: swivl is an AI automation platform built specifically for the self-storage industry. It combines a unified CRM and contact center that consolidates calls, texts, emails, and chats with AI agents for sales, billing, support, and review management, plus a tenant mobile app (Spot) for access codes, payments, and referrals. Its self-storage natural-language model is trained on hundreds of thousands of customer conversations and serves 3,500+ locations. Founded in New York City and backed by Techstars, swivl advertises open APIs and integrations with major self-storage management systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: 1QBit
providers.description: 1QB Information Technologies Inc. (1QBit) is a quantum computing software company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. It builds hardware-agnostic algorithms and software for optimization, simulation, and machine learning that run across quantum, quantum-inspired, and classical high-performance computing hardware, with work spanning computational finance, life sciences and quantum chemistry, materials, and telecommunications. 1QBit has hardware and platform partnerships with D-Wave, Fujitsu, IBM, and Microsoft Azure Quantum, and participates in DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) on automated design tools for utility-scale quantum computation. The company markets a 1Qloud optimization platform whose own marketing page cites Python SDK, gRPC, and REST API interfaces, but as of August 2026 1QBit publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract — the former portal.1qbit.com host no longer resolves and access is arranged through industry partnerships. Its only public developer surface is a small GitHub organization of research code plus two first-party Python libraries on PyPI.

providers.name: Brain Corp
providers.description: Brain Corp builds BrainOS, an autonomy platform that powers commercial service robots for floor care, inventory scanning, and remote site management across retail, warehouses, education, airports, malls, healthcare, and hospitality. The product portfolio includes the BrainOS Sense Suite, Clean Suite, ShelfOptix scanning-as-a-service, RFID localization, and remote site management tools. Brain Corp integrates with OEM partners and operators rather than offering a public developer portal, and does not publish open APIs.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Whill
providers.description: WHILL, Inc. designs and manufactures enhanced personal mobility solutions — electric power chairs and mobility scooters, including the Model C2, Model F, the Modo Breeze ultralight foldable wheelchair, and the Model R three- and four-wheel scooters — and operates an autonomous personal mobility service that has completed over 700,000 rides worldwide across airports and other venues. WHILL was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this writing it is a consumer hardware and mobility-service company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record and will be enriched if WHILL launches a developer program.

providers.name: Amera
providers.description: Amera (Amera Health Solutions) is a Seattle-based, Y Combinator (Fall 2025) healthcare technology company that automates claims processing workflows for health insurance payers, third-party administrators (TPAs), and self-insured employers. Its normalization engine ingests messy claim inputs from any source — EDI, PDFs, paper, fax, and proprietary/non-standard formats — and turns them into adjudication-ready, structured data that plugs into existing claims cores via API, EDI, or SFTP. The platform automates validation, reconciliation, stop-loss reporting, and real-time visibility and analytics, reducing plan administration costs and cutting carrier submission times from weeks to minutes while keeping full audit trails and HIPAA compliance. Founded in 2025 by Louise Tanski and Deep Kapur (both formerly of Rupa Health), Amera already works with payers and plan administrators representing roughly 100,000 members. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Amera does not yet publish a public developer portal or API specification.

providers.name: Berkshire Grey
providers.description: Berkshire Grey is a Bedford, Massachusetts-based AI and robotics company that builds integrated pick-and-place, parcel sortation, trailer-unloading, and shuttle-sortation systems for eCommerce fulfillment, retail replenishment, and parcel logistics operations. Its product portfolio is organized around four flagship robotic systems — Core robotic picking system, Dispatch parcel sorter, Scoop trailer unloader, and Stride shuttle sorter — supported by the BG Flex mobile robotic platform and a centralized operating environment that orchestrates fleets of industrial-grade mobile robots for induct, transport, sort, sequence, and fulfill workflows including buy-online-pickup-in-store, curbside, and store replenishment. The company holds 700+ awarded patents (300+ pending) and has deployed solutions with Global-100 retailers and logistics service providers including Walmart, Target, and FedEx, with FedEx expanding from small-parcel sortation into broader AI robotic package-handling capabilities. Berkshire Grey originally went public via SPAC merger with Revolution Acceleration Acquisition Corp in 2021, then entered into a definitive merger agreement with SoftBank Group in 2023 (approximately $375M / $1.40 per share) and is now operated as a private SoftBank portfolio company. Integration with warehouse-management systems is delivered through a proprietary RESTful API surfaced via professional services and a 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive-maintenance support model; the API, BG-OS platform, and any associated SDKs are not publicly documented, and Berkshire Grey does not operate a public developer portal, downloadable SDK, or open-source release for its robotic operating environment.

providers.name: Fetch Robotics
providers.description: Fetch Robotics is a provider of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for the manufacturing, distribution, and fulfillment industries, enabling customers to optimize warehouse and material-handling workflows through robotic automation. Its Fetch and Freight robots are programmed through a ROS (Robot Operating System) interface — standard ROS topics, services, and actions conforming to ROS Enhancement Proposals (REPs) — rather than an HTTP/REST API, and the first-party client, driver, and simulation libraries are published as open source in the fetchrobotics GitHub organization. Fetch Robotics was acquired by Zebra Technologies in August 2021 for approximately $290M; fetchrobotics.com now redirects to Zebra and the autonomous-mobile-robot product line is being wound down (2025-2026), though the open-source ROS packages remain available.

providers.name: Improbable
providers.description: Improbable (Improbable Worlds Ltd) is a London-based technology company and venture builder. Founded in 2012, it originally built SpatialOS, a distributed simulation and networking platform for large-scale real-time multiplayer games, and later Morpheus / M² (MSquared), a network of interoperable metaverse worlds. Today Improbable operates primarily as a venture builder and capital allocator, partnering with founders to launch and scale companies across AI, Web3 and the metaverse. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its historical developer surface centered on the SpatialOS Platform SDK, Worker SDK and the `spatial` CLI (distributed via NuGet), plus the improbable-eng and spatialos GitHub organizations; the standalone documentation, status and IMS subdomains have since been retired as the company pivoted away from a standalone developer platform.

providers.name: Wisk Aero
providers.description: Wisk Aero is an autonomous, all-electric eVTOL air taxi developer and a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company. Wisk is developing its Generation 6 aircraft, a four-passenger self-flying eVTOL designed to operate under human supervisor oversight from a multi-vehicle supervision center, pursuing certification under three FAA programs: Type Certification, Production Certification, and Operation Certification. Wisk evolved from earlier Kitty Hawk programs and has logged over 1,750 autonomous test flights across five aircraft generations since 2010. Announced launch communities include Houston, Texas and Brisbane, Australia (in support of the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games). In March 2026 Wisk was selected by the White House to help lead the safe U.S. introduction of autonomous air taxi flight. Wisk is hardware- and operations-focused, with no public consumer or developer APIs.

providers.name: Azuqua
providers.description: Azuqua was a Seattle-based integration platform as a service (iPaaS) and no-code workflow-automation company, backed by Insight Partners and Techstars, that let business teams build integrations and automated workflows (FLOs) across SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Slack, Marketo and ServiceNow. Azuqua was acquired by Okta in 2019 and its workflow orchestration engine and connectors were folded into Okta Workflows (part of Okta Lifecycle Management). The standalone product is now end-of-life: azuqua.com serves an acquisition notice and the API is no longer available for purchase. This API Evangelist profile documents the surviving public developer surface (legacy ReadMe docs, changelog, llms.txt) and the product's lifecycle status.

providers.name: Denta
providers.description: Denta is a San Francisco-based dental practice management and automation platform, founded by Jack Beecher (Jack Beecher LLC, dba Denta) and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2026 batch). Positioned as "the dental practice that runs itself," Denta embeds AI into dental organizations to automate back-office operations: it ingests fragmented data from a practice's existing software, provides analytics so dentists can understand their business, and runs in the background to handle administrative work such as insurance payment posting. Its roadmap includes all-in-one native practice management software and an "autonomous dental practice." As of this profile Denta publishes a marketing site, a blog, and login and legal pages, but no public developer portal, API, or OpenAPI surface has been located.

providers.name: Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence
providers.description: Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence is a division of Hexagon AB providing metrology, quality management, and manufacturing intelligence software and hardware. Products include PC-DMIS (CMM measurement software), WORKXPLORE (CAD viewer), SFx (smart factory platform), and HxGN Smart Quality. The division offers APIs and SDKs for automating CMM measurement programs, integrating quality data into MES and ERP systems, and building custom metrology applications.

providers.name: Luminai
providers.description: Luminai is an AI-powered automation platform for health system operations, marketed as "The AI Platform for Health System Operations." It automates complex, high-volume healthcare back-office workflows including referral intake and processing, provider inbox automation, patient registration, orders and referrals, pharmacy renewals, payor contract management, denial appeals, and underpayment recovery. The company reports over 12 million automations driven, an average 5.3x ROI, and a 48-day average time to value, with enterprise-grade security and flexible deployment options (on-premises, VPC, or fully managed). Luminai is SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR compliant. It is a venture-backed company in the General Catalyst portfolio. Luminai does not publish a public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Polaron
providers.description: Polaron is a London-based AI software company that builds "the intelligence layer for materials science." Its platform applies machine learning to microscopy and image data to automate microstructure analysis, connecting process, structure, and performance so materials engineering teams can characterise, design, and manufacture materials faster and with less uncertainty. The platform centers on three core model families: Segmentation (identifying and measuring microstructural features), Reconstruction (converting 2D micrographs into 3D representations), and Design (optimising microstructural parameters). It is applied across batteries, metals and alloys, composites, ceramics, additive manufacturing, and pharmaceuticals, spanning R&D, quality and qualification, and modelling and simulation workflows. Polaron is backed by Speedinvest and research institutions including Imperial College London, Manchester, Oxford, and Cambridge.

providers.name: RightHand Robotics
providers.description: RightHand Robotics builds autonomous piece-picking robotic systems for order fulfillment. Its RightPick platform combines computer vision, machine learning, and adaptive grasping hardware to pick and place millions of SKUs at cycle times as fast as three seconds across e-commerce, pharmaceutical, apparel, health & beauty, and grocery operations. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and SoftBank Vision Fund. RightHand Robotics does not publish a public web API; integration, deployment, and operator documentation is provided to authorized customers and partners through a login-gated partner portal (rhrdocs.com). The public GitHub organization hosts open-source ROS packages and C control libraries for the earlier ReFlex robotic hand hardware rather than web-API client SDKs.

providers.name: Akkari
providers.description: Akkari is an autonomous customer operations platform that runs the operational work across the entire customer lifecycle — from the first sales call through onboarding, success, and expansion. It captures every commitment, issue, request, and opportunity surfaced across customer channels like Slack, Discord, email, calls, and meetings, then executes the actual work to close each loop: drafting follow-ups, converting bug reports into tickets, scheduling meetings, and flagging expansion signals. Built for AI-native startups by 2x Y Combinator founders (OrderAhead, acquired by Square; and BLADE), Akkari integrates with tools including Slack, Linear, GitHub, Gmail, and PostHog.

providers.name: Bliq
providers.description: Bliq is a Berlin-based premium driverless-car subscription service rolling out across Europe. Instead of owning a car or paying per ride, members subscribe monthly to a private autonomous vehicle that Bliq charges, cleans, insures, maintains, and parks on their behalf. Cars are booked for time windows (hours or days) rather than single trips, every journey is remotely supervised by licensed local operators, and there is no surge pricing. Backed by Speedinvest, Bliq positions itself as "ownership without ownership." The company currently operates a consumer marketing site with early-access and waitlist flows and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Dwelly
providers.description: Dwelly (legal entity PROSPIRE TECHNOLOGIES LTD, also trading as Dwelly Group) is a UK-based, AI-first lettings and property-management company founded in 2023 by Ilya Drozdov (CEO), Dan Lifshits (CPO) and Dmitry Khanukov (CTO). Rather than selling software, Dwelly grows by acquiring independent UK lettings agencies and succession-planning their owners out, then running the acquired books on its own AI-powered operating platform. That platform automates tenant find (self-service enquiry chat, virtual viewings, verified offers), banking-grade tenant screening (KYC, Right to Rent, referencing), Direct Debit rent collection with automatic reconciliation and arrears handling, maintenance and property management workflows with centralised communications, and continuous lettings compliance. Dwelly is backed by General Catalyst, Begin Capital and S16VC. As of this profile Dwelly publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or technical documentation — the platform is operated internally for its own and its acquired agencies' portfolios.

providers.name: Laelaps AI
providers.description: Laelaps AI is a Zurich- and UK-based autonomous security company building what it calls "the brain behind security" — a hardware-agnostic, fail-safe autonomy layer that unifies aerial, ground, and stationary robots together with a site's existing fixed cameras into a single coordinated monitoring force. The platform pairs field foundational models and visual intelligence with multi-agent coordination so that critical infrastructure and commercial and defense sites can be watched continuously, incidents detected and triaged automatically, and robots dispatched to observe and deter without a human operator watching every screen. Founded by Dr. Sophia Belser (CEO), Dr. Maria "Mania" Stamatopoulou (CRO), and Rokas Bendikas (CTO), the company is backed by Speedinvest, Expeditions Fund, Florent Venture Partners, Fund F, ESA BIC Switzerland, and NVIDIA Inception. As of this profile Laelaps AI publishes a three-page corporate website and no public developer surface — no documentation, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts were found.

providers.name: Ontora
providers.description: Ontora is an AI operational-intelligence platform that runs parallel, voice-based AI-agent interviews with every employee to map how work actually gets done across operations, sales, finance, and change management. It synthesizes the roughly 80% of undocumented, tacit process knowledge that lives only in employees' heads into prioritized automation and cost-reduction roadmaps, compressing a discovery effort that traditionally takes a consulting firm months into a matter of hours. Founded in 2026 and backed by Y Combinator, Ontora targets mid-market companies of roughly 200-2,000 employees undergoing AI transformation. As of this profile the company publishes a product and app but no public API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Shred Video
providers.description: Shred Video automates cinematic video and photo production for adventure tourism operators. Using LiDAR, GPS, smart camera technology, and proprietary algorithms, the platform automatically captures, edits, and delivers finished cinematic videos and photos to a customer's phone within seconds of an activity. It serves adventure tour operators such as skydiving centers, bungy jumping and giant swing operators, river rafting outfitters, and paragliding services, with documented clients including Skydive Utah and AJ Hackett locations in Australia and Singapore. Shred Video is a Y Combinator portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a marketing and demo-request website but publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: CMR Surgical
providers.description: CMR Surgical is a British medical-device company headquartered in Cambridge, UK, founded in 2014 (as Cambridge Medical Robotics). It develops Versius, a small, modular and portable robot-assisted surgical system used across urology, general, gynaecological and thoracic surgery, and Versius Plus, its next-generation platform cleared by the US FDA in December 2025. More than 45,000 patients have been treated globally, making Versius one of the most widely used soft-tissue robotic surgery platforms. CMR reached unicorn status in 2019 and raised a $600M Series D at a $3B valuation in 2021, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, GE Healthcare, ABB Technology Ventures and others. Its digital ecosystem (Versius Connect, Versius Team, Versius Clinical Insights) is a login-gated clinical surface; CMR publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs or developer portal.

providers.name: Emancro
providers.description: Emancro is an AI robotics company automating hospital logistics. Its flagship product, EASO, is described as the world's first fully autonomous robot for hospital medication logistics: it streamlines supply distribution, restocks medication dispensing cabinets, and retrieves medications from pharmacy storage to reduce errors and free clinical staff to focus on patient care. The technology combines vision-language-action (VLA) models with geometric planning, and Emancro is piloting EASO with leading U.S. hospitals. The company is backed by Amplify Partners. Emancro is a physical-robotics and healthcare-AI company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Niricson Software
providers.description: Niricson Software Inc. is an infrastructure technology company making concrete infrastructure safer through AI-powered digital condition assessment. Its patented AUTOSPEX platform uses machine learning and multi-sensor data fusion (visual, thermal, and acoustic) to automatically detect, quantify, and track defects such as cracks, spalling, delamination, and alkali-aggregate reaction in dams, spillways, bridges, and airfields. Data is collected with its DRONIC architecture and NCX acoustic drone payload, which simulates the traditional concrete hammer-sounding test to identify subsurface delamination up to eight inches deep. Asset owners and civil engineers access results through the login-gated, web-based AUTOSPEX platform to interact with defect maps and compare surveys over time. Niricson operates across the USA, Canada, Australia, and India, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Noah Medical
providers.description: Noah Medical is a surgical robotics company building the Galaxy System, a robotic-assisted bronchoscopy platform for interventional pulmonology. The system combines advanced imaging, precision targeting, single-use scope technology, and an adaptive workflow to deliver "tool-in-lesion" confidence for diagnosing lung nodules, improving diagnostic yield and workflow efficiency for physicians. Noah Medical is a medical-device manufacturer focused on clinical hardware and does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company backed by Hongshan (HongShan Capital / formerly Sequoia China).

providers.name: REEV
providers.description: REEV is a medical-technology company developing AI-powered wearable robotics for mobility recovery and neurological gait rehabilitation. Its REEV SENSE platform uses smart shoe- and leg-mounted sensors to analyze gait and visualize biomarkers in a mobile app, and its DREEVEN motorized knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO) delivers robotic walking assistance personalized from REEV SENSE gait data. REEV serves outpatient clinics and rehabilitation centers treating stroke, multiple sclerosis, and paraplegia, and is backed by Techstars, NVIDIA Inception, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: Segway-Ninebot
providers.description: Segway-Ninebot is a global personal-transportation and robotics company, formed when Ninebot acquired Segway in 2015. It designs and manufactures electric kickscooters (the world's top-selling e-kickscooter brand, 13M+ units sold across 100+ countries), self-balancing personal transporters, e-bikes, and — through its Robotics division — RMP mobile-robot chassis and delivery/service robots (Nova Carter, NVIDIA Isaac-powered developer kits). Backed by HongShan. Its public developer surface is limited to Segway Robotics' open-source ROS / NVIDIA Isaac integration packages on GitHub; no first-party REST or OpenAPI product API is currently published.

providers.name: Whirl
providers.description: Whirl AI is an enterprise IT platform that uses AI agents to help IT teams understand, enhance, and transform business processes and core systems. It automates research and impact analysis, generates business requirements, epics and user stories, and accelerates configuration and code changes across applications and integrations, compressing enterprise system changes from weeks and months into days and hours. Whirl runs on dedicated single-tenant AWS infrastructure per customer with immutable, versioned, auditable pipelines (no SSH access), FIDO2 device-based access, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. Founded by former Snowflake CIO Sunny Bedi and backed by ICONIQ, with advisors from Okta, Splunk, and VMware.

providers.name: ANYbotics
providers.description: ANYbotics is a Swiss deep-tech robotics company that builds ANYmal, an autonomous four-legged inspection robot used to automate routine and hazardous industrial inspections across power and utilities, oil and gas, mining, chemicals, and metals. Its platform pairs the legged robot with inspection-management software and analytics to increase plant uptime, cut costs, and remove workers from dangerous areas. ANYbotics is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is exposed; this API Evangelist profile currently captures the company's published security and trust posture.

providers.name: Arzana
providers.description: Arzana is an AI-powered Office Execution System for US manufacturers and distributors, founded in 2025 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026). Arzana trains custom models on a factory's historical data and deploys agents that automate back-office work — quoting, estimating, order entry, purchasing, prospecting, outreach, CRM, AP 3-way match, AR tracking, and customer service — alongside a customizable ERP/CRM/MES with every agent pre-installed. Forward-deployed engineers configure each agent per operation; Arzana reports going live in 120 days with 99%+ accuracy. Arzana currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; it does publish a /llms.txt for agent discovery.

providers.name: Hadrian
providers.description: Hadrian (Hadrian Automation) is a Los Angeles-area precision-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power, building software-driven, AI-powered factories that produce high-tolerance machined components for the aerospace and defense industrial base — including parts for rockets, satellites, jets, drones, and missiles. The company's core software stack is Opus, described as a full-stack, AI-powered Factory Autonomy platform that interprets legacy engineering designs, automates CNC machining, inspection, tool-path optimization, adaptive programming, scheduling, and quality assurance, and enables new operators to be productive in 30 days or less. Hadrian operates multiple factories — Factory 2 (F2) and Factory X (FX) in Torrance, California, and Factory 3 (F3) in Mesa, Arizona — and offers three commercial models: precision component manufacturing, Manufacturing-as-a-Service (dedicated automation cells for a single customer), and Factories-as-a-Service (turnkey factory design and operation). Customers and partners include major aerospace and defense primes such as Lockheed Martin. Hadrian has also launched an additive manufacturing division to expand U.S. defense production capacity. The Opus platform is internal-only — Hadrian sells finished precision parts and factory capacity, not software access — and there is no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release for Opus or any Hadrian system.

providers.name: Diligent Robotics
providers.description: Diligent Robotics is an Austin, Texas-based healthcare robotics company founded in 2017 by Andrea Thomaz (CEO) and Vivian Chu (CIO), both trained as roboticists at MIT, Georgia Tech, and the University of Texas at Austin. The company builds Moxi, a socially intelligent mobile manipulator that operates autonomously inside hospitals to handle non-clinical material transport — delivering medications, lab samples, supplies, PPE, and patient items so nurses and clinical staff can focus on patient care. Moxi combines mobile manipulation (grasping, opening doors, riding elevators), social navigation, and human-guided learning, and is deployed 24/7 with minimal facility infrastructure (existing Wi-Fi). Operationally, Moxi has logged 500,000+ deliveries and 100,000+ autonomous elevator rides across customer hospitals including UTMB, Shannon Health, ThedaCare, Carilion Giles Community Hospital, and Medical City Denton. The platform is HIPAA compliant, SOC 2 Type II audited, and TX-RAMP Level 2 certified. Diligent has raised roughly $100M across rounds led by Canaan, True Ventures, Tiger Global, DNX Ventures, Next Coast Ventures, and Northwestern Medicine Innovation. Diligent's revenue model is robot deployment/leasing and enterprise services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Moxi or its underlying robotics stack.

providers.name: Flyzipline
providers.description: Flyzipline (Zipline International Inc., flyzipline.com / zipline.com) designs, manufactures, and operates autonomous delivery drones for food, groceries, and medicine. Its instant logistics platform flies vital shipments — blood products, vaccines, pharmaceuticals, prepared meals, and retail goods — on direct aerial routes at up to 70 mph, with temperature-controlled pods and real-time tracking. Zipline operates distribution centers across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan, partnering with health systems, retailers (Walmart, Chipotle), and restaurant technology providers (Olo) that submit delivery requests through Zipline's ordering system or software integrations. As of early 2026 the fleet has completed more than two million commercial deliveries across 120+ million autonomous miles. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-adjacent portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Zipline publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time — partner integrations are bespoke.

providers.name: Andromeda
providers.description: Andromeda is a robotics company building personalised humanoid robot companions for aged care and assisted living. Its flagship robot, Abi, adapts to each resident's personality, ability, and language to provide social connection, conversation, and engagement that improves resident mood and wellbeing while extending care-team capacity. Founded by Grace Brown and backed by Forerunner Ventures and Paradigm, Andromeda has deployed Abi across aged-care providers in Australia and the United States (partners include mecwacare and Medical & Aged Care Group) and has been featured by the BBC, CNN, Forbes, and ABC Australia. The company currently publishes a public marketing and news site but no developer platform, API, or public technical documentation.

providers.name: ARX Robotics
providers.description: ARX Robotics is a European defense technology company building autonomous unmanned ground systems and the software that runs them. Its flagship Mithra OS is an AI-driven autonomy platform that turns legacy and modern military vehicles into software-defined, autonomous units, while its Gereon RCS line delivers scalable robotic ground vehicles for reconnaissance, firepower, clearance, surveillance, cargo, and casualty evacuation across defense and commercial missions. Headquartered in Munich with offices in Berlin, the UK, and Ukraine, ARX operates one of Europe's largest autonomous defense systems production facilities and has delivered unmanned ground systems to Ukraine. The company is venture-backed (a €31M Series A extended by €11M, with HV Capital among its investors) and partners with RENK, DEUTZ, Helsing, and Quantum Systems to strengthen Europe's technological resilience and defense sovereignty. ARX publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web presence and an llms.txt it publishes for AI agents.

providers.name: Atalanta
providers.description: Atalanta is a mathematical AI company building provably correct decision-making for the world's most important missions. Its flagship platform, Argo, is described as the first software understanding platform - it uses mathematical proof and formal verification to establish safety, security, and performance guarantees for software-defined and autonomous systems at operational speed, moving beyond the limits of traditional testing. Argo identifies failure modes before deployment and verifies compliance with critical constraints across energy (nuclear and grid control systems), space (satellite and communications networks), and defense (complex military systems and data isolation). Atalanta was founded by Anjana Rajan and Jonathan Ring, is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and is backed by Felicis and In-Q-Tel.

providers.name: Avidbots
providers.description: Avidbots is a robotics company that designs and manufactures fully autonomous commercial floor-cleaning robots, including the Neo, Neo 2W, and Kas scrubbers, powered by its proprietary Avidbots Autonomy AI, lidar, and 3D sensing for real-time mapping, dynamic route planning, and intervention-free cleaning. Its robots serve airports, warehouses, retail, manufacturing, education, and healthcare facilities, and are managed through the web-based Avidbots Command Center. Avidbots was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: ECOVACS Robotics
providers.description: ECOVACS Robotics is a global home service robotics company founded in 1998 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, that designs, manufactures, and sells AI-powered autonomous cleaning devices for consumer and commercial use.
