Its product families include DEEBOT robotic vacuum and mopping robots, WINBOT window-cleaning robots, GOAT robotic lawn mowers, ULTRAMARINE pool-cleaning robots, and the DEEBOT PRO commercial line, all managed through the ECOVACS HOME mobile app. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; as of this enrichment pass ECOVACS publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface — this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Field AI
providers.description: FieldAI builds general-purpose robot intelligence through its Field Foundation Models (FFMs) and EDGE brain — a new class of physics-first, risk-aware foundation models for embodied AI. FieldAI's embodiment-agnostic autonomy lets robots navigate dynamic, unstructured environments without maps, GPS, or predefined trajectories, and has been proven across quadrupeds, humanoids, wheeled robots, and passenger-scale vehicles. Founded in 2023 (formerly AI for Humanity) and based in Mission Viejo, California, the company is led by veterans from DeepMind, Google Brain, Tesla Autopilot, NASA JPL, and SpaceX, and serves construction, energy, mining, logistics, manufacturing, power and utility, agriculture, and federal applications. FieldAI has raised over $405M from investors including Bezos Expeditions, Canaan Partners, Khosla Ventures, Temasek, Intel Capital, Hyundai Motor Company, and Prysm Capital.

providers.name: Agile Robots
providers.description: Agile Robots SE is a Munich-based robotics and artificial intelligence company founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics. The company develops force-sensitive industrial and service robots, robotic arms (Diana series), grippers and hands (Agile Hand), mobile robotics, and the AgileCore / AgileAI software platform that lets system integrators and operators build and deploy AI-driven automation for the automotive, consumer electronics, healthcare, and service industries. Headquartered in Munich's Sendling district with manufacturing across Europe, China, and India, Agile Robots reached unicorn valuation in a 2021 Series C and is backed by investors including Hongshan (Sequoia Capital China). This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Agile Robots does not currently publish a public developer portal, REST API, or first-party SDKs.

providers.name: Belts
providers.description: Belts covers the landscape of APIs, data standards, and digital resources related to conveyor belts and industrial belt systems. This topic encompasses conveyor belt monitoring and predictive maintenance APIs, industrial IoT sensor data for belt condition tracking, and the standards bodies that govern belt conveyor design and safety. Key organizations include CEMA (Conveyor Equipment Manufacturers Association) and ANSI, which define design, installation, and safety standards for belt conveyors used in mining, manufacturing, food processing, and bulk material handling industries.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: Ike Robotics (Nuro)
providers.description: Nuro is an autonomous-vehicle technology company that builds the Nuro Driver, an AI-first self-driving system it now licenses to automakers and mobility providers rather than operating its own delivery fleet. Nuro acquired the assets and team of Ike Robotics, an autonomous-trucking startup, folding that self-driving expertise into its Level 4 autonomy platform. The company partners with firms such as Uber and Lucid to deploy robotaxis and other autonomous applications, and pairs the Nuro Driver with the Nuro Toolkit for validation and deployment. Nuro operates a B2B licensing model and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Photoneo
providers.description: Photoneo is a Slovak (Bratislava, founded 2013) machine-vision company and a global pioneer of high-resolution structured-light 3D measurement. Its flagship products are the PhoXi 3D Scanner family and the MotionCam-3D, a parallel structured-light camera that captures moving scenes in real-time 3D, together with AI-enabled software such as Bin Picking Studio, Locator, and Palletizing for robotic automation. Rather than a hosted web/REST API, Photoneo exposes a developer surface through the PhoXi Control software and its official C++, C#, and Python device APIs, GenICam/GigE Vision standard connectivity, TCP/IP robot interfaces (UR, ABB, FANUC, Staubli, Mitsubishi, Kawasaki, Yaskawa), and a set of BSD-licensed example repositories on GitHub. Documentation lives in the Photoneo Knowledge Base (docs.photoneo.com) and the 3D scanning wiki. Photoneo (now part of the Brightpick Group) was acquired by Zebra Technologies.

providers.name: Rabbit
providers.description: Rabbit Inc. is a consumer technology company building AI-powered devices, best known for the Rabbit R1, a $199 handheld AI companion with industrial design by Teenage Engineering. The R1 runs rabbitOS and centers on a Large Action Model (LAM) that automates tasks across operating systems and applications (DLAM), alongside features like the Magic Camera, voice recording with transcription, and vibe-coded "creations." Rabbit is a portfolio company of a16z. As of this profile, Rabbit is a consumer hardware and device company with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its public surface is a marketing site, support center, blog, and newsroom.

providers.name: TurbineOne
providers.description: TurbineOne builds a frontline AI/ML platform that turns raw sensor data into real-time detection, classification, and targeting at the edge for defense and national-security missions. Its product suite spans Frontline Perception (edge computer vision on live sensor feeds), Frontline Command, Frontline Autonomy, a Model Hub for managing and deploying ML models, and EdgeWorks, a program that brings warfighters, mission teams, and engineers together to develop and validate mission capabilities for contested, disconnected environments. The company was founded on expertise in artificial intelligence, mesh networking, and sensing technology, and positions its work as "Responsible AI for our nation's heroes." It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. TurbineOne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, GitHub organization, and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Verdant Robotics
providers.description: Verdant Robotics is an agricultural robotics company building precision farming systems for specialty crop growers. Its flagship SharpShooter uses "Aim & Apply" technology - machine learning and computer vision that identify crops and weeds in real time, build a three-dimensional map of the field, and deliver microliter-precise applications directly onto weeds without contacting the crop, doing over 240 targeted applications per second. The Robotics-as-a- Service platform reduces herbicide use by up to 99% and manual labor costs by up to 85% across carrots, leafy greens, cabbage, onions, and grass seed and sod production. Founded by leaders from the self-driving vehicle industry and commercial agriculture, Verdant is backed by DCVC. This profile was surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company; Verdant publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation - its GitHub organization hosts robotics tooling and forks (cbuf message serialization, Jetson build scripts, YOLO/ultralytics forks) rather than a product API.

providers.name: Lightberry
providers.description: Lightberry is a San Francisco robotics software company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) that builds conversational AI "personality" software for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its platform lets a robot listen, speak, see its surroundings, and act on natural-language instruction without the owner writing any code, emphasizing emotional intelligence, contextual awareness, and autonomy rather than a simple speech-to-text voice pipeline. Lightberry ships pre-installed on robots sold through its partnership with Unitree, and the company runs a manufacturer-compatibility program with robot makers including Fourier, Booster Robotics, and High Torque. Its published documentation today covers device setup (power-on, WiFi provisioning, starting a conversation) plus an MCP architecture note describing a Model Context Protocol server that routes tool calls to individual Lightberry devices, which each expose a REST endpoint. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: Town
providers.description: Town is a personal AI assistant that works across email, calendar, Slack, docs, WhatsApp, and the web. Users connect their accounts and Town — through a personal agent called a "Townie" — learns how they work, then suggests and runs automated "routines" (meeting briefs, email drafting, follow-ups, scheduling) on their behalf. Founded by Jean-Denis Greze (former Plaid CTO) and Tony Vincent (former Google product/AI lead), Town raised a $55M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (June 2026) with Forerunner Ventures, First Round, Alt Capital, and Conviction participating. Town publishes no public developer program: the product is fully auth-gated, api.town.com is a Convex backend deployment rather than a public API, and its robots.txt carries explicit Content-Signal declarations restricting AI training on its content.

providers.name: TreeX Robotics
providers.description: TreeX Robotics is an Israeli physical-AI company founded in 2024 that is bringing autonomous robotics to outdoor field operations at scale. TreeX replaces human field crews with fleets of physical AI-powered autonomous workers that perform high-skill field operations as an on-demand labor service, regardless of terrain or ground conditions. The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (seed, 2024) and operates in Israel, the United States, and Italy. TreeX publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: 1X Technologies
providers.description: 1X Technologies (formerly Halodi Robotics) is a Norwegian-American humanoid robotics company building general-purpose bipedal robots designed to live and work alongside people. Founded in 2014 in Norway by Bernt Øyvind Børnich, the company is now headquartered in Palo Alto, California with R&D and manufacturing presence in Moss, Norway and a new vertically integrated NEO factory in Hayward, California. 1X is backed by the OpenAI Startup Fund, EQT Ventures, Tiger Global, Samsung NEXT, and others through Series A2 ($23.5M, 2023), Series B ($100M, 2024), and a $1B raise reported in 2025. Its commercial robots are EVE — a wheeled upper-humanoid deployed in industrial and security settings since 2022 — and NEO, a bipedal home humanoid that began pre-orders October 28, 2025 at $20,000 (or $499/month) with consumer deliveries in 2026. 1X also acquired Kind Humanoid (Jan 2025) and announced a partnership to deploy up to 10,000 NEO robots into EQT portfolio company factories and warehouses between 2026 and 2030. Unlike most humanoid robotics vendors, 1X publishes meaningful open-source artifacts: the EVE ROS2 API (custom WholeBodyTrajectory and DrivingCommand message types) and the halodi-messages package on GitHub under Apache-2.0, plus the 1X World Model Challenge with 100+ hours of vector-quantized EVE observations and GENIE baseline models released on Hugging Face. There is no public REST/HTTP developer API or hosted developer portal — the developer surface is ROS2 messages, robot models in URDF, and the world-model dataset/model artifacts.

providers.name: Bedrock
providers.description: Bedrock (Bedrock Ocean Exploration) builds advanced autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and Mosaic, a cloud-native data platform that transforms how the world maps, monitors, and understands the seafloor. Its AUV fleet carries multibeam echosounder, side-scan sonar, magnetometer, and sub-bottom profiler payloads to deliver high-resolution geophysical survey data for offshore energy (wind, oil and gas, renewables), ports and harbors, submarine telecom infrastructure, defense, and scientific research. A Northzone portfolio company, Bedrock is an enterprise ocean-data provider; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Cyclone Robotics
providers.description: Cyclone Robotics is an enterprise Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and hyperautomation platform provider serving large organizations across Asia. Its product suite spans RPA Studio, RPA Robot and RPA Controller for building and orchestrating software robots; AI capabilities including AI Skill Studio, Task Intelligence, Process Intelligence, Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) and chatbots; and delivery options such as Robot-as-a-Service and RPA Mobile. The platform lets business and technical users automate finance, government, manufacturing, banking, insurance, logistics, healthcare and customer-service processes, and can expose robot business functions as callable services (RaaS) for third-party integration. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kinetic
providers.description: Kinetic (Kinetic Automation) builds robotics-based automated collision repair for modern vehicles equipped with advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). The company operates robotic repair facilities (Kinetic Hubs), automated imaging for collision damage assessment and repair estimates (Kinetic Vision), and AI-powered calibration identification software (Kinetic ID) that determines which ADAS sensors need recalibration after a repair. Backed by Menlo Ventures and Techstars, Kinetic was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and corporate site plus a login-only identity portal (id.kinetic.auto); it exposes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or webhooks surface.

providers.name: Dronamics
providers.description: Dronamics is a European deep-tech company that designs, builds, and operates autonomous long-range cargo drones for middle-mile logistics. Its flagship aircraft, The Black Swan, is a remotely piloted UAV that carries up to 350 kg (770 lb) of cargo over distances up to 2,500 km (1,550 mi), enabling same-day, cross-border, point-to-point deliveries that are faster, cheaper, and lower in CO2 emissions than traditional air freight. Founded in 2014 in Sofia, Bulgaria by brothers Svilen and Konstantin Rangelov and operating as Dronamics Group Limited, the company is building the world's first cargo drone airline, operating a proprietary drone fleet from a network of low-cost droneports. The public dronamics.com marketing site is built on Wix and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access; Dronamics does not publish a developer-facing logistics API, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: ThayerMahan
providers.description: ThayerMahan, Inc. is a U.S. maritime autonomy and ocean-intelligence company headquartered in Groton, Connecticut, founded in 2016 and led by former U.S. Navy Vice Admiral Michael Connor. It builds and operates uncrewed surface and subsurface sensing systems — Outpost, SeaPicket, SeaGuard (a non-kinetic counter-UUV defeat system) and the TransparenSea data platform — combining passive acoustic arrays, electronic sensors, edge processing, AI classification and human analysts to deliver persistent undersea surveillance, port and critical-infrastructure security, subsea infrastructure monitoring, passive acoustic marine-mammal monitoring and illegal-fishing (IUU) detection for defense, government and commercial offshore customers. ThayerMahan sells outcomes as a service rather than developer tooling: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable contract. The only public reference to programmatic access is on the TransparenSea page, which states that contact reports are delivered by application programming interface (API), voice report, or other means in near real-time — a customer-delivery integration negotiated per engagement, not a self-serve public API. Its GitHub organization holds two forks of third-party tools and no first-party libraries.

providers.name: Belden
providers.description: Belden Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets networking, connectivity, and cable products and solutions for industrial automation, smart buildings, and broadcast markets. The company delivers end-to-end signal transmission solutions for mission-critical applications, including industrial Ethernet infrastructure, cybersecurity, and IIoT connectivity. Belden's Hirschmann brand is a leading provider of industrial network switches and management software with CLI, SNMP, and REST API interfaces for network device management.

providers.name: Boson Motors
providers.description: Boson Motors is an electric vehicle and robotics company founded in 2017, building a modular electric off-road utility vehicle (UTV) platform for agriculture, farm automation, and work applications. Its flagship LX40 is a user-serviceable, low-maintenance electric 4WD UTV that charges from a standard 110v outlet and accepts interchangeable work modules for spraying, hauling, and crew transport. The company operates engineering and production out of Tada, Andhra Pradesh, India, with a strategic base in Fremont, California, and maintains a robotics arm (Boson Robotics) focused on autonomous and agricultural automation. Boson Motors is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes a consumer marketing and reservation site with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer documentation; its public engineering footprint is a GitHub organization of ROS/robotics libraries. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead and enrichment target.

providers.name: BRINC
providers.description: BRINC builds a connected ecosystem of drones, software, and services purpose-built for public safety in the United States. Its Drone as First Responder (DFR) systems — the Guardian and Responder outdoor drones, the Lemur 2 indoor tactical drone, and the throwable BRINC Ball — pair with LiveOps teleoperations software (livestreaming, two-way comms, evidence management) to put a camera overhead within seconds of a 911 call. BRINC reports deployments across 900+ public safety agencies in all 50 states, sub-70-second average drone arrival times, and a recent $125M funding round. The company also runs its Safeguard upgrade-and-repair program and grant/DFR playbook services. BRINC exposes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface as of this profile; this entry is enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Careforce
providers.description: Careforce (Helpcare AI, Inc., d/b/a Careforce) provides an autonomous AI workforce platform for healthcare operations. Its AI agents — Angelica, a care coordinator handling preventive-care outreach, appointment scheduling, reminders, and referral management, and David, a data analyst that pulls and analyzes patient data across EHR and portal systems — integrate with 30+ healthcare platforms including Epic, Cerner, Athenahealth, and NextGen to close care gaps and reduce staff workload. Backed by CRV. Careforce consumes third-party healthcare APIs rather than publishing a public developer API; no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Cellares
providers.description: Cellares is an Integrated Development and Manufacturing Organization (IDMO) for cell therapies, operating a global network of automated "Smart Factories." Its FDA-recognized Cell Shuttle platform delivers high-throughput, end-to-end, cGMP industrial-scale cell therapy manufacturing, and its Cell Q platform automates quality-control testing of cell therapy products. Smart Factories operate in South San Francisco (CA), Bridgewater (NJ), Leiden (Netherlands), and Kashiwa (Japan). Cellares was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as a cell therapy manufacturing organization it publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: COMSOL
providers.description: COMSOL is a Swedish-American engineering software company best known for COMSOL Multiphysics, a desktop platform for physics-based simulation. The platform exposes a unified COMSOL API that powers the GUI, the Application Builder (Java-based Method Editor), LiveLink for MATLAB, LiveLink for Excel, and the LiveLink family of CAD/CAE interfacing products (SOLIDWORKS, Inventor, AutoCAD, Revit, Solid Edge, CATIA V5, MATLAB, Simulink, Excel). COMSOL is primarily licensed desktop software with web deployment via COMSOL Server and standalone applications via COMSOL Compiler. There is no public web REST API and no public GitHub SDK organization; programmatic surfaces are the Java API, the MATLAB LiveLink interface, and the module-specific LiveLink integrations bundled with the licensed product.

providers.name: Geopipe
providers.description: Geopipe uses AI and machine learning to build game-ready digital twins of real-world cities and environments. It ingests raw sensor data (imagery and laser scans) and reconstructs regions as semantically-modeled, multi-level-of- detail 3D models that developers stream or download into games, simulations, training, architecture, and metaverse applications without any manual 3D modeling. Delivery is through Cesium 3D Tiles streaming for Unity and Unreal Engine, downloadable 3D meshes in common file formats, ready-to-use Unity Asset Store packs, and a first-party Unity SDK, backed by an open-source geospatial and 3D-tiles toolchain on GitHub. Founded in New York City by Christopher Mitchell and Thomas Dickerson and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Jarmin
providers.description: Jarmin is a Y Combinator-backed company building autonomous "AI employees" for technical and operational roles — ML engineers, financial analysts, account executives, compliance analysts, data analysts, project managers, and paralegals. Rather than a single chatbot, Jarmin operates a system of proprietary agents, models, and automations that learn a role's responsibilities, connect to a company's internal systems and data sources, experiment with approaches, and run end-to-end workflows autonomously (with optional human approval at key decision points). For ML work this spans domain-specific feature engineering, model selection under constraints, hyperparameter optimization, and deploying production pipelines. Founded by engineers from Meta, Apple, AWS, Lockheed Martin, and JPMorgan Chase, Jarmin targets investment banking, fintech, and legal verticals. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead; at enrichment time Jarmin publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Mendaera
providers.description: Mendaera is a healthcare robotics company building the Focalist handheld robotic system, which combines robotics, real-time ultrasound imaging, and software to guide needle-based medical procedures with greater precision and consistency. The FDA-cleared platform is preparing for broad commercial launch in 2026. Mendaera is backed by Lux Capital, Threshold Ventures, Founders Fund, PFM Health Sciences, and Puma Venture Capital. The company is focused on medical devices rather than a developer-facing platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Haber
providers.description: Haber (Elixa Technologies Private Limited), headquartered in Pune, India with a US presence in Chicago, is an industrial AI company delivering AI-led automation for smart manufacturing across heavy industries including pulp, paper, packaging and tissue, metals and mining, food and beverages, oil and gas, and water/utility institutions. Its product suite spans eLIXA, an IIoT-powered process intelligence platform; Mt. Fuji for historical data storage, visualizations, digital twins and predictive interventions; Kaiznn, an optimization engine for trim-loss reduction, inventory and production scheduling; plus Kensei and FiMorph. The platform emphasizes real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and enterprise-grade security (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Slintel
providers.description: Slintel is a B2B sales and market intelligence platform that mines buyer and technographic signals — company firmographics, technology installs, psychographics, and buying-intent scores — to help revenue teams prioritize accounts and time outreach. Founded in 2016 and backed by Accel and Sequoia, Slintel was acquired by 6sense in 2021 and its data and API services are now consolidated into the 6sense Revenue AI platform. Slintel's programmatic surface (company identification, firmographics, lead scoring, and enrichment) is delivered through the 6sense API Portal rather than a standalone Slintel developer portal; this profile reflects that consolidation and captures the surviving public developer surface.

providers.name: Aaru
providers.description: Aaru is an AI synthetic-research and prediction company based in New York City, founded in 2024 by Cam Fink, Ned Koh, and John Kessler. Aaru builds multi-agent simulation software that generates thousands of AI agents from public and proprietary behavioral data to model how individuals, groups, and entire populations will respond to future events, products, policies, and messaging. Its platform (marketed as Lumen) replaces traditional survey-based market research and polling with measurable-outcome simulation, covering price-sensitivity analysis, voter-behavior prediction, and disaster-communication testing. Customers include Accenture, EY, Interpublic Group, and political campaigns; the company raised a Series A at a roughly $1B headline valuation in December 2025, with backing from General Catalyst, Redpoint Ventures, Felicis, Abstract Ventures, and others. Aaru currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Arc Simulations
providers.description: Arc Simulations is a London-based sports technology company, founded in 2022 by Henry Smith and Michael Armenakis and part of the Techstars London Spring 2024 accelerator cohort. Arc builds ball-tracking and simulation technology for cricket and other ball sports: professional-standard cricket balls carry embedded tracking tags that transmit position data to sensors up to 200 times per second, feeding a real-time simulation and analytics platform. The system predicts ball trajectory post-impact from velocity, angle and spin to deliver millimetre-accurate, autonomous feedback for every shot, with customisable field configurations that mirror live match scenarios. Arc serves players, coaches, scouts, analysts, broadcasters and fans through a hosted application (app.arcsim.io) and a player-facing app (player.arcsim.io) offering ball-by-ball 3D simulations. Arc's technology is built first for cricket but is designed to track nearly any sports ball. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity and web/security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Finch Legal
providers.description: Finch Legal (Finch) is an AI-powered pre-litigation platform built for personal injury law firms, combining US-based expert legal operators with AI agents to run cases on autopilot from intake through demand. Its services span 24/7 bilingual intake and client sign-up, insurance claim and police-report retrieval, treatment tracking with client check-ins, and expert-reviewed demand-letter generation, with beta capabilities for medical chronologies and litigation support. Finch writes updates directly into a firm's existing case-management system rather than adding a new tool, integrating with Filevine, Smokeball, Litify, Neos, SmartAdvocate, MyCase, Clio, Casepeer, and Cloudlex. The company is SOC 2 certified, headquartered in New York City, and backed by venture investors. Finch exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK at this time; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Agtonomy
providers.description: Agtonomy is a physical-AI and automation software company, founded in 2021 by growers and technologists, that embeds machine vision, connectivity, and AI directly into agricultural and off-road equipment from manufacturers such as Bobcat, Kubota, and Clemens. Its platform combines GPS guidance, computer vision, and fleet intelligence so a single operator can plan, remotely monitor, and review autonomous tasks like mowing, hauling, spraying, and cultivation across 10+ tractors at once. The TeleFarmer product controls these field missions through an intuitive app, helping growers address labor shortages and rising operational costs. Backed by investors including GV and Allison Transmission, Agtonomy operates primarily across the western United States with expansion into the Southeast US and Australia. This profile was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agtonomy publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Arx Robotics
providers.description: ARX Robotics is a German defense-technology company building autonomous mobile robots and a software-defined digitalization platform for European armed forces and commercial operators. Its product line includes Gereon, a small tracked reconnaissance and casualty-evacuation robot; Hector, a larger autonomous all-terrain ground vehicle for scalable land operations; and Mithra OS, a digitalization platform that modernizes legacy vehicle fleets through software integration. ARX positions itself around strengthening Europe's technological resilience and sovereignty with mission-ready, software-defined unmanned ground systems. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Bedrock Robotics
providers.description: Bedrock Robotics develops advanced autonomy for the built world, retrofitting existing heavy construction machinery with an autonomous kit the company calls the Bedrock Operator. The system adds machine intelligence to equipment such as excavators and dozers so jobsites can run around the clock with reduced human intervention, compressing project timelines, improving safety by removing operators from hazardous work, and enabling remote progress tracking. Backed by 8vc and Emergence Capital, the company raised a $270M Series B. Bedrock is a robotics and physical-autonomy company; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time. This profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network and captures its public web and security posture.

providers.name: Blue Water Autonomy
providers.description: Blue Water Autonomy is a Boston-based defense technology company building autonomous warships for open-ocean operations, with the goal of revitalizing U.S. shipbuilding through scalable, reliable, uncrewed naval vessels. Founded in 2025 by Rylan Hamilton (ex-U.S. Navy officer and founder of 6 River Systems), Scott N. Miller (ocean engineer and early iRobot engineer), and Austin Gray (former Navy intelligence officer), the company unveiled its 190-foot Liberty Class autonomous ship platform for the U.S. Navy in February 2026. Backed by a $50M Series A led by GV, Blue Water Autonomy operates from offices in Boston MA, Washington DC, Morgan City LA, and San Diego CA. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Bluewhite (fka Blue White Robotics)
providers.description: Bluewhite (formerly Blue White Robotics) is an autonomy company that builds an AI-powered "Field Intelligence" physical-AI engine for operating vehicles in demanding, unstructured, real-world environments. Founded in Israel, the company first commercialized autonomous agriculture — retrofitting existing tractor fleets with an aftermarket autonomy kit for driverless spraying, mowing, and other field operations — and has since extended the same edge-processing autonomy stack to defense and security missions through OEM integrations and complete unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). Bluewhite is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. The company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation; this API Evangelist profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Chemify
providers.description: Chemify is a Glasgow-based programmable-chemistry company, spun out of the University of Glasgow in 2022 by chemist Lee Cronin, that digitizes the creation of molecules through what it calls "Chemputation." The platform fuses AI/ML-driven molecular design, a universal chemical programming language, and robotic synthesis so pharmaceutical, biotech, and industrial partners can move from a novel concept to a makeable compound end to end. In 2025 Chemify opened its first Chemifarm, a fully automated chemistry facility in Glasgow's Maryhill district that pairs its molecular-design engine with industrial-scale robotic synthesis, and closed a $50M Series B co-led by Wing Venture Capital and Insight Partners, with backing from DCVC. Chemify does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; engagement runs through its partner program.

providers.name: Chemify Limited
providers.description: Chemify Limited is a chemistry-automation company founded in 2022 by Professor Lee Cronin, building on two decades of research at the University of Glasgow and headquartered in Glasgow, Scotland. Chemify develops "Chemputation" — programmable chemistry — fusing chemistry, robotics, computation, machine learning, and its own universal chemical programming language (chi-DL / XDL) to digitize the discovery, design, and synthesis of molecules on hardware-agnostic robotic chemistry platforms. Its ASSEMBLER stack converts optimized reaction information into fully defined chemical code that automated synthesis machines can execute. The company is backed by Insight Partners and DCVC. Chemify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record with domain-security posture and public site properties.

providers.name: Clarium
providers.description: Clarium is a healthcare supply chain resiliency company founded in early 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic and headquartered in New York City. Its AI-powered platform, Astra OS, unifies real-time data from hospitals and their suppliers across systems of record, then layers data-enabled workflow apps on top: Disruption Monitoring to detect and resolve supply chain disruptions faster, Substitute Management to automate product approvals, and Procedure Card Optimization to standardize and cut cost. Clarium has raised $43M+ (including a $27M Series A led by General Catalyst, with Northzone among its backers) and works with leading health systems such as Mount Sinai, Ochsner Health, Allina Health, and Yale New Haven.

providers.name: Detect
providers.description: Detect Technologies is an IIT Madras-incubated industrial AI company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chennai, India. Its 360-degree Workplace Intelligence Platform, T-Pulse, combines proprietary IoT sensors, drones, robotics and machine vision with industrial AI to deliver automated inspections, predictive maintenance, gas and oil leak detection, structural health monitoring, and real-time workplace safety, operations and security monitoring for enterprises such as Shell, Vedanta, Adani Group and Hindustan Zinc. Backed by Accel and Elevation Capital. The company does not publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Field AI
providers.description: Field AI is a physical-AI robotics company founded in 2023 and based in Mission Viejo, California, building Field Foundation Models (FFMs) — a class of risk-aware, embodied AI that gives general-purpose robots a single "brain" (marketed as EDGE) that works across many robots, tasks, and unstructured real-world environments. Its Belief World Model reasons under uncertainty and runs entirely on the edge, without pre-built maps, GPS, or pre-programmed paths, integrating vision, LiDAR, and other multimodal sensor data. Field AI has production deployments across three continents and serves construction, urban operations, industrial and energy, federal/government, manufacturing, mining, power and utility, and agriculture, with partnerships including Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA (Omniverse), and Certis. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Field AI as a network company; the enrichment pipeline found no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Forterra
providers.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.

providers.name: Fuchsia
providers.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Geek+
providers.description: Geek+ (Geekplus, HKEX: 2590) is a global leader in AI-driven autonomous mobile robot (AMR) solutions for warehouse and logistics automation. Founded in 2015, it delivers end-to-end smart-warehouse systems spanning shelf-to-person (PopPick), tote-to-person (RoboShuttle), pallet-to-person (Skycube) storage and retrieval, robot-arm picking, sorting, and intralogistics transport. Its All-in-One Software Suite (Robot Management System, Warehouse Execution System, Intelligent Warehouse Management System, data and simulation platforms) exposes open REST APIs and SDKs so customers and partners can integrate robot fleets with major WMS, ERP, and MES platforms including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Manhattan Associates, and Blue Yonder. Geek+ serves 3PL, retail, e-commerce, apparel, grocery, healthcare and pharma, manufacturing, automotive, electronics, and cold-chain logistics across 40+ countries, with 950+ deployed warehouses. In 2025 it became the world's first publicly listed AMR warehouse robotics company on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

providers.name: Glydways
providers.description: Glydways is an autonomous urban-transit company building on-demand, high-capacity mobility networks that combine small self-driving electric vehicles (Glydcars), an AI fleet-orchestration layer, and dedicated narrow guideways separated from regular road traffic. The system is designed to move up to 10,000 people per hour while cutting construction cost by roughly 90% and operating cost to about 30% of conventional transit, with launch projects underway in Atlanta, Contra Costa County, California, and at San Jose Airport. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Glydways was surfaced through the venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As an autonomous-transit infrastructure company it publishes a corporate and news presence but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Iconbuild
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. (iconbuild.com) is an Austin, Texas construction technologies company using large-scale robotics, advanced materials, and software to build homes and structures. ICON develops the Vulcan and Phoenix 3D-printing robots, proprietary Lavacrete and CarbonX building materials, and design/build tooling (including its CODEX architectural catalog and ICON Prime), and has printed communities across the US as well as researched off-world construction with NASA (Project Olympus). Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a physical construction / building-technology company; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no API artifacts were harvested.

providers.name: Nanotronics
providers.description: Nanotronics (rebranded to CubeFabs in 2025) builds AI-driven inspection, process-control, and automation systems for advanced industrial manufacturing, with a focus on semiconductors, data centers, EV/automotive, and aerospace/defense. Its "AI factory" platform combines optical imaging, machine learning, and robotics to improve manufacturing precision, yields, and cost efficiency for customers including Hologic, Broadcom, Coherent, and Standard BioTools. Surfaced as a founders-fund portfolio company; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Omnitron Sensors
providers.description: Omnitron Sensors designs advanced MEMS (micro electro mechanical systems) sensors using innovative 3D manufacturing techniques, aiming to deliver high-performance, low-cost sensing with major gains in precision and reliability. Its technology targets AI data centers, autonomous systems and vehicles, environmental and climate monitoring, and extended reality (XR) devices. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, the company is a hardware/semiconductor business with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Re:Build
providers.description: Re:Build Manufacturing is a U.S.-based industrial engineering and manufacturing company that takes complex products from concept to full-rate production through integrated design, engineering, and scalable domestic manufacturing. Founded to rebuild American manufacturing capacity, the company operates a family of specialized engineering and production businesses across more than 14 U.S. locations, spanning aerospace and defense, electrification, energy and environment, medical devices, and robotics and automation. With 400+ engineers and roughly one million square feet of industrial footprint, Re:Build partners with startups and established manufacturers to develop, industrialize, and produce advanced physical products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment confirms it is an industrial/manufacturing company with no public API, developer, or machine surface at this time.

providers.name: Recycleye
providers.description: Recycleye is a London-based company building AI-powered sorting equipment and analytics for waste management and material recovery businesses worldwide. Its products include Recycleye QualiBot robotic sorting cells, Recycleye QuantiSort optical sorting technology, and Recycleye Insights, a data analytics platform that uses computer vision (WasteNet) to identify and categorize waste streams. The company sells hardware and software into recycling operations to improve purity, recovery rates, and profitability. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC. As of this enrichment pass Recycleye publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Ripcord
providers.description: Ripcord is a document digitization and data-extraction company that uses proprietary robotics and AI to turn paper and digital records into structured, actionable business data. Its pipeline runs in three stages — robotic digitization (scanning paper to high-quality digital files), intelligence (AI classification, extraction, validation and enrichment), and action (accessing the resulting data through existing enterprise systems or Ripcord's Canopy cloud content-management platform). Ripcord serves manufacturing, financial services, insurance, real estate, energy, public sector, HR, food & beverage, and accounts-receivable management, with customers including Coca-Cola Bottlers, BP, UCLA, MUFG Bank, Agilent, and the IRS. Integration with enterprise systems (ERP, ECM, RPA, BI) is offered through direct engagement rather than a public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV and Lux Capital.

providers.name: Robust.AI
providers.description: Robust.AI is a robotics company building Carter, an AI-powered collaborative mobile robot for warehouse fulfillment and manufacturing environments. Founded by Rodney Brooks (co-founder of iRobot and Rethink Robotics) and colleagues, the company designs human-centered autonomous material-handling robots that work alongside people with minimal infrastructure change, no capital expenditure, and rapid ROI. Robust.AI is backed by Playground Global and was recognized among Fast Company's World's Most Innovative Companies of 2026. This is a physical-robotics company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or GitHub surface.

providers.name: Vita Inclinata
providers.description: Vita Inclinata Technologies is a Colorado-based hardware company that builds physics-based load stabilization systems for helicopter hoists and construction cranes, eliminating the dangerous spin and sway of suspended loads. Its ecosystem spans Vita Aerospace (helicopter and rescue hoist stabilization), Vita Industrial (crane and construction load control), Air Rescue Systems (hoist training and products), and the Vita Rescue System used in military MEDEVAC operations. The company is Techstars-backed. It was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network; as a physical-hardware manufacturer it currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Zeitview
providers.description: Zeitview (formerly DroneBase) is an AI-powered aerial inspection and asset intelligence platform. It combines a managed network of drone and aircraft pilots with computer-vision analytics and lifecycle asset-management software to deliver inspection imagery, condition assessments, and actionable intelligence for wind energy, solar, utilities, oil & gas, construction, commercial real estate, and property management. As of this profile the company operates a customer web platform, support center, and blog but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; data access is arranged through direct customer engagement.

providers.name: Physicsx
providers.description: PhysicsX is an AI-native engineering software company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in London (Shoreditch) with an office in New York, building a platform that embeds physics AI directly into industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows. The platform unifies simulation, physics AI, data, and engineering applications into a single foundation, pairing fast AI-driven physics inference (Deep Physics Models) with numerical simulation to compress development cycles and expand the design space engineers can explore. It integrates with industry-standard CAE/CAD tooling (ANSYS, CATIA, Siemens NX, OpenFOAM, Siemens Star-CCM+), runs cloud-agnostically across AWS and Azure plus hybrid and on-premises deployments, and serves aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy and renewables. Born out of Formula One, PhysicsX has raised roughly $489M across five rounds from investors including General Catalyst, Atomico, Temasek, NVIDIA, Siemens, and Applied Materials. There is no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Reliable Robotics
providers.description: Reliable Robotics is a California-based aerospace company developing continuous autopilot and remote piloting systems that retrofit existing fixed-wing aircraft for automated and remotely supervised flight across all phases (taxi, take-off, cruise, landing). The company has flown automated Cessna 208 Caravan demonstrations including a fully uncrewed take-off and landing in 2023, and is pursuing FAA Part 23 supplemental type certification for its automation system. Reliable Robotics has contracts with the U.S. Air Force AFWERX program and the Defense Innovation Unit to evaluate automated cargo and ISR missions on platforms including the Cessna 208, and has partnered with Textron Aviation on certification work. The company's founders are alumni of SpaceX and Tesla autopilot teams. Reliable Robotics is partner- and government-gated and does not currently offer public consumer or developer APIs.

providers.name: Unchained Labs
providers.description: Unchained Labs is a life-science tools company that designs, manufactures, and sells analytical instruments, automation, and consumables for biologics, gene therapy, cell therapy, nanoparticle, exosome, and genomics research. Its product line includes plate-based systems for protein characterization, concentration and quantification (Lunatic and Stunner), protein stability and formulation (Uncle), automated buffer exchange and sample prep (Big Tuna, Little Big Tuna), viscosity measurement, and lipid-nanoparticle synthesis and analysis. The company serves biopharma R&D, process development, and QC labs. Unchained Labs is primarily a hardware, reagent, and lab-software vendor; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, REST/GraphQL surface, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and enriched with verified company identity and link properties from its public website.

providers.name: Instalily
providers.description: InstaLILY builds Lily, an AI "Forward Deployed Engineer" for the physical and regulated economy. Lily learns how an enterprise operates, builds custom software agents for high-friction operational work such as quoting, routing, field service, and approvals, and runs them inside the systems companies already use including SAP, NetSuite, Epicor, Salesforce, HubSpot, and Snowflake. InstaLILY serves industrial distribution and MRO, manufacturing and OEM, field service, healthcare and pharma, and private equity. The company is headquartered at 455 Broadway, New York, and is backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Ubiq (now NECTURE)
providers.description: Ubiq is a Vienna, Austria mobility-intelligence company (NECTURE GmbH) that rebranded from UBIQ to NECTURE in 2024. Its "distributed operations" SaaS platform turns fleet data into action for shared-mobility operators, business fleets transitioning to EVs, autonomous fleets, and last-mile delivery -- offering automated rebalancing, predictive charging (Charging as a Service), and airport peak services, alongside StreetCrowd, its decentralized community workforce for fleet operations. Founded in 2015 around city parking optimization, it pivoted to shared-mobility SaaS in 2020 and is backed by Speedinvest among other investors. No public developer portal, API documentation, or client packages were found.

providers.name: Rational
providers.description: Rational (rational.to) is a Y Combinator (S26) company building AI employees, or "AI coworkers," for accounting and finance teams. Its AI agents onboard themselves to a firm, build a company "brain," and perform recurring accounting work — accounts payable, AR collections, bookkeeping, bank reconciliation, document collection, expense review, and month-end close — while keeping postings, payment release, and policy-sensitive decisions behind explicit human approval gates with an inspectable review history. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco by Jibril Moinuddin and Christ Xu, Rational targets accounting firms and finance teams facing a structural capacity and labor shortage. As an early-stage company it currently exposes a marketing and agent-discovery surface (llms.txt, ai-discovery.json, RFC 9116 security.txt) rather than a public developer API; this profile captures that surface and will be enriched as a developer platform ships.

providers.name: Relay.app
providers.description: Relay.app was a workflow automation platform (an AI-assisted alternative to Zapier and Make) that let teams build and run automated, multi-step workflows connecting external SaaS applications, with human-in-the-loop approval steps and AI actions embedded in the automation flow. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of 2026 the product has been discontinued: free users lost access on 2026-08-15 and paying customers on 2026-09-14, with the site now serving a shutdown notice and a data-export path only. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook reference are published for the platform.

providers.name: Sales Patriot
providers.description: SalesPatriot deploys artificial intelligence into enterprise supply chain operations, embedding engineers onsite to build custom AI solutions that integrate fragmented business systems (ERP, CRM, email, spreadsheets, and supplier portals) and automate routine workflows. The platform aggregates data from scattered sources into a unified, searchable system, automates tasks such as quoting, sourcing, and data entry, and visualizes real-time operational metrics for executives. It serves defense contracting and procurement, complex multi-source procurement operations, and high-volume distribution. SalesPatriot is a portfolio company of CRV. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network and enriched by the pipeline; the company publishes no public developer or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Agility Robotics
providers.description: Agility Robotics is a Salem, Oregon humanoid robotics company building industrial bipedal robots for warehouse and factory automation. Founded in 2015 as a spin-out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Laboratory, its flagship product is Digit — described as the first humanoid robot in commercial production deployment — and Arc, the cloud-based automation platform that operates Digit fleets, provides real-time visibility, manages task assignments, and connects Digit to existing warehouse automation including AMRs, WMS, and WES systems. Digit has commercial deployments and pilots with Amazon, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre, with an expanded NVIDIA partnership for foundation-model and simulation tooling. Agility operates RoboFab, a humanoid robot factory in Salem, OR with capacity to produce 10,000 robots annually. Digit has surpassed 100,000 totes moved in commercial deployment at a single Georgia facility. Agility Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Digit or Arc; integration is performed by Agility's solutions team and partners through a gated low-level JSON-over-WebSocket API and pysdk delivered with the robot. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (JFrog, Bazel, Fluent Bit, Kubernetes Cluster API) plus an archived documentation repo for the earlier Cassie research platform.

providers.name: Burnbot
providers.description: Burnbot is a wildfire mitigation and fuels management company that builds autonomous, remotely-operated machines and delivers field services to reduce hazardous vegetation and conduct controlled, precision fuel-reduction burns. Its equipment operates in steep, remote, and hazardous terrain around the clock in most weather conditions, cutting fuel loads without disturbing healthy vegetation or compacting soil, and is used across fire hazard mitigation, systematic fuels management, and timber operations. Burnbot works with utilities, transportation agencies, land managers, and tribal governments including PG&E, Caltrans, the U.S. Forest Service, and CAL FIRE. Burnbot was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a hardware and field-services company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Collabra
providers.description: Collabra (Collabra Pty Ltd, ABN 35 672 933 818) is an Australian enterprise AI automation company whose platform combines robotic process automation with large language models to run back-office operations — contract review, revenue assurance, financial operations, vendor management, data processing, and compliance monitoring. Its product suite is CollabraCore (isolated, segmented data-protection workspaces), CollabraGuard (an AI-safety layer that constrains LLM output to prevent hallucinations and errors while logging every action), and CollabraFlow (a rapid build-test-deploy environment for automation workflows). The public tagline is "AI you can trust to run your operations". As of this profile Collabra is a demo-led SaaS with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Emerson Electric
providers.description: Emerson Electric is a Fortune 500 global automation leader with more than 135 years of innovation history. Its portfolio spans automation systems, discrete automation, final control, measurement instrumentation, and test and measurement, marketed through brands such as Fisher, Rosemount, DeltaV, Micro Motion, ASCO, Bettis, PACSystems, Flexim, and NI. Emerson serves industries including power, oil and gas, chemical, life sciences, food and beverage, automotive, data centers, mining, and marine. This repository captures the public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable artifacts associated with Emerson Electric.

providers.name: Human Archive
providers.description: Human Archive is a Stanford- and Berkeley-founded, Y Combinator-funded data lab building foundational multimodal datasets for training AI and robotics systems to understand human movement and interaction. It collects and labels first-person video, RGB-D, audio, tactile, and motion-capture data from a network of 100,000+ contributors and 500+ industry partners, and provides dataset access to researchers and enterprise partners through a customer dashboard on request. The company is a B2B data infrastructure provider rather than a self-serve platform, and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: ICON
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. is an Austin, Texas construction-technology company building large-scale robotic 3D printing systems, materials, and software to make home building faster, more affordable, and more resilient. Its flagship Titan 3D construction printer, orchestrated by the proprietary BuildOS software that translates architectural designs into robotic tool paths and manages material flow, can print the wall system of a 2,500 sq. ft. home in under seven days. ICON operates a Design + Build division delivering 3D-printed homes and communities, a Technology division selling its printers and building systems to other builders, the CODEX digital home design catalog, and ICON Prime. The company is privately held and backed by investors including Bond Capital and Pantera Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a venture-portfolio lead; ICON publishes a marketing and product presence but no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Insitu
providers.description: Insitu Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company that designs, builds, and operates uncrewed aerial systems (UAS) and related intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance technologies for defense and government customers. Its product line includes the Integrator, ScanEagle, and RQ-21A air vehicles alongside imaging payloads, ground control stations, and mission software such as TacitView, the Media Management Suite, and the Tungsten SDK. Insitu delivers end-to-end capabilities for collecting, processing, and distributing information, with more than 1.6 million operational flight hours across 30-plus international customers. Insitu operates as a defense contractor and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: KUKA
providers.description: KUKA AG is a German industrial automation company headquartered in Augsburg, Bavaria, founded in 1898 and majority-owned by China's Midea Group since 2016. KUKA designs and manufactures industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), production cells, controllers, and the software stack that drives them. Its product portfolio spans six-axis articulated robots (KR series), sensitive collaborative robots (LBR iiwa, LBR iisy), mobile platforms (KMR iiwa, KMP), and palletizing/welding/CNC cells, controlled by the KR C4 and KR C5 / KR C5 micro controller generations. The robot software stack centers on KUKA System Software (KSS/VSS) for KR C4-class hardware, the newer iiQKA.OS / iiQKA.OS2 operating system for KR C5, and the KUKA Robot Language (KRL) for motion programming, with extension surfaces including KUKA.RobotSensorInterface (RSI), KUKA.EthernetKRL, KUKA.PLC mxAutomation for external PLC control, KUKA.OPC UA, and KUKA.AppTech / iiQKA App Builder for option packages. Engineering and simulation are delivered through iiQWorks (iiQWorks.Sim, iiQWorks.App Builder, iiQWorks.Copilot) and KUKA.Sim, while operational software includes KUKA Xpert (documentation/cloud), KUKA iiQoT (condition monitoring), and KUKA Connect / my.KUKA customer portals. KUKA does not publish a first-party public REST/OpenAPI developer API or an official GitHub organization for its robot control stack; integration is performed through proprietary protocols (RSI, EthernetKRL, mxAutomation, OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) and SDKs distributed via the iiQKA Creator portal and KUKA Xpert. A meaningful body of open-source KUKA integration code lives in the community-maintained kroshu GitHub organization (ROS 2 drivers, external-control SDK, URDF robot descriptions) and the roboticsapi / openkuka projects. KUKA serves automotive, electronics, battery, metal, consumer goods, healthcare, aerospace, and e-commerce logistics customers, and through its Swisslog subsidiary extends into warehouse and intralogistics automation.

providers.name: Nickelytics
providers.description: Nickelytics is a data-driven out-of-home (OOH) and digital-out-of-home (DOOH) advertising platform that turns moving assets into measurable media. It wraps gig-economy and rideshare vehicles, autonomous sidewalk delivery robots, and e-scooters with brand campaigns, then layers geo-targeting, programmatic DOOH buying, route verification, proof-of-play, and performance reporting into a single campaign dashboard. Nickelytics was acquired by Kiwibot for roughly $25M in September 2024 and now operates as the "r-ads" advertising product of Robot.com. It has no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; campaign activation runs through an advertiser dashboard rather than an API.

providers.name: Open Bionics
providers.description: Open Bionics is a Bristol, UK-based medical technology company that designs and manufactures advanced multi-grip bionic arms for children and adults with upper-limb differences. Its Hero product family (Hero ARM, Hero PRO, Hero RGD, Hero FLEX and Hero GAUNTLET) pairs 3D-printed, lightweight myoelectric prosthetic hands with an ecosystem of MyoPods wireless electrodes and the Sidekick companion app, delivered through a network of specialist prosthetists and clinics in the US and UK. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: PitPro Automation
providers.description: PitPro Automation is a fleet-maintenance technology company building automated tire-service systems that perform full tire changes and rotations on commercial fleet vehicles in under fifteen minutes. Targeting Class 2 and smaller vehicles, the company serves last-mile delivery, rideshare, utility, telecom, moving, and government fleets with in-bay automation, 24/7 monitoring, and field support. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, PitPro is a hardware-and-software provider focused on reducing fleet downtime; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Tennibot
providers.description: Tennibot builds AI-powered ball machines and autonomous ball collectors for tennis, pickleball, and padel. Its flagship Partner ball machine and Rover ball collector use computer vision and robotics to deliver realistic drills and eliminate manual ball pickup, controlled through the Tennibot mobile app for iOS and Android. The company, based in Auburn, Alabama and backed by Techstars, sells direct-to-consumer hardware; it ships a companion mobile app but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; no external API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: TerraFirma
providers.description: TerraFirma, Inc. is a construction technology and physical-AI company building the robotic infrastructure stack for modern heavy-civil construction. Founded in 2024 by former SpaceX engineers and based in Austin, Texas, it combines AI-enabled pre-construction software (Mission Planner), a remote command-and-control center (Mission Control), and retrofitted semi-autonomous heavy machinery — excavators, bulldozers, loaders, graders and rollers operated autonomously, remotely, or traditionally. The company raised roughly $115M including a $100M Series A led by Kleiner Perkins with Bain Capital Ventures. TerraFirma publishes no public developer/API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Zimmer Biomet
providers.description: Zimmer Biomet is a global medical technology company that designs, manufactures, and markets orthopedic reconstructive products, sports medicine, biologics, extremities, trauma products, dental implants, and related surgical products. The company is a Fortune 500 organization with operations in over 25 countries and a portfolio of digital and robotic technologies including ZBEdge Dynamic Intelligence, ROSA Robotics, the mymobility patient app, Persona Knee, and ZBEdge Analytics. Zimmer Biomet does not currently publish a public REST API developer portal; its digital platforms are surfaced through partner integrations, hospital systems, and proprietary devices.

providers.name: Zoox
providers.description: Zoox is an Amazon subsidiary developing a purpose-built, bidirectional, symmetrical robotaxi vehicle designed from the ground up for autonomous ride-hailing rather than retrofitted from a conventional car. The vehicle carries up to four riders in a carriage-style seating layout, has no steering wheel or pedals, and is engineered for dense urban operation. Zoox provides the autonomous driving stack, the vehicle hardware, and a consumer ride-hail app. Commercial robotaxi service has launched in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with expansion announced for Austin, Miami, Atlanta, and Los Angeles. Acquired by Amazon in 2020, Zoox does not publish a public developer API or open research dataset; its public surface is product, ride-experience, and safety content. This profile captures the company surface for API Evangelist reference.

providers.name: HavocAI
providers.description: HavocAI (Havoc) is a Providence, Rhode Island-based defense technology company building all-domain collaborative autonomy software and autonomous surface vessels for the U.S. Navy, U.S. Army and allied militaries. Its software suite pairs Havoc OS, an edge autonomy operating system for heterogeneous platforms, with Havoc C2 for one-to-many operator control, Havoc Insights for real-time sensor and telemetry analytics, and Havoc Connect, a resilient peer-to-peer overlay network for degraded or GPS-denied environments. The company builds the Rampage, Seahound, Kiakoa and Atlas autonomous surface vessels and is partnered with Hanwha on 200-foot ASVs. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no public developer API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no developer portal or documentation, no published SDKs or packages, no MCP server, and no A2A agent card - the platform is delivered under defense contract rather than as a self-serve developer product.

providers.name: Jenkins Pipeline
providers.description: Jenkins Pipeline is a suite of plugins for the Jenkins automation server that supports implementing and integrating continuous delivery pipelines as code. It provides an extensible domain-specific language (DSL) with two syntax styles - Declarative and Scripted - and core building blocks (agents, stages, steps) for modeling simple-to-complex CI/CD workflows that are versioned with application source code via a Jenkinsfile.

providers.name: Nexiu
providers.description: Nexiu (Nexiu AI LLC) is a Latin America-focused recruiting automation platform that uses AI agents to source, contact, screen, and schedule high-volume candidates over the official WhatsApp Business API, integrating with Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Meet) and existing ATS systems and job boards. It offers a fully managed pay-per-hire service (Nexiu Managed) and a self-service SaaS platform (Nexiu Platform) for internal talent-acquisition teams, and is backed by 500 Global (500 Latam) and NVIDIA Inception. As of this pass Nexiu consumes third-party APIs (WhatsApp Business, Google, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI) but does not publish a public developer API of its own.

providers.name: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories
providers.description: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories (RedWing Labs, operated by Kitemaps AMS Pvt Ltd) is a Bangalore, India based, Techstars-backed company that designs, develops and deploys fully autonomous drones to transform logistics supply chains. It offers a fleet of long-range, urban and medium-range delivery aircraft plus an operations software suite, and runs an autonomous four-step delivery flow (order, handoff to flight operations, proof of delivery, return to hub) used to move healthcare products, food and other goods within the hour. The company reports operational milestones including 145,930+ kilometers flown and thousands of deliveries completed. RedWing does not publish a first-party developer API; its public agent surface is the platform-provided Wix Site MCP endpoint advertised in its llms.txt.

providers.name: Westmag
providers.description: Western Magnetics (Westmag) designs and manufactures brushless DC (BLDC) drone motors and robot actuators in South San Francisco, California. Built and scaled in America and NDAA-compliant from day one, Westmag is a vertically integrated motor company spanning design, manufacturing, and supply chain — producing high-volume BLDC drone motors for Group 1, 2, and 3 UAS platforms (20-100mm stators, Kv 100-3,000, outrunner and inrunner) and integrated actuators for humanoid and mobile robots (torque 1-150Nm, 24-48V, gearing 6:1-12:1). Founded by David Hansen (CEO) and Jordan Sanders (COO) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Menlo Ventures, and NFDG. This is a hardware company; it currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Wonderful
providers.description: Wonderful is an applied-AI company building an enterprise AI platform for critical, high-volume workflows. It combines an AI platform (run any model, any modality, any use case, fully governed) with local deployment teams and a strategic partnership model to help large organizations accelerate AI adoption. Wonderful powers agentic automation for enterprises such as national telecom operators, energy providers, and financial-services firms, covering customer-service containment, collections across millions of clients, internal IT automation, and end-to-end billing resolution, with reported outcomes like a 91.5% containment rate across millions of customers. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and IVP. Wonderful sells an enterprise platform with deployment services rather than a self-serve public developer API; its developer documentation is login-gated.

providers.name: Covariant
providers.description: Covariant is an Emeryville, California warehouse-robotics AI company founded in 2017 (originally as Embodied Intelligence) by UC Berkeley professor Pieter Abbeel and his former students Peter Chen, Rocky Duan, and Tianhao Zhang. The company builds the Covariant Brain, a universal AI platform that enables industrial picking robots to handle virtually any SKU regardless of shape, size, or packaging, and in March 2024 it introduced RFM-1 (Robotics Foundation Model 1), an 8-billion-parameter multimodal transformer trained on text, images, video, robot actions, and numerical sensor readings to give robots human-like reasoning over the physical world. Covariant ships AI-powered solutions for order picking, sortation, item induction, kitting, depalletization, and goods-to-person workflows, delivered through long-running integration partnerships with KNAPP (Pick-it-Easy Robot, since 2020) and ABB (warehouse robotics, since 2020), as well as deployments with retailers and logistics providers worldwide. In August 2024, Amazon announced a non-exclusive license to Covariant's robotic foundation models and hired its three co-founders along with roughly a quarter of its workforce in a reverse-acquihire arrangement; Covariant continues to operate independently under COO-turned-CEO Ted Stinson and co-founder Tianhao Zhang. The Covariant Brain and RFM-1 are proprietary, deployed on-premise on partner robotics hardware, and the company has no public developer API, SDK, open-source release, or third-party developer program.

providers.name: Farmwise
providers.description: FarmWise Labs is an agricultural technology company building AI-powered robotics for specialty crop farming. Its flagship product, Vulcan, is an intra-row weeder and precision cultivator that uses computer vision and machine learning to identify and mechanically remove weeds without herbicides, covering up to three acres per hour and saving growers an estimated $250+ per acre. The self-calibrating machine operates in all field conditions and receives over-the-air software updates. Founded in San Francisco and backed by GV (Google Ventures), FarmWise is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.

providers.name: Hessian
providers.description: Hessian is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building a forward-deployed AI agent platform for automating business operations. Its engineers embed on-site to map real workflows, then build and operate custom AI agents on the Hessian platform to run those processes end-to-end — spanning sales proposals, financial reconciliation, data management, and internal-system synchronization. The platform surfaces workflows, task and agent orchestration, workers, queue groups, prompts, assets, artifacts, secrets, webhooks, and audit logging, with integrations for tools such as GitHub, Slack, Postgres, AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, OpenAI, and Claude. Hessian does not yet publish a public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or an OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and web properties while the developer surface is awaiting release.

providers.name: Symbotic
providers.description: Symbotic is an AI-powered warehouse automation company that designs, manufactures, and operates end-to-end robotic distribution and micro-fulfillment systems for food and beverage, retail grocery, healthcare, apparel, retail general merchandise, and consumer packaged goods customers. Its portfolio includes the Symbotic distribution solution for case handling, SymMicro for less-than-case micro-fulfillment, autonomous SymBots mobile robots, warehouse AI software, and Warehouse-as-a-Service offerings. Symbotic operates as a hardware-and-services vendor and does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs.

providers.name: Theker
providers.description: Theker (THEKER Robotics) is a Barcelona-based robotics and artificial intelligence company whose stated mission is "solving 100% of physical work" — building humanoid and physical-AI systems it frames as "a power beyond human" and "the next frontier of robotics and intelligence." The company is at a stealth stage: its public site is a landing page and careers portal with product details deliberately withheld ("Details remain secured").
