Its public GitHub organization (THEKER Robotics, Spain) works in the physical-AI/ROS 2 stack — forks of the ZED ROS 2 wrapper, NVIDIA cuRobo CUDA motion planning, and Meta SAM 3 perception. Backed by CRV. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is published yet; this profile captures its identity and public surface pending a developer platform.

providers.name: Airforestry
providers.description: AirForestry is a Swedish climate-technology company developing autonomous electric drones that perform forest thinning from the air. Its system pairs AI and computer vision for tree identification and selection with a lightweight aerial harvesting tool, letting a fleet of drones fell and extract trees without ground machinery. The result is forestry with zero soil compaction, no root damage and no machine tracks, higher operational efficiency, and lower emissions than conventional harvesters, while increasing forest growth and carbon sequestration. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. It currently publishes a marketing and news presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: EverestLabs
providers.description: EverestLabs builds AI, computer vision, and robotics for the recycling industry. Its RecycleOS platform identifies, tracks, and sorts recoverable materials on the conveyor lines of Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs), giving recyclers, reclaimers, and packaging manufacturers analytics, bale tracing, plant optimization, and compliance reporting to increase recovery rates, cut labor costs, and verify recycled content. Headquartered in Fremont, California and backed by Sierra Ventures. EverestLabs does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, GitHub, and discovery surface.

providers.name: Turbine
providers.description: Turbine (Turbine Ltd) is a Budapest-based AI biotechnology company that virtualizes biological experiments to accelerate and de-risk drug discovery. Its Simulated Cell platform trains virtual cells on genomic, transcriptomic, and perturbation-response data, then runs millions of in silico experiments per day to predict therapy response across cell lines, patient-derived organoids and xenografts, and patient samples. Turbine offers partner-facing products for target discovery and de-risking, combination design, and ADC (antibody-drug conjugate) intelligence, and works with pharmaceutical partners including AstraZeneca and MSD. The company publishes research code and benchmarks on GitHub but exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: blueflite
providers.description: blueflite is a Techstars-backed unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) company that designs and manufactures autonomous cargo and delivery drones built on its SLATE platform for all-weather, time-sensitive logistics. Its aircraft target last-mile shipping and medical or life-saving delivery (such as defibrillators and emergency supplies), and the company complements the hardware with blueDelivery (a consumer ordering app), blueDigital (a cloud productivity tool), and blueControl, alongside drone consulting, engineering, and project services. blueflite is on the FAA Section 44807 approved UAS list and holds FCC conditional approval, and was founded by Frank Noppel and James McClearen. No public developer or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Gather AI
providers.description: Gather AI is a Physical AI platform for logistics that gives warehouses dock-to-dock inventory visibility. Cameras mounted on autonomous drones and forklifts capture inventory, and computer vision extracts structured data (LPNs, UPCs, lot codes, and free text) from the imagery. Its Sage AI engine analyzes operations and surfaces prioritized actions before each shift, while automated Workflows route tasks to the right personnel across integrated systems. The plug-and-play solution deploys in hours alongside existing warehouse management systems, serving manufacturing, healthcare, food & beverage, retail, and 3PL operations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: Riiico
providers.description: RIIICO is a Duesseldorf-based industrial software company building 3D-AI tools that digitalize the factory shop floor. Its platform turns reality scans (point clouds) of existing plants into CAD-ready, pre-classified 3D models, cutting 3D modeling time by up to 80% and accelerating factory retrofit, robot programming, and simulation. RIIICO integrates with NVIDIA Omniverse (OpenUSD) and Siemens Xcelerator, and counts Siemens, Volvo, and Schaeffler among its customers. It won the Siemens Inventors of the Year Award 2024 and is backed by Earlybird, PiLabs, and seed + speed. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Vestris
providers.description: Vestris is an AI-powered platform that automates the real estate pre-closing process for mortgage title and closing operations. It uses browser agents to log into county tax portals, extract property records, parse purchase contracts, run tax calculations, generate title abstracts, and produce title commitments and closing documents. Positioned as "the AI processing unit for mortgage title and closing," Vestris aims to replace manual title searchers and accelerate property deal closing. The company is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup based in San Francisco. As of this profile it operates a product application (waitlist / demo access) with no publicly documented developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: CloudMinds
providers.description: CloudMinds (Dataa Robotics / 达闼科技) is a cloud-robotics company founded in 2015 with dual headquarters in Beijing, China and Irvine, California, backed by SoftBank and Foxconn. It builds cloud-connected smart machines and the HARIX ("Human Augmented Robot Intelligence with eXtreme reality") cloud AI robot brain, operating cloud robots over its Mobile-intranet Cloud Services (MCS) and Virtual Backbone Network (VBN). Its developer offering is the HARIX Robot Development Kit (RDK) — an app behavior blueprint editor, motion/dance editor, scene-map tools, and a robot simulation/training platform — distributed through the HARIX RDK portal, the HarixRDK GitHub organization, and the official "harix" Python SDK on PyPI. CloudMinds does not publish a public REST API; it exposes flexible APIs and middleware to integrate robots with legacy systems. Added to the U.S. BIS Entity List in May 2020.

providers.name: Dexory
providers.description: Dexory is a UK-based warehouse intelligence and robotics company whose DexoryView platform pairs fleets of autonomous mobile scanning robots with physical AI to deliver real-time "ground truth" visibility across warehouses and distribution centers. The robots autonomously scan more than 10,000 pallet locations per hour and up to 18 meters of racking height, building a live digital twin that feeds AI-driven analytics for inventory accuracy, space and slotting optimization, damage/compliance detection, and operational performance. DexoryView is organized into modules (Integrity for stock accuracy and automated cycle counts, Optimise for space and productivity analytics, and Adapt for real-time operational response) and connects into existing warehouse and ERP systems such as SAP EWM, Manhattan, Blue Yonder, and Körber through pre-built connectors. Dexory serves 3PL logistics, manufacturing, food & beverage, retail, pharma, and air cargo operators. Added to the API Evangelist network from Atomico's portfolio and enriched via the pipeline; Dexory does not currently publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Firestorm
providers.description: Firestorm (Firestorm Labs, Inc.) is a San Diego based defense technology company founded in 2022 that builds expeditionary manufacturing systems and modular unmanned aerial systems. Its xCELL containerized production unit uses HP Multi Jet Fusion additive manufacturing to 3D print industrial-grade PA-12 nylon composite airframes and spare parts at the tactical edge, feeding modular UAS platforms including the Tempest fixed-wing family and the Squall FPV drone. The company holds a five-year, $100M U.S. Air Force IDIQ and closed an $82M Series B in April 2026 led by Washington Harbour Partners. Firestorm ships hardware, not software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Lily Camera
providers.description: The domain lily.camera currently serves "Lily Camera", a consumer-facing marketplace that connects clients with certified drone pilots for aerial photography and videography across real estate, events, agriculture, construction, and media production. It is a client-rendered single-page application: every requested path returns the same HTML shell, and the routes defined in its JavaScript bundle cover browsing pilots and drones, comparisons, bookings, messaging, a pilot dashboard, and a drone raffle. There is no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDKs, and no /.well-known discovery surface. The site is built on Lovable (GPT Engineer), monetized with Google AdSense, and backed by a hosted Supabase project. No API artifacts could be harvested because the provider publishes none.

providers.name: Aerodyne
providers.description: Aerodyne Group is a Malaysia-headquartered DT3 (drone technology, data technology, and digital transformation) enterprise solutions provider, founded in 2014. Through its Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) model and the AI-powered, cloud-based vertikaliti asset-management platform, Aerodyne turns aerial and sensor data into deep analytics and actionable insights for infrastructure, power line, wind turbine, solar, and agricultural (Agrimor) asset inspection and management. Operating across 45 countries with a global network of AeroRangers, it was ranked the world's number-one drone service provider by Drone Industry Insights in 2021 and 2022. Aerodyne is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable specification has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Aseon Labs
providers.description: Aseon Labs builds robotic pitstops for self-driving cars — distributed robotic micro-depots (the "Aseon Pod") that automate charging, interior and exterior cleaning, and inspection for autonomous vehicle fleets directly within their operating zones, so vehicles reset locally instead of returning to centralized facilities. The company says the approach can cut reset costs by up to 50%, reduce downtime by ~65%, and add $50,000+ in annual revenue per vehicle. Founded in 2026 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026 batch), the Redwood City, CA startup is a physical-infrastructure and robotics company; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Skycatch
providers.description: Skycatch built spatial data capture, processing, and analytics for mining and construction sites, turning drone and aerial imagery into high-precision 3D data, volumetrics, and AI-driven site insights. Its products included Spatial Sight, Spatial DataHub (datahub.skycatch.com), and EdgeServer for on-site edge processing. Skycatch was acquired by Caterpillar Inc. on July 7, 2026 (following Caterpillar's RPMGlobal acquisition) to expand its mining technology capabilities. A developer platform exists at docs.skycatch.com but is password-gated, and no public API specification is available. Originally surfaced as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company.

providers.name: Asylon
providers.description: Asylon Robotics is an American-made robotic security company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Norristown, Pennsylvania, that automates physical perimeter security with autonomous drones, ground robots, software, and AI. Its flagship products include the Guardian automated security drone (the most widely used automated security drone system, with tens of thousands of patrol and alarm-response missions completed), the DroneDog quadruped ground robot built on Boston Dynamics Spot with the Asylon DogHouse charging enclosure and PupPack cellular PTZ payload, and DroneIQ, the Robotic Security Operations Center (RSOC) and software platform that coordinates robotic assets, fixed surveillance, and human operators. DroneIQ exposes an open-architecture integration layer for third-party alarms and sensors (radar, smart fences, Bosch alarm panels, gun-detection computer vision, Genetec), but the company publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; API and integration access is arranged directly with Asylon. Asylon raised a $26M Series B in July 2025 led by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Armstrong Robotics
providers.description: Armstrong Robotics is building general-purpose robots for commercial kitchens, beginning with autonomous dishwashing systems that load, run, and unload dishware without human intervention. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company is an early-stage robotics startup focused on kitchen labor automation. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead awaiting a public API surface, and this profile carries only the identity and domain-security signals that could be verified from its public website.

providers.name: Burt
providers.description: Burt builds AI teammates (AI coworkers) for logistics, aimed at freight brokers and forwarders. Its agents automate the repetitive, manual work of daily freight operations — track and trace, quoting, scheduling, carrier booking, document processing, proof-of-delivery chasing, and invoice and data entry — so human operators can focus on customer relationships and growing the business. Burt gives full visibility into every AI action with human oversight and approval workflows, rolls out autonomy gradually, and learns from operator corrections and exceptions to build institutional knowledge over time. Burt is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Y Combinator and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Burt does not currently publish a public developer/API surface.

providers.name: ChemTech AI
providers.description: ChemTech AI is an industrial software company, founded in 2018 and headquartered in New York, that builds autonomous AI control systems for chemical production plants. Its software continuously optimizes manufacturing by autonomously adjusting DCS setpoints to push plants to their maximum safe capacity, sustaining peak production while reducing emissions and losses. The platform is applied across chemical processes including ammonia, nitric acid, phosphoric acid, sulfuric acid, methanol, ethanol, and polyethylene, serving the chemicals, food, cosmetics, and oil and gas sectors. ChemTech AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal are currently published.

providers.name: Plus
providers.description: Plus (PlusAI) develops AI-based autonomous driving technology for commercial trucks. Its flagship SuperDrive is an AI-powered Level 4 autonomous driving system, and HyperFoundry is an integrated development platform for Physical AI. Plus works through partnerships with truck OEMs including TRATON GROUP, Hyundai, and IVECO rather than shipping a public developer API. Backed by GGV Capital, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; this enrichment pass confirmed it exposes no public API, SDK, or developer portal surface, and captured its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Poetic
providers.description: Poetic is an enterprise AI automation company whose platform learns an organization's rules and procedures and then executes end-to-end business processes with high precision and compliance. Marketed as "turn your business into software," Poetic ingests procedures, training materials, and expert feedback to build self-healing automations that adapt when underlying systems change, targeting long, multi-step workflows such as fraud detection, KYC, and dispute resolution. The company emphasizes enterprise-grade security with zero data retention (processing data in-transit only) and states SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance, and cites customers including AIG, SoFi, and Chime. Poetic is an early-stage, Kleiner Perkins-backed AI company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Scout
providers.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sensemesh
providers.description: Sensemesh builds an AI-powered operating system that unifies cameras, sensors, and drones into a single intelligent network for real-time perception and autonomous response. The platform fuses visual, thermal, audio, and pressure sensor data so organizations can detect threats, investigate incidents, dispatch drones autonomously, and query sensor history in natural language across law enforcement, corrections and prisons, events and venues, homeowners associations, and schools and universities. Backed by DCVC, Sensemesh was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single marketing site (sensemesh.ai) with no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or well-known metadata.

providers.name: Solomon
providers.description: Solomon (Solomon AI, solomontax.ai) is an agentic AI platform for tax preparation aimed at accounting firms, automating the preparation of review-ready individual 1040 returns for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients. The system interprets K-1/K-3 footnotes, applies multi-state SALT rules to K-1s, reconciles rental and real estate investments, analyzes brokerage statements for foreign income, and produces workpapers and audit trails, positioning itself to replace legacy tools such as SurePrep and K1x. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes no public developer/API surface at this time.

providers.name: The Bot Company
providers.description: The Bot Company is a San Francisco robotics startup founded in 2024 by Kyle Vogt, the co-founder and former CEO of Cruise, building a helpful general-purpose robot for every home to automate everyday household chores. Its team draws from Tesla, Cruise, OpenAI, Google, and Pixar, and the company has raised roughly $301M (reportedly valued near $2B) from investors including Spark Capital and SV Angel. As of this profile the company operates a marketing and careers site only and publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Thirdwave
providers.description: Thirdwave (Third Wave Automation) builds autonomous material-handling systems for warehouses and distribution centers, led by its shared-autonomy forklift platform where one human operator can supervise a fleet of self-driving forklifts that operate independently and hand control back to a person when needed. Its ArmadaFMS (Armada Fleet Management System) software coordinates the robotic fleet across facilities. The company is a venture-backed logistics-robotics provider (backed by Homebrew and Norwest Venture Partners). As of this enrichment pass Third Wave publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: WeRide
providers.description: WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD) is an autonomous driving technology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Guangzhou, China. It develops Level 4 self-driving technology across a portfolio of five core products — Robotaxi, Robobus, Robovan, Robosweeper (autonomous sanitation) and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) — and operates its fleets in more than 40 cities across 12 countries. WeRide does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web presence and domain-security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Zipline
providers.description: Zipline is a South San Francisco–headquartered autonomous logistics company operating the world's largest commercial drone delivery network, with more than two million customer deliveries flown across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan. Zipline designs, builds, and operates two end-to-end aircraft platforms: Platform 1 (P1, "Sparrow"), a long-range fixed-wing aircraft that launches from a catapult, parachutes payloads from altitude, and is used primarily for national-scale healthcare logistics — delivering blood products, vaccines, medicines, and lab samples to hospitals and clinics — and Platform 2 (P2), a short-range hybrid VTOL aircraft with an autonomous tethered "droid" delivery vehicle that lowers packages from a hovering aircraft directly to a designated point on the ground, enabling precision quick-commerce delivery from restaurants, retailers, pharmacies, and hospitals. Zipline's customer roster includes Walmart, OhioHealth, Michigan Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic Florida, MultiCare, Sweetgreen, GNC, Jet's Pizza, the governments of Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, and Kenya, and Japan's Toyota Tsusho, with the P2 platform actively scaling across the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex, Pea Ridge (AR), and expanding into Houston and Phoenix in 2026. The company also operates one of the largest civil autonomous aviation stacks in the world — proprietary detect-and-avoid, route planning, weather, fleet operations, and flight-control software — and in 2025 received the first-ever FAA Part 135 BVLOS (beyond-visual-line-of-sight) operational approval permitting drone package delivery without visual observers. Zipline is a privately held company; its revenue model is drone-as-a-service contracts with healthcare systems, retailers, restaurant brands, and governments. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, GitHub organization, status page, changelog, or self-service developer portal — integrations with customer systems (order management, EHR, WMS, dispatch) are delivered as managed enterprise integrations rather than as a public programmable API.

providers.name: Cyngn
providers.description: Cyngn (NASDAQ: CYN) is a Mountain View, California autonomous vehicle technology company that develops and deploys industrial autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for material handling. Its flagship DriveMod stack is a vehicle-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy system that retrofits onto standard industrial vehicles such as tuggers and forklifts, paired with the Cyngn Insight fleet-management, teleoperation, and analytics platform and the Cyngn Evolve data toolkit — together marketed as the Enterprise Autonomy Suite. Cyngn targets warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics operators facing labor shortages and safety challenges, and integrates with major warehouse management systems (Manhattan, Blue Yonder, SAP EWM). The company traces its corporate lineage to Cyanogen Inc. (the CyanogenMod company), whose dormant GitHub organization still links to cyngn.com.

providers.name: Nebu
providers.description: NEBU (legal entity NEBU LAH SDN. BHD., Malaysia) is an early-stage, AI-powered DevOps-as-a-Service platform positioned as "the missing brain for your cloud" — offering intelligent understanding of cloud infrastructure rather than scripted automation alone. Founded in 2024, the company markets AIOps/MLOps-style cloud management, cost optimization, and intelligent automation for enterprise cloud estates, and self-states a security posture of SOC 2 Type II readiness, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance. As of this profile the product is pre-launch ("we're building what comes next") with a single-page marketing site and no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs yet. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead; the only machine-readable surface found is a valid RFC 9116 /.well-known/security.txt.

providers.name: Netic
providers.description: Netic (legal entity Cybernetic Labs Inc.), headquartered in San Francisco, builds production-grade autonomous AI systems for America's essential service industries — home services, pest control, roofing, consumer health, and veterinary. Its AI Growth Engine spans speech, text, and data with products including Convert (autonomous multi-channel job booking into CRM/FSM systems), Cultivate (autonomous upsell and membership campaigns), Empower (analytics and data-driven decision support), and Evaluate (AI call-center scoring), with Expand announced as coming soon. Netic is backed by Founders Fund, Greylock, and SV Angel. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity, blog, privacy policy, domain-security posture, and its Secureframe-hosted trust center.

providers.name: Nomagic
providers.description: Nomagic builds Physical AI for end-to-end warehouse automation, using AI-powered robotic arms and computer vision to automate picking, packing, sorting and other fulfillment tasks across e-commerce, fashion, pharmaceutical and third-party logistics warehouses. Nomagic exposes a standard Station API for systems integrators, WCS/WMS providers and customers to control its robots, and a Grip AI API that adds an intelligence layer to third-party robot hardware; all robot actions are recorded to the Nomagic Cloud to continually improve its models. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures. Public developer documentation for these APIs is not published; integration is arranged directly with Nomagic.

providers.name: Pickle Robot
providers.description: Pickle Robot builds Physical AI systems for supply chain automation, best known for autonomous truck- and container-unloading robots that handle non-palletized, floor-loaded freight. Its Dill Autonomy Engine (DAE) pairs classical optimal control with generative AI and foundation models, driving an industrial arm with vision, LiDAR, and an air-suction gripper to unload 400-1,500 cases per hour. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in the Boston, Massachusetts area, the company deploys into existing warehouses in days with no WMS integration and counts UPS among its customers. Pickle Robot exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sereact
providers.description: Sereact GmbH is a Stuttgart, Germany based physical-AI company building intelligent robotic systems for warehouse and fulfillment automation. Its "Cortex" platform pairs a Vision Language Action Model (VLAM) with robot control so robots can pick, place, sort, induct, and inspect diverse items in production without task-specific retraining, running across 50+ deployments in Europe and the US. Products include Pick-and-Place, Putwall, Induction, Bin Handling, Returns Handling, and the Lens perception system. Backed by Creandum and Point Nine; announced a $110M Series B. Sereact does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — an internal api.sereact.ai host exists but is a placeholder. This profile captures the company identity and public web/GitHub surface.

providers.name: AKASA
providers.description: AKASA is a generative AI company for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM), building AI-powered products that automate coding, clinical documentation integrity (CDI), prior authorization status, and claim status work for hospitals and health systems. Its platform includes the Prebill Optimization Suite (Coding Optimizer and CDI Optimizer), AI Advisor, Auth Status, and Claim Status, trained on millions of clinical and financial documents. AKASA reports serving 650+ hospitals and 6,500+ outpatient facilities across all 50 states, with customers citing reductions in A/R days and hundreds of monthly staff hours saved. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Tera-ai
providers.description: Tera AI is a San Francisco-based robotics AI company (founded 2023, out of stealth March 2025 with $7.8M seed co-led by Felicis and Inovia) that builds the first unified, software-only spatial reasoning stack for camera-based mapping and navigation across air, onroad, offroad, and sea platforms. Its foundation-model approach delivers GPS-denied, manufacturer-interoperable autonomy that runs on a robot's existing camera and onboard GPU. Tera publishes research (TARDIS/STRIDE) and technical field results but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; this profile captures its public web, research, and GitHub surface.

providers.name: Zalos
providers.description: Zalos is a Y Combinator-backed (F25) company building AI "computer agents" for finance operations. Rather than integrating through APIs, its agents log into a company's existing systems — ERPs, accounting platforms, banks, invoicing and CFO tools such as NetSuite and SAP — and operate the user interface the way a human would, learned from screen recordings. Zalos automates repetitive, multi-step finance workflows including reconciliation, transaction categorization, billing, form filling, month-end close and cross-system KPI reporting, while building a living process graph of an organization's finance operations for documentation and compliance. Founded in 2025 by William Fairbairn (CEO) and Hung Hoang (CTO, previously Apple Pay), the company is based in London and San Francisco and raised a $3.6M seed round led by 14 Peaks. Because Zalos operates entirely through computer-use automation of third-party interfaces, it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs or developer portal.

providers.name: Zauber
providers.description: Zauber is an AI agent platform purpose-built for sea and air freight forwarding operations. Freight forwarders describe their processes in plain language and Zauber's AI agents execute them consistently across global operations, automating rate and booking workflows with exception handling, deploying global workflows with local execution, and giving operators real-time operational visibility into conversion rates, response times, and exception patterns. The platform integrates with existing systems including Office 365, CargoWise One, carrier portals, and proprietary tooling. Zauber is a portfolio company of Point Nine. No public API, developer portal, or developer documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company's identity and security posture.

providers.name: Apptronik
providers.description: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas-based humanoid robotics company founded in 2016 as a spinout from the Human Centered Robotics Lab at the University of Texas at Austin. Co-founded by Jeff Cardenas (CEO), Dr. Nick Paine (CTO), and Dr. Luis Sentis (scientific advisor), the company designs and manufactures Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot standing 5'8", weighing 160 lbs, capable of lifting 55 lbs, and running for roughly 4 hours on a swappable battery. Apollo targets warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics applications including trailer unloading, case picking, palletization, machine tending, and workcell delivery. Apptronik has commercial pilot programs and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz (automotive manufacturing logistics), GXO Logistics (multi-phase R&D in U.S. distribution centers), Jabil (supply-chain partner helping scale production and an internal Apollo deployment), and Google DeepMind (Apollo integrates Gemini Robotics vision-language-action models). The company previously built NASA's Valkyrie humanoid and ten-plus other research robots. As of February 2026 Apptronik had raised more than $935M (including a $520M Series A-X extension) at a reported $5B valuation, with investors including B Capital, Google, and Mercedes-Benz. The company sells/leases Apollo to enterprise customers via a direct contact-sales motion and ships a proprietary "point-and-click" control suite for deploying solutions; there is no public developer portal, no published REST/AsyncAPI/gRPC API, no public SDK, no open-source release, and no public GitHub repositories under the `apptronik` org.

providers.name: Neocis
providers.description: Neocis is a medical robotics company and the maker of Yomi, described as the first and only FDA-cleared robot-assisted dental surgery system. Yomi combines preoperative implant planning software with intraoperative haptic robotic guidance to assist dentists during dental implant placement procedures. The company sells hardware, planning software, and practitioner training to dental practices rather than operating a public developer platform. Neocis is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Path Robotics
providers.description: Path Robotics is a Columbus, Ohio autonomous welding robotics company founded in 2018 by brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (CEO and CTO) out of Case Western Reserve University. The company builds AI-powered intelligent welding cells that automate metal fabrication for defense shipyards, utility and energy infrastructure, data centers, and heavy industry. Its core technology is Obsidian, a physical-AI reinforcement-learning agent trained inside Path's proprietary Weld World Model on tens of millions of welded inches; Obsidian runs at the edge of each cell and makes real-time, seam-by-seam welding decisions using a sensor stack of two cameras plus four lasers that deliver sub-millimeter 360-degree awareness around the torch. Path markets the cells with a CapEx-free consumption model and reports 97%+ first-pass yield, 4x productivity, and 30% lower welding costs across customers including HII (America's largest military shipbuilder), Saronic, LAD Services, Tycrop, Mine Rite Technologies, and Millerbernd. In April 2026 Path announced Rove, a mobile welding system mounted on a quadruped platform, extending its addressable geometry beyond fixed-cell applications. The company has raised approximately $271M across Seed through Series D from Drive Capital, Matter Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Addition, and Yamaha Motor Ventures, with the most recent $100M Series D closing in October 2024. Path Robotics has no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; its GitHub organization contains roughly 50 repositories that are almost entirely upstream open-source forks (ROS, protobuf, abseil, ceres-solver, pytorch3d, etc.) used as internal build dependencies rather than published developer artifacts. Revenue is earned through welding-cell deployments, services, and the consumable weld-output model — not API monetization.

providers.name: Sainapse
providers.description: Sainapse, built by Bayestree Intelligence, is a unified, explainable AI engine for customer support, outreach, and operations that is embedded directly in an enterprise's environment. It connects to existing integrations to source real-time data for autonomous resolution, grounds every response in verified sources of data, and can act as an agent copilot (next best actions, suggested responses) or as an autonomous agent. Sainapse learns from human-in-the-loop corrections and evolving business rules, supports 220+ integrations, and is offered as a hosted service or deployed on-premises. It publishes SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance. Sainapse is an enterprise, demo-led product with no public self-serve API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: Synphony
providers.description: Synphony builds and deploys robots that work in the real world, combining AI, robotics, and human-in-the-loop systems so machines can perform practical physical tasks across agriculture, assembly, and inspection. Its platform trains AI models on real-world data, tests robot performance in realistic scenarios, and deploys systems into production. The company's first application is autonomous strawberry-harvesting robots plus farm software services (bed-level analytics, data-pipeline integration, and agentic solutions), targeting California's roughly $3B strawberry industry where labor is about 60% of costs. Founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), Synphony runs a customer-facing platform at app.synphony.co but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: CruxOCM
providers.description: CruxOCM is a midstream automation software company that delivers closed-loop, real-time process control for oil and gas pipeline operations. Its Industrial Automation Hub (IAH) runs on top of existing SCADA and DCS infrastructure to automate control-room procedures, unlock asset throughput, reduce operating expenses, and improve safety without adding headcount. Product families include pipeBOT, gatherBOT and draBOT for pipeline, gathering and drag-reduction automation, and maxOPT, leanOPT and powerOPT for throughput, cost and power optimization, alongside a Deployment Manager, Log Analyser and Status Dashboard. CruxOCM is headquartered in Houston, Texas and closed a $17M Series A in 2024 led by Microsoft's M12 venture fund. This company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Electio
providers.description: Electio (Electio Technologies) is a San Francisco-based, General Catalyst-backed software company building modern control-system software for energy production and transportation infrastructure. The company modernizes the legacy industrial control layers behind power generation, oil and gas, and transportation networks with next-generation software for monitoring, automation, and operational reliability. Electio is an early-stage, largely stealth company: it publishes a company website, a careers page, a contact page, and a privacy policy, but has not released a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation as of this profile. This entry was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Locusrobotics
providers.description: Locus Robotics is a warehouse automation company that builds autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and the LocusONE platform, a data-science-driven system for enterprise-wide AMR deployments and warehouse performance management. Its fleet (Locus Array, Origin, and Vector robots) plus integrated software supports robots-to-goods and autonomous fulfillment across 3PL, retail, healthcare, and industrial operations. LocusONE integrates with leading WMS platforms through the LocusConnect middleware, a REST API secured with OAuth 2.0 and documented as OpenAPI 2.0 via SwaggerUI; API access is provisioned per customer rather than published as an open developer program. Locus Robotics is backed by Bond Capital and maintains an active open-source presence in the ROS (Robot Operating System) ecosystem on GitHub.

providers.name: Urban Machine
providers.description: Urban Machine is a GV-backed robotics company building AI and computer-vision powered machines that remove metal fasteners (nails, staples, and screws) from construction and demolition lumber waste, reclaiming it for premium wood products and circular-economy reuse. The company publishes no public API, but maintains an open-source ROS/Python robotics tooling footprint on GitHub, including the colcon-poetry-ros package on PyPI.

providers.name: Istante
providers.description: Istante is an Italian technology company (VAT IT03635230547, based in the Perugia area) that develops and operates Athena, a business-process-automation platform built around a team of specialized AI assistants. Athena covers assistants for communication routing and email classification, credit management and collections, a 24/7 voice/phone assistant, quote and order processing, automated tender monitoring and scoring, outbound lead engagement, contract and legal analysis, and HR and onboarding. It is positioned to collaborate with staff rather than replace them, keeping critical decisions under human oversight, and is offered on a fixed-cost "Digital Working Units" (DWU) pricing model rather than variable token pricing. The platform integrates across email, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, SMS, and phone, and is presented as GDPR and EU AI Act compliant. Istante was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Kinro
providers.description: Kinro is an AI-powered commercial insurance brokerage for small businesses, founded in the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch and based in San Francisco. Its autonomous AI agents run the full broker workflow around the clock, from prospect identification and quote preparation through comparison, binding, and ongoing certificate and renewal servicing. Kinro targets the roughly 77% of the 36 million U.S. small businesses that are underinsured because traditional brokers cannot profitably serve low-premium accounts. It is licensed across 30 states, appointed by 15+ carriers with access to 50+ markets, and offers general liability, business owner's policies, workers' compensation, commercial auto and trucking, professional liability, cyber, and more. Kinro was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Kiva Systems (Amazon Robotics since 2012)
providers.description: Kiva Systems was a warehouse robotics company founded in 2003 that pioneered the goods-to-person mobile fulfillment model, in which fleets of low-profile drive units lift and carry mobile storage pods to human pick stations instead of moving workers to static shelving. Amazon acquired Kiva Systems in March 2012 for approximately US$775 million and renamed it Amazon Robotics in 2015. Since the acquisition the technology has been developed exclusively for Amazon's own fulfillment and sortation network and is no longer sold to third parties. Amazon Robotics publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; amazonrobotics.com now redirects to Amazon's internal identity provider and kivasystems.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical and acquisition record in the physical-AI and warehouse-robotics space rather than as an integratable API provider. Not to be confused with AWS RoboMaker or AWS IoT RoboRunner, which are AWS product APIs.

providers.name: Fourier Intelligence
providers.description: Fourier (Fourier Intelligence, founded 2015 and headquartered in Shanghai, China) is a full-stack robotics company that develops core robot technology and finished robot products. It began in rehabilitation robotics — exoskeletons and upper/lower-limb rehab devices such as the ArmMotus and ExoMotus lines and the RehabHub intelligent rehabilitation ecosystem — and has expanded into general-purpose humanoid robots (the GRx series, including GR-1 and GR-2), smart actuators (FSA), and dexterous hands. Fourier publishes first-party developer SDKs for robot control through its FFTAI GitHub organization: the RoCS (Robot Control System / General Robotics OS) client libraries for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, and the fourier-grx control stack for the GRx humanoid series. Fourier is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. These are device/robot-control developer libraries rather than a hosted web API; the company publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Mirana Toys
providers.description: Mirana Toys (Mirana Innovations Pvt Ltd) is an India-based smart-toy company and OEM/ODM manufacturer of electronic toys — RC cars, monster trucks, drones, educational toys, and AI/AR toys. It pairs its consumer products with the Mirana smart app (iOS and Android), a mobile gaming platform that lets kids and adults control and play with Mirana toys over Bluetooth. As an OEM partner it offers in-house PCB/PCBA design and SMT assembly, tooling and mold design, mobile app development, compliance support (ASTM, EN-71, RoHS, ISO, SMETA), and global logistics for toy brands and retailers. Backed by Accel. The company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and support center but no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Allen Control Systems
providers.description: Allen Control Systems is a defense technology company building autonomous precision weapon stations that detect, track, and neutralize unmanned aerial systems (drones) for military and partner forces. Its Bullfrog family of robotic gun mounts (M240C, M2, M230, M134) pairs passive machine-vision drone detection with autonomous fire-control targeting, synthetic training-data generation, and low-collateral engagement options such as laser dazzlers and composite rounds. The systems use an open architecture to integrate with command-and-control platforms. Backed by Craft Ventures, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a defense-sector provider; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or specification at this time.

providers.name: Aurelius Systems
providers.description: Aurelius Systems is a defense technology company building autonomous directed-energy laser defense platforms for counter-unmanned-aerial-system (C-UAS) missions. Its flagship product, Archimedes, fuses high-power lasers, advanced optical sensing, and AI-guided autonomous tracking into a compact, field-deployable platform that detects, tracks, and neutralizes Group 1 and Group 2 drone threats at the speed of light and a fraction of the cost of traditional interceptors. The system runs on grid, generator, or commercial off-the-shelf batteries, is designed to operate without human operators, and can be networked into modular defensive grids to protect troops, bases, and critical infrastructure. Founded in 2025 by Michael LaFramboise and John Marmaduke, the company raised a $10M seed round co-led by General Catalyst and Draper Associates and is partnered with American Rheinmetall. Aurelius currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface — it is a directed-energy hardware company.

providers.name: Brumby
providers.description: Brumby (formerly GrazeMate) is a Y Combinator-backed (W2026) precision-grazing company based in Sydney, Australia, building an autonomous drone toolkit for cattle ranchers. Brumby drones plan routes and move herds with gentle, AI-guided pressure, fly scheduled monitoring missions that locate and count every animal, measure standing dry-matter pasture biomass from the air, and inspect water troughs, tanks and fences on every flight — all managed from a single phone app that works online or in a local base-station mode without connectivity. The company is running pilot programs and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is a company lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Connected Robotics
providers.description: Connected Robotics Inc. is a Japanese foodtech startup, founded in 2014 by Tetsuya Sawanobori and headquartered in Koganei, Tokyo, that develops specialized robotics and AI systems to automate labor-intensive work across food factories and restaurants. Its product line pairs AI image-processing and robot-control technology with purpose-built machines including the Delibot S plating robot, Delibot X filling robot, AI inspection software, a soft-serve ice-cream robot, and a french-fry cooking robot, targeting labor shortages, productivity, and food safety. The company has raised multiple rounds (including a July 2019 Series A led by Global Brain and a Series B closed in 2023 with strategic investors such as Yaskawa Electric, Hoshizaki, and Mitsubishi HC Capital) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As a hardware and robotics manufacturer, Connected Robotics publishes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Crewline
providers.description: Crewline is an autonomous heavy-equipment company that retrofits existing construction machinery to operate self-driving. Its hardware retrofit kit installs on-site in about an hour and adds autonomy to drum rollers today (compatible with Caterpillar, Bomag, Hamm, Volvo, and CASE), with dozers on the 2027 roadmap and rock trucks, excavators, motor graders, and wheel loaders in development. It is offered on a subscription model with zero upfront cost, a fixed monthly rate per machine, and 24/7 technical support, targeting earthworks and grading crews. Crewline is backed by Initialized Capital and headquartered in San Francisco. It publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Cron Systems
providers.description: Cron Systems (now operating as Cron AI) builds deep-learning perception software for 3D sensor and LiDAR data. Its flagship platform, senseEDGE, performs real-time 3D object detection, classification, and tracking from point-cloud data at the edge, with multi-sensor fusion and adverse-weather resilience. The technology serves intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, autonomous mobility, smart cities, and security and surveillance — powering use cases such as traffic management, autonomous tolling, crowd and queue management, smart parking, vehicle counting, and airport and aircraft-movement monitoring. Object output is emitted as JSON and Flatbuffers binary over WebSocket, with a web-based configuration and visualizer utility, VPN and PTP time-synchronization support, and a privacy-preserving, GDPR-compliant design. Cron AI was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Cx2
providers.description: CX2 is a defense technology company building AI-enabled electromagnetic spectrum (electronic warfare) systems for the tactical edge. Founded in 2024 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, CX2 develops attritable, machine-learning-powered hardware and software that detect, disrupt, and geolocate RF threats across land, air, sea, and space. Its flagship products are Wraith, a roughly 32-pound autonomous airborne EW platform that geolocates and identifies hostile emitters such as jammers and radars in GPS-denied environments, and Vadris, an RF-seeking payload for FPV drones that hunts ground control stations and other emitters of interest. CX2 is backed by 8VC, Point72 Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and sells directly to military and government customers. It does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Dryft
providers.description: Dryft, Inc. is a Palo Alto, California startup building an AI operating system for manufacturing operations. The platform pairs context-aware, agent-based intelligence with mathematical optimization to mimic, optimize, and automate complex human decisions across the shop floor and supply chain. Dryft reads operational data from existing ERPs and inventory systems, identifies issues such as late items or stockouts, and autonomously recommends and executes actions like adjusting order quantities and safety stocks or following up with suppliers. The company frames this as a shift from static Enterprise Resource Planning to Enterprise Resource Automation, freeing planners to focus on strategy over administrative work. Founded in 2024 by CEO Anna-Julia Storch and CTO Leonie Freisinger, Dryft raised a $5M round led by General Catalyst with participation from Neo and Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners. Dryft does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation; this profile captures its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Elementary
providers.description: Elementary is an AI-powered machine-vision inspection company for manufacturing, founded in 2017 in South Pasadena, California (originally Elementary Robotics). Its VisionStream self-training edge AI detects production defects in seconds without rules, labeling, or tuning, while the QualityOS cloud platform delivers traceability, analytics, and MES/ERP integration across production lines. Elementary inspects over one billion parts annually for Fortune 500 manufacturers across food & beverage, automotive, consumer packaged goods, electronics, and life sciences, and is backed by Rockwell Automation, Tiger Global, Toyota Ventures, Threshold Ventures, Fika Ventures, and Idealab. The company exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Entalpic
providers.description: Entalpic is an AI-driven materials science company that designs molecules and materials for industrial processes by combining machine learning, atomistic simulations, and experimental feedback loops to engineer surfaces and materials at the atomic scale. Its work spans a Discovery Engine for high-throughput screening of chemical spaces, process modeling with ML-plus-CFD digital twins, and quantum/atomistic simulation for surface chemistry, applied to semiconductors and thin-film coatings, battery cathode and interface chemistry, catalysis and active-site design, and advanced specialty materials. Founded in 2024 with research roots at the Mila AI lab, the company is based at Station F in Paris and Mila in Montreal and raised an 8.5M euro seed round. Entalpic does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile tracks its public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fernride
providers.description: FERNRIDE (FERNRIDE GmbH) is a Munich, Germany based ground-autonomy company delivering human-assisted autonomous driving for logistics. Its platform automates electric and diesel trucks and terminal tractors across container terminals, yard operations, manufacturing supply, defence logistics, and open-road trucking, pairing on-vehicle autonomy with remote human oversight (teleoperation) for reliability at scale. A centralized Management Suite lets fleet managers monitor and control the autonomous fleet and integrates with existing terminal operating systems (TOS) and yard management systems (YMS). Customers and partners have included DB Schenker, Volkswagen, HHLA, and NVIDIA. FERNRIDE was acquired by Quantum Systems in December 2025. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest; the company exposes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Generative Engineering
providers.description: Generative Engineering (Generative Vision Ltd) is a London-based deep-tech startup, founded in 2021, building a platform that generates, tests, and simulates thousands of engineering designs in parallel, in a fraction of the time traditional processes take. A code-first integration framework lets engineers plug in their existing tools alongside out-of-the-box integrations, spanning concept engineering, systems integration, and cost engineering. Parallel engineering aims to radically cut product development time for real-world products across energy, decarbonization, agriculture, and mobility. The company is backed by a pre-seed round led by EQT Ventures with participation from Join Capital. It publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: IONA
providers.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Lydia AI
providers.description: Lydia AI is an enterprise AI company whose flagship platform, ORCA, reasons through complex operational problems and delivers structured work product rather than chat replies. ORCA spans three domains: Content & Commerce (generating product content, campaign assets, and structured search data), Evidence & Analysis (analyzing large document sets for legal discovery), and Operations & Logistics (optimizing routing, dispatch, and disruption response). The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Lydia AI exposes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API surface; engagement is via a book-a-demo/contact sales motion.

providers.name: Mach Industries
providers.description: Mach Industries develops and manufactures asymmetric aerospace and defense systems and components at scale, with a product portfolio that includes the Viper vertical-takeoff attack drone, the Glide precision strike munition, the Stratos high-altitude pseudo-satellite, the Pike long-range munition, the Dart counter-drone kinetic interceptor, and energetics testing services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The company is a defense hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: MeetFuture Technology
providers.description: MeetFuture Technology (弥费科技) is a Shanghai-based, global-leading supplier of semiconductor Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) and core components, founded in 2014. It designs and manufactures overhead hoist transport (OHT), stocker/storage, purge, and AMHS control-software solutions for semiconductor wafer fabrication plants, integrating with fab MES systems over SEMI equipment communication standards (E37/HSMS, E30/GEM, E82, E84, E10). MeetFuture holds 300+ intellectual-property items, operates China's largest AMHS cleanroom test center, authored China's first semiconductor OHT standard (T/SICA 006—2024), and won the 2025 SEMI Product Innovation Award. It is a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. MeetFuture is an industrial semiconductor-equipment maker and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery.

providers.name: Orqa
providers.description: Orqa is an aerial robotics company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Osijek, Croatia, that designs and manufactures mission-ready FPV (first-person view) drone systems for the defense and enterprise markets. With full vertical integration, Orqa builds every component in-house — tactical drones such as the MRM1-5 and MRM2-10, FPV goggles (FPV.One Pilot), controllers, simulators, and detection equipment — to keep its supply chain secure and its systems high-performance. The company is ISO 9001 certified and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (Seed round, 2024, partners Antoine Moyroud and Alexander Schmitt). As of this profile Orqa is a hardware manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a programmatic developer surface; this repository tracks it for identity and network completeness.

providers.name: Overland AI
providers.description: Overland AI is a Seattle- and Washington, DC-based defense technology company building autonomous ground vehicle systems for military and national-security applications. Its product line spans ULTRA (a fully autonomous tactical vehicle with modular payloads), OverDrive (an off-road autonomy stack for tactical maneuver in GPS- and comms-denied environments), OverWatch (a command-and-control platform for single-operator control of multiple ground vehicles, which the company describes as offering an open API for integration with existing C2 systems), and SPARK (modular hardware that adds autonomous mobility to existing platforms). Overland AI is a portfolio company of 8VC. The company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; its "open API" is referenced only in marketing material and integration is handled through direct contact.

providers.name: PopCom
providers.description: PopCom is an AI-powered automated retail technology company founded by e-commerce entrepreneur Dawn Dickson. Its flagship product, the PopShop, is a robotic self-service kiosk that dispenses physical and digital products while capturing customer data through computer vision, facial recognition, and real-time analytics. The platform gives brands and entrepreneurs the kind of sales metrics, inventory monitoring, targeted advertising, and customer-sentiment insight that online retailers enjoy, but for physical, unattended retail. PopCom sells its hardware on an annual lease with a monthly software subscription. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass PopCom publishes no public developer platform, API, or specification.

providers.name: Savion Aerospace
providers.description: Savion Aerospace (FlySavion) is an aerospace company developing sustainable, zero-emissions aviation technology. Its flagship SavionJet is an autonomous blended-wing-body (ABWB) aircraft with a standup cabin and satellite-based piloting via proprietary autonomous flight software, and the company offers Zero-Emissions Flight Credits (ZFCs) as a subscription for organizations seeking carbon-free air travel beyond offsetting. Savion demonstrated a cryogenic LNG-fueled flight in 2019 and is a 500 Global (500 Startups) and Alchemist Accelerator portfolio company. The company operates as an aviation hardware and services business and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Simr
providers.description: Simr (a registered trademark of The UberCloud, Inc., based in Los Altos, California) is a Simulation Operations Automation (SimOps) platform that streamlines complex engineering simulations across the product-development lifecycle. It provides self-service, automated infrastructure for running CFD, FEA, multi-physics, and system-level simulations with major solvers such as ANSYS, Abaqus, and COMSOL, deploying directly into customer-owned cloud environments on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, or on-premises. Simr targets enterprise manufacturers, reducing operational overhead for engineering teams while keeping data control and compliance security-first. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Earlybird and profiled in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Simr publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: Vermeer
providers.description: Vermeer is an American-Ukrainian defense-technology startup (founded 2018 by Brian Streem; headquartered in New York with forward operations in Kyiv) building vision-based autonomy for unmanned aerial platforms. Its Visual Positioning System (VPS) uses electro-optical and infrared cameras plus onboard AI (NVIDIA) to match imagery to 2D/3D maps and deliver precise navigation in GPS-denied, jammed, or spoofed environments. Products include Air (absolute positioning without GPS), Celestial (star-based navigation), and Terminal Guidance (precision targeting). The technology has been fielded by the Armed Forces of Ukraine and is aimed at defense customers including Lockheed Martin, General Atomics, Northrop Grumman, and the U.S. Air Force and Army. Vermeer exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time; this profile is a company/marketing surface with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Vitesse
providers.description: Vitesse is a universal physical-AI platform for industrial machines, founded by the team behind Tesla's "Model 3 automation hell" fix alongside leaders from SpaceX, Siemens, and Safran. It connects any machine - Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, and legacy PLCs - through 135 native OT connectors, generates control logic from a natural-language description of a process (up to 15x faster than traditional PLC programming), and runs the full stack at the edge on purpose-built industrial controllers with no cloud required. The platform layers hardware, live data dashboards and SCADA views, interoperability, physical AI, and zero-trust OT/IT cybersecurity (NIS2 and NIST aligned) into one stack, with real-time browser-based monitoring across 800,000+ machine hours. Vitesse exposes a marketing website and a login-gated product application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Andustry
providers.description: Andustry is an AI-native industrial equipment broker that streamlines sourcing and procurement for manufacturers. The platform combines AI-powered supplier discovery with manual qualification and commercial negotiation to source industrial machines (CNC mills, lathes, press brakes, laser cutters, robotic cells), machined/forged/cast parts, and robotics and electronics across Europe, China, India, and the United States. Clients hand off a sourcing need and Andustry returns a verified supplier shortlist within 24-48 hours, delivering an average of roughly 30% cost savings and 2x faster sourcing timelines on a commission-only basis with no subscription. Founded in 2026 (Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch) by Het Dave and Johann Stuerken and operated as Andustry GmbH.

providers.name: Efference AI
providers.description: Efference AI is a robotics perception and compute company building the hardware-plus-software foundation for data-driven robotics at scale. Founded in 2025 by Gianluca Bencomo and based in San Francisco (Y Combinator Fall 2025), Efference treats machine vision as a software problem, pairing affordable stereo-camera hardware with learned 3D-perception foundation models ("cheap hardware + great algorithms"). Its M1 device targets distributed, robotics-grade data collection at scale, while the H1 stereo system is built for real-time cloud inference with foundation models. The company serves autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots, and drones, and publishes hardware-interfacing documentation and firmware through its GitHub organization. As of this profile Efference exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or authenticated service surface.

providers.name: Mandolin
providers.description: Mandolin (operating as Coral Automation, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based AI automation platform for specialty pharmaceutical workflows, serving infusion centers and specialty pharmacies. Its AI agents handle the complete back-office lifecycle — patient intake, benefits verification, prior authorization, claims, and revenue cycle management — by navigating existing systems, reading faxes, and reasoning over data rather than through developer integrations. The company explicitly markets a no-API, no-integration approach ("Every step, fully automated"), citing outcomes such as 24x faster document processing and eliminated prescription backlogs. Backed by Greylock and SV Angel.

providers.name: Simile
providers.description: Simile is a simulation platform for human behavior. Its AI-driven simulations show how and why customers, employees, or populations respond to change, so enterprise teams can find their audience, reach niche populations, de-risk decisions, segment sentiment at scale, and test concepts before a real-world launch. Simile is building a foundation model that predicts human behavior and a product that deploys it at scale. It raised a $100M Series A led by Index Ventures and is backed by Bain Capital Ventures; named customers include CVS Health, Wealthfront, Suntory, Garnett Station Partners, and Banco Itau.

providers.name: Agile Loop L.L.C.
providers.description: Agile Loop L.L.C. is a London-founded enterprise AI company (founded 2023, backed by 500 Global) building Large Action Models — action-first foundation models trained on thousands of software interfaces so AI agents can operate any user interface and execute multi-step workflows end-to-end from natural-language instructions. Its product suite spans Sector Fusion (telecom network analytics), an Intelligent Evaluation Platform (AI scoring and fraud detection), LLM Ops (governance for LLM applications), an Aviation Ops Suite, and SAM-X (natural-language Excel automation), alongside the open-source Synapse Copilot toolkit for connecting LLMs to APIs and an embeddable Copilot widget for SaaS products. Agile Loop publishes no public OpenAPI, developer portal, or versioned client SDKs at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Alba Robot
providers.description: ALBA Robot is a Turin, Italy based autonomous micro-mobility company building a fleet of self-driving robots for indoor and pedestrian spaces such as airports, hospitals, and large facilities. Its product line includes ALBA One, ALBA Ride, ALBA Ride +, and the ALBA Caddie autonomous baggage transport robot, and it layers digital services such as Digital Twins and Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH) advertising on top of the mobility platform. ALBA Robot runs pilots and deployments with airports including Cagliari, London Gatwick, Dallas, Milan, Turin, and Dubai (with dnata), and operates from Turin with a US presence in Detroit, Michigan. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or GitHub organization; it is a hardware/robotics fleet operator rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Apex.AI
providers.description: Apex.AI is an embedded and autonomous software company whose tagline is "software that moves," focused on safe, real-time, software-defined systems (SDx) for automotive, robotics, and other safety-critical embedded platforms. Its product line includes Apex.Grace (deterministic embedded execution framework, an automotive-grade evolution of ROS 2), Apex.Ida (high-speed fault-tolerant middleware for sensor, compute, and cloud connectivity), Apex.OS for V&V (data recording and replay for validating autonomous systems), and Apex.Alan (automated tooling and CI/CD workflows for safe software development at scale). Apex.AI also provides technical assessment, architecture, embedded and cloud software development, CI/CD pipeline, and ROS 1 to ROS 2 migration services. The company is a maintainer of substantial ROS 2 and embedded middleware open source. It is backed by Canaan Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Apex.AI publishes no public developer REST API at this time.

providers.name: Jifflenow
providers.description: Jifflenow is a B2B meeting automation and scheduling platform for trade shows, conferences, and corporate events, now part of Cvent (acquired 2021) as Cvent Jifflenow. It lets sales and event teams request, approve, and confirm meetings before attendees arrive on the show floor, with automated routing and notifications, a unified calendar that combines customer meetings and internal staff activities, on-site mobile check-in and no-show tracking, and reporting dashboards that tie meeting volume and outcomes back to pipeline. It integrates with Salesforce (native CRM sync of accounts, opportunities, campaigns, and leads), Outlook, and iCapture badge scanning. The standalone jifflenow.com now redirects to Cvent; there is no public first-party developer API, SDK, or documentation surface for Jifflenow as a distinct product.

providers.name: Aerialoop
providers.description: Aerialoop is a drone technology and urban logistics company that designs, builds, and operates intelligent aerial networks for cargo delivery, surveillance, and infrastructure inspection. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Miami with operations rooted in Quito, Ecuador, it is one of the fastest-growing drone delivery operations in Latin America. Its ALT 6-8 delivery drone carries a 5kg payload for urban logistics, while the ALT 6-ISR line adds HD, infrared, and night-vision cameras with AI-powered intrusion detection; extended-range variants operate up to 120km using LEO satellite connectivity for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights. The company has completed over 50,000 flights across six countries. Aerialoop is a Techstars Miami (powered by J.P. Morgan) portfolio company. It currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Trucks Venture Fund I
providers.description: Trucks Venture Capital (Trucks VC) is an early-stage venture firm headquartered in San Francisco investing in companies building the future of transportation — making mobility decarbonized, safer, and more accessible. Its focus spans autonomous vehicles, electric aviation, agricultural robotics, fleet management, and mobility infrastructure. Trucks Venture Fund I is the firm's first fund; notable portfolio outcomes include Joby Aviation (NYSE: JOBY), Bear Flag Robotics (acquired by John Deere), nuTonomy (acquired by Delphi), Roadster (acquired by CDK Global), and Zendrive (acquired by Intuit). Surfaced as a portfolio relation of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital firm; it publishes a marketing/portfolio website but no developer API surface.

providers.name: Blendid
providers.description: Blendid operates fully autonomous robotic smoothie kiosks that prepare chef-created blended beverages from real whole fruits, vegetables, seeds, nuts, and juice with no artificial flavors or added sugar. Each kiosk uses AI and robotics to run without on-site staff, taking mobile-app orders with customization and payment, producing up to eight simultaneous drinks and roughly thirty per hour. Blendid deploys its Blendid M2 platform into retail, colleges and universities, health clubs, and hospitals as a low-labor, low-capex, 24/7 automated food-service offering. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech in the Food & Agritech sector; the company publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: CODEOWNERS
providers.description: CODEOWNERS is the file format originally introduced by GitHub and later adopted by GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Gitea, and Azure Repos that lets a repository declare which individuals or teams are responsible for a path or pattern within the codebase. Platforms use it to auto-request reviews on pull/merge requests, enforce required approvals via branch protection or push rules, and route pings on issues. The file is plain text with one rule per line - a glob pattern followed by one or more owner handles (`@username` or `@org/team`) or email addresses. Comments start with `#` and the last matching pattern wins.

providers.name: Dotterel
providers.description: Dotterel Technologies is an Auckland, New Zealand acoustics and audio-hardware company founded in 2015 out of the Callaghan Innovation C-Prize. It began by solving drone noise, building acoustic shrouds, low-noise propellers, and onboard active audio-recording systems for UAVs used in film, security, and noise mapping. That work led to Konos (now marketed as Konos Digital), an 80-element directional MEMS microphone array with a continuously variable 60-300 degree beam width that streams four channels of AES67 / SMPTE ST 2110 audio over a single Power-over-Ethernet cable, targeting film, broadcast, and live-sports production. The microphone exposes a firmware-updatable on-device HTTP control interface (a web page plus a POST control endpoint for beam steering) rather than a public developer web API. Dotterel is backed by Techstars (Adelaide 2017 cohort) and is tracked here as a hardware company; it publishes no public API specification, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Edra
providers.description: Edra is an AI automation platform that analyzes an organization's existing business data - tickets, logs, messages, and system records - to automatically discover and document how operational processes actually run, then turns that knowledge into workflows that AI agents can execute reliably. The company targets knowledge-intensive functions such as IT service management and technical support, and integrates with common enterprise systems including ServiceNow, JIRA, Zendesk, Salesforce, and Outlook. Edra was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Edra publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: KEENON Robotics
providers.description: KEENON Robotics is a global commercial service-robotics company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, designing and manufacturing autonomous service robots deployed across more than 70 countries and 600+ cities. Its product lines span catering and delivery robots (the T-series and W3), the KLEENBOT commercial floor-cleaning range (C20/C30/C40/C55), heavy-load delivery robots (S100/S300), humanoid service robots (XMAN-R1/XMAN-F1), hospital and hotel logistics solutions (including the WITMED medical line), and the Keenmow K1 domestic robot.
