KEENON is a hardware-and-solutions company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Procuri
providers.description: Procuri (procuri.ai) presents itself as an AI-powered procurement automation platform that uses specialized AI agents to discover and vet suppliers, optimize contract negotiation and pricing, monitor policy and regulatory compliance, and assess supplier and market risk for enterprise procurement teams. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass the public site publishes no developer/API surface (no docs, developer, API-reference, or OpenAPI pages resolve).

providers.name: sento
providers.description: sento is a Munich-based B2B software company (sento GmbH) building a cloud-based EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) platform that automates complex business-partner processes, letting companies replace slow, manual partner-integration workflows with automated document and data exchange. Founded by Nimar Blume and Felix Krauth and backed by Insight Partners, sento raised a EUR 9 million seed round to expand its partner-onboarding and document-automation product. As of this profile sento does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation - only its corporate marketing site and legal pages are publicly available.

providers.name: TRIC Robotics
providers.description: TRIC Robotics builds autonomous agricultural robots that replace chemical pesticides with ultraviolet light. Its flagship platform, Luna, is a tractor-scale robot that roams California strawberry fields after dark, using UV-C light to kill fungal pathogens such as powdery mildew and botrytis while a mechanical "Bug Vac" removes pests like Lygus bugs, spotted wing drosophila, and spider mites — without a single drop of pesticide. Founded in 2017 by Dr. Adam Stager and Vishnu Somasundaram out of the University of Delaware and now based in California, TRIC operates a robotics-as-a-service model that requires no upfront investment from growers, and reports pesticide reductions of up to 70% across the farms it serves. The company raised a $5.5M seed round led by Version One Ventures to expand its fleet across Santa Maria, Oxnard, and Watsonville. TRIC Robotics is an agricultural robotics operator and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Zeromatter
providers.description: Zeromatter is a deep-tech simulation platform that lets teams build, test, and train autonomous systems in one environment. It provides high-performance sensor simulation, automatic environment generation, and multi-agent co-simulation frameworks used to accelerate development across autonomy, aerospace, automotive, agriculture, drones, and green energy. Backed by Spark Capital, Zeromatter currently exposes a marketing and company site only; no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a lead pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Bioyond Robotics
providers.description: Bioyond Robotics (奔曜科技) is a life-sciences intelligent-automation company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Shanghai's Zhangjiang Science City. It combines robotics, machine vision, and artificial intelligence to build autonomous laboratory solutions for scientific research, drug discovery, applied chemistry, synthetic biology, multiomics, and clinical diagnostics. Its product line spans the LabGenius robot platform (liquid-handling and transport robots), the LabMate automation platform (material/liquid handling, stackers, and intelligent scheduling), the LabMind laboratory software platform for integrating external instruments and modules, and the BIOYOND AutoSeq genetic-analysis system. Bioyond is backed by Qiming Venture Partners. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this record captures its identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Mips
providers.description: MIPS is a processor IP and compute company building embedded and edge AI silicon for automotive, robotics, and mission-critical systems. Its portfolio spans the MIPS RISC-V CPU families (M8500, I8500, P8700, S8200), the ARC processor and NPX/VPX accelerator lines, and development tooling such as MIPS Atlas Explorer virtual platforms and the ASIP Designer / ASIP Programmer toolchains. MIPS frames its offering around a "Sense, Think, Act, Communicate" signal chain for real-time autonomy — what it calls Physical AI at the edge. MIPS is a semiconductor IP licensor rather than a public web-API provider; this profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched with identity and probed security posture.

providers.name: Rhyme (fka PriorAuthNow)
providers.description: Rhyme (formerly PriorAuthNow) is a healthcare technology company that eliminates prior authorization burden by automating the exchange between payers and providers. Its platform delivers touchless prior authorization, gold carding (removing auth requirements entirely through payer-provider collaboration), and a shared dashboard for tracking efficiency. Rhyme processes over four million prior authorizations annually and connects 83 of the largest US health systems with 300+ payers. The company is backed by Insight Partners and was surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; it publishes no public developer or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Zudo
providers.description: Zudo builds AI-powered agents purpose-built for the warranty industry, automating customer service and back-office operations for home warranty, auto warranty, and OEM third-party administrators. Its agents (Adam for customer service, Emma for operations) handle claim follow-ups, initiations, and authorizations around the clock to improve warranty customer experience and operating margins. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; the public site is marketing-only with no developer/API surface published at enrichment time.

providers.name: dopl technologies
providers.description: Dopl Technologies is a Seattle-based data and AI company (founded 2022, Techstars-backed) democratizing access to diagnostic exams and interventional procedures through telerobotic ultrasound. Its Dopl Traverse platform and SonoFlex app let a remote sonographer operate an ultrasound probe over a network from significant distances, extending specialist-level imaging into rural and workforce-constrained regions. Field testing in rural Washington hospitals has reduced patient wait times by over 90 percent. The company cites 50M+ missed ultrasound exams annually and $19.5B in lost revenue from unequal imaging access, and expects FDA clearance in 2027 before expanding into minimally invasive procedures. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation; this record is a network stub maintained for discovery and future enrichment.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: Anki
providers.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: Vsim
providers.description: Vsim (Vsim Technology Ltd) is a Manchester, UK physics-simulation startup founded in 2022 by ex-NVIDIA simulation engineers Michelle Lu (CEO) and Kier Storey (CTO). The company builds a next-generation physics simulation platform and an end-to-end reinforcement-learning training framework for robotics, reporting up to 100x training performance speed-ups over existing solutions, with applications across robotics, AI, visual effects, aerodynamics, gaming, and e-commerce. Vsim raised a $21.5M seed round led by EQT Ventures (total ~$24M). It does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Auxos
providers.description: Auxos is an AI-powered customer research platform that builds 1:1 AI clones of a company's real customers to simulate how they respond to business decisions before those decisions ship. The company recruits and interviews real people matching a client's ideal customer profile, then models each participant as an always-on AI avatar grounded in that interview data. Teams use the resulting synthetic audience to test surveys, messaging, ad creative, pricing, and product flows and retrieve population-scale quantitative results plus qualitative commentary in minutes rather than the weeks traditional market research takes. Auxos is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company founded by Ashton Daniel, Jerry Wu, and Kerry Lu, targeting marketing, product, and research teams. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist; as of enrichment Auxos publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Ciridae
providers.description: Ciridae is building an AI-native operating system for services businesses — the industrial, construction, and field-service companies that make up the real economy. Its platform replaces fragmented ERPs and spreadsheets with a unified system that automates core business operations across project management, financials, CRM, accounts payable and receivable, and reporting, while keeping humans in the loop to oversee AI decisions. Modules span AI-generated field workforce scheduling, vendor onboarding and compliance, automated payment workflows, and customer order expediting, typically deployed in a two-to-four-week implementation with embedded engineers. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, Ciridae is backed by Accel. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Doxel
providers.description: Doxel is a Menlo Park, California construction technology company providing AI-powered observability and progress tracking for large capital projects. Founded in 2015 by CEO Saurabh Ladha, the company combines 360-degree reality capture (via Insta360 X5 hardware partnership) with computer vision models that compare site video against BIM models to automatically quantify work-in-place by trade, system, and stage. The platform layers a "rules of credit" engine on top of those quantities to drive earned-value, schedule, and budget analytics — including 3D Progress View, Production Rates, Schedule (a visual Gantt replacement), Utilities Underground Tracking from drone imagery, and Portfolio-level dashboards. Doxel uses advanced language models to map schedule line items to physical progress and supports Procore-style construction management workflows, with deployments across data centers, healthcare, semiconductor fabs, and EV battery factories. Doxel has raised approximately $57M from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and counts 18 of the top 30 U.S. general contractors, 14 of the top 20 data center developers, and 3 of 4 hyperscalers as customers. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or GitHub organization — the platform is delivered as a managed SaaS application at app.doxel.ai with hardware-assisted capture and enterprise integrations arranged via direct engagement.

providers.name: Maquoketa Research
providers.description: Maquoketa Research is a defense-technology startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building autonomous terminal-guidance systems for one-way attack drones. Its platform-agnostic guidance modules add custom computer-vision object tracking to low-cost FPV drone hardware, raising strike success rates from under 25% to roughly 80% while maintaining target lock through GPS jamming and signal loss. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the five-person team ships hardware modules (product lines include GCS, Magpie, Odin, and TGS) that integrate with existing drone flight controllers rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; it currently exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Syntropy
providers.description: Syntropy is an autonomous, agentic coding application built for complex, long-horizon software engineering tasks. A developer describes a feature in natural language and Syntropy plans, writes, and tests the implementation, returning a production-ready pull request without the developer having to manage a terminal or an IDE agent session by hand. The product emphasizes large-context handling for heavy, real-world codebases ("no context ceiling, no truncation"), supports custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations so it can pull in a team's own tools, and joins Slack to post updates as tasks complete. Syntropy is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in San Francisco, founded by Saahil Sundaresan and Andrew Kuik. As of this profile it ships as a hosted end-user coding product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Atlas
providers.description: Atlas is an AI implementation partner built for independent accounting firms, deploying supervised, firm-specific AI "junior accountants" that automate repetitive, data-intensive workflows such as client onboarding, follow-ups, bookkeeping, compliance, and financial reporting while keeping human accountants in control of every decision and client relationship. Founded by Arpit Maheshwari (CEO) and Jagmal Singh (CTO) and co-led by Accel and Stellaris with Felicis participation, Atlas raised a $6M seed round in 2026 to scale its network of partner firms across North America. Atlas is currently a services-led AI company and publishes no public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Birdstop
providers.description: Birdstop is an American autonomous-drone and remote-sensing company that lets organizations monitor and inspect field assets at scale without personnel onsite. Its Fealty system is an all-weather, always-on drone that launches in under three seconds, flies for up to 45 minutes, cruises at 45 mph, and patrols 24/7 across public safety, utilities, transportation, construction, and data-center sites. Birdstop pairs networked UAVs and ground stations with computer vision and a patented optical/acoustic detect-and-avoid system to enable safe beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight under some of the FAA's most advanced approvals, delivering Observation-on-Demand intel over the internet. The company is FAA-authorized, SOC 2 certified, and NDAA compliant, and builds its drones in Detroit. Backed by Techstars, Birdstop currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Blue River Technology
providers.description: Blue River Technology is an agricultural robotics and machine-learning company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and a wholly owned subsidiary of John Deere (Deere & Company), which acquired it in 2017. Founded in 2011 by Jorge Heraud and Lee Redden out of Stanford University, the company builds intelligent machinery that combines computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and full-stack software to make farming more precise and sustainable. Its flagship product, See & Spray, uses onboard cameras and deep-learning models to distinguish crops from weeds in real time and target herbicide only where it is needed, dramatically reducing chemical use. Blue River operates as John Deere's autonomy and computer-vision engineering hub, applying the same perception and edge-AI stack across agriculture, construction, and mining equipment. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its technology ships embedded in John Deere machinery and is surfaced to growers through John Deere Operations Center rather than a standalone developer program.

providers.name: Cofia
providers.description: Cofia is an AI automation platform that learns how a team actually works and automatically builds custom workflow automations without manual setup. By monitoring system events and recognizing repetitive patterns, Cofia proposes and assembles custom agents for tasks like prospect list building, outreach and follow-ups, recruiting pipeline management, and data report creation. The company markets itself as "AI automations that implement themselves." Cofia is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in New York City, founded by Moses Wayne (formerly Engineering Director at Duolingo) and Paola Martinez (formerly Senior Product Manager at Brilliant.org). It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched with what the company publishes publicly. As of this pass Cofia exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Flexion
providers.description: Flexion Robotics builds the autonomy stack for humanoid robots — from command to control, from manipulation to locomotion, across any hardware and task. Founded by former NVIDIA and ETH Zurich reinforcement-learning researchers (Nikita Rudin, David Höller, Julian Nubert), the Zurich- and San Francisco-based company uses large-scale simulation and reinforcement learning to train generalizable robot policies that transfer to real-world hardware. Its Flexion Reflect model line targets long-horizon autonomous humanoid work. The company raised $50M and is backed by Prosus Ventures. Flexion does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: GitOps
providers.description: A operational framework that takes DevOps best practices used for application development such as version control, collaboration, compliance, and CI/CD, and applies them to infrastructure automation. GitOps uses Git as a single source of truth for declarative infrastructure and applications.

providers.name: Isengard Industries Inc
providers.description: Isengard Industries builds sovereign production capability for defense: the means for allied nations to manufacture precision-strike and counter-drone (counter-UAS) systems by the thousand, on their own soil, at a fraction of what traditional prime contractors charge. The company describes its approach as "Weapons of Mass Production." Founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch, it is led by Francisco Serra-Martins (previously co-founder/CEO of Terminal Autonomy) and James Tennant (former Australian Army officer), and is headquartered in San Francisco. As a hardware and defense-manufacturing company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Machindustries
providers.description: Mach Industries develops and manufactures asymmetric aerospace and defense systems and components, aiming to produce them by the millions to deter conflict and advance prosperity. Its product line includes Viper (a turbojet vertical-takeoff attack drone), Glide and Pike precision strike munitions, Stratos high-altitude platforms, Dart counter-drone interceptors, and an Energetics propulsion and explosives testing practice. The company is a Khosla Ventures portfolio company. It is a hardware and manufacturing business with no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company identity and monitoring.

providers.name: newmo
providers.description: newmo (newmo株式会社, "ニューモ") is a Japanese mobility company with the mission "移動で地域をカラフルに" — coloring regions through movement. It modernizes regional transportation through a consumer ride-hailing app and taxi service (newmo-taxi.jp), driver recruitment and dispatch, and its newmo Autonomy initiative (newmo.ai), which since 2025 has run Level 4 autonomous-driving taxi trials spanning safety, remote monitoring, operations design, and vehicle integration. newmo is a consumer transportation service rather than a developer/API platform; probing found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. Backed by DCM Ventures.

providers.name: Nimble Robotics
providers.description: Nimble Robotics (Nimble) is an autonomous robotic third-party logistics (3PL) company building AI-powered robots that pick, pack, and fulfill ecommerce orders with minimal human intervention. Founded by Simon Kalouche, the company operates fully autonomous robotic fulfillment centers and is training general-purpose robot AI to power fast, economical commerce. Backed by Accel and partnered with FedEx, Nimble raised a $106M Series C at a $1B valuation, with board member Marc Raibert (Boston Dynamics founder). Nimble is a physical robotics and logistics operator and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: RIVR
providers.description: RIVR (RIVR Technologies AG, formerly Swiss-Mile) is a Swiss robotics and AI company spun out of ETH Zurich that develops autonomous legged-wheeled robots for doorstep delivery across parcel, grocery, and instant food/convenience segments. RIVR pursues "General Physical AI" by combining large-scale reinforcement learning in simulation with real-world self-supervised learning from live delivery operations, owning the full stack from software to hardware for reliability, safety, and cost efficiency. The company operates commercial deployments with partners including Just Eat Takeaway.com, Swiss Post, Migros Online, Evri, and Veho, and is backed by investors including Hongshan and Bezos Expeditions. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record; RIVR publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Slip Robotics
providers.description: Slip Robotics is an Atlanta, Georgia-based robotics company that builds SlipBots, autonomous omnidirectional Automated Loading Robots (ALRs) that load and unload any truck trailer in about five minutes without a forklift ever entering the trailer. Each SlipBot carries up to eight pallets and roughly six tons, cutting driver dwell time from around ninety minutes to five while reducing material-handling damage and loading-dock accidents. The company also offers SlipLift, a platform that extends autonomous trailer loading and unloading to heavier freight and regional and last-mile routes. Slip Robotics markets its robots-as-a-service offering as requiring no IT integration, is backed by DCVC, and won Best New Innovation in supply chain technology at MODEX 2024. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Third Dimension AI
providers.description: Third Dimension AI is a spatial-generation company building high-fidelity 3D worlds and simulation for embodied AI, autonomy, robotics, gaming, and entertainment. Its core product, SuperSim, models the world across the full fidelity spectrum - from real-world reconstruction of scenes captured from sensor data to open-ended generative simulation - so autonomy teams can validate, train, and deploy AI systems and close the simulation-to-reality domain gap without hand-built 3D art. Founded by Tolga Kart (CEO) and Piotr Sokolski (CTO), with Oxford professor Christian Rupprecht as Chief Researcher, the team draws on experience from Wayve, Tesla, Google, Luma AI, Nvidia, Niantic, Amazon, and Unity. The company raised $7 million and is backed by Felicis. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; enrichment captured its identity and probed its domain security posture.

providers.name: Waabi
providers.description: Waabi is a Toronto-based artificial intelligence company founded in 2021 by Raquel Urtasun, pioneering Physical AI for autonomous driving and starting with self-driving trucks. Its flagship product, the Waabi Driver, pairs a generative-AI, end-to-end interpretable and verifiable autonomy stack with sensors and compute, trained and validated in Waabi World, a high-fidelity neural closed-loop simulator, and designed for factory-level OEM integration and large-scale commercialization. Waabi is a product/technology company: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Akara
providers.description: Akara is a healthcare automation company building AI-powered systems for the operating room and clinical environments. Its platform combines the Akara AI Sensor, a thermal-only computer-vision system that passively tracks surgical and procedure events without capturing identifiable patient data (named to TIME's Best Inventions list); the Akara AI Platform, which delivers real-time OR monitoring, automated alerts, interactive dashboards, analytics, and Clara, an AI chat assistant for exploring surgical data and optimizing scheduling; and the Akara UV Robot (Violet), a fully autonomous UV-C disinfection robot that generates 3D UV dose maps and disinfects occupied clinical spaces up to six times faster than manual cleaning. Akara is trusted by hospitals across Europe and the US. The company does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: AutoStore
providers.description: AutoStore is a global warehouse robotics and technology company headquartered in Nedre Vats, Norway, that pioneered the cube storage automated storage and retrieval system (AS/RS). Its goods-to-person solution combines autonomous robots, an aluminum storage grid of stacked bins, workstation ports, and controlling software (marketed as CubeVerse, spanning design, simulation, operations, and predictive diagnostics) to fulfill orders in a fraction of the floor space of conventional warehouses. With more than 1,950 systems deployed across nearly 65 countries, AutoStore serves retail, grocery, 3PL, healthcare, and industrial customers. Systems are distributed, designed, installed, and serviced through a global network of qualified system integrators rather than a public developer/API program. AutoStore was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Basis Set Ventures
providers.description: Basis Set Ventures is an AI-native, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2017 by Dr. Lan Xuezhao and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. The firm invests at the seed and early stages in founders building artificial intelligence across AI infrastructure, autonomous systems, molecular and materials discovery, agentic development tooling, intelligent collaboration, and automated workflows. Basis Set announced a $250M Fund IV and describes itself as "the first capital when it's just you and your vision," pairing capital with an operator-led founder concierge team. Portfolio companies include Path Robotics, Quince, Sakana AI, Tigris Data, Mem0, OpenArt, Cusp, Simular, Vizcom, and Entire. This is an API Evangelist network profile of the firm; Basis Set Ventures does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so this record captures firm identity, web properties, and derived security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Beyond Imagination
providers.description: Beyond Imagination, Inc. is a Los Angeles based robotics and artificial intelligence company founded in January 2018 by Dr. Harry Kloor and Dr. Ray Kurzweil, building general-purpose humanoid robots and the AI software stack that runs them. Its flagship platform is Beomni, a wheeled humanoid robot with an articulated upper body and dexterous hands that can be teleoperated through VR headsets and haptic gloves or run autonomously. The software side is marketed as four products: AURA (Adaptive Unified Robotic/Human Administrator), a universal operating system for coordinating robots, humans and infrastructure across manufacturing ecosystems; ARCANA, an LLM-free synthetic brain architecture for real-time perception, decision making and coordination; Expert Minds, modular AI job modules trained for specialized roles such as chemical handling, bio-reactor operation, surgical prep and warehouse logistics; and Hive Mind Intelligence, a fleet learning layer where robots upload new skills to a shared cloud memory. The company has run pilot programs in commercial kitchens, laboratory work, healthcare and pharmaceutical manufacturing, and announced a manufacturing partnership with Korean electronics manufacturer Dreamtech. As of this profiling pass Beyond Imagination publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs or MCP/agent surface; its public web presence is a marketing site only.

providers.name: Rollup AI
providers.description: Rollup is a browser-based, real-time collaboration platform for engineering teams building complex hardware. It supports the full hardware development lifecycle across modular tools for systems engineering, systems modeling, requirements management, technical documentation, CAD viewing, and design reviews, with modules that interlink so changes propagate across a project. Rollup markets first-class APIs and developer-friendly features so teams can integrate it into new and existing systems; the platform exposes a REST API (authenticated with API keys or OAuth tokens) with pagination and websockets. Rollup serves early-stage hardware companies from small satellite builders to robotics firms, and offers Self-hosted and GovCloud options for ITAR/EAR export-controlled data. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Thiel Capital ($5.6M seed) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company.

providers.name: Traderion
providers.description: Traderion is a fintech company that combines technology and gamification to build digital learning platforms for banks and financial institutions. Its products include a gamified sales and trading simulator covering equities, FX, bonds, and commodities with AI-powered feedback, a MiFID II regulatory-compliance training platform built as a virtual simulated bank, and a risk-profiling platform for identifying and detecting risky behavioral patterns within organizations. A Seedcamp portfolio company, Traderion does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Avea Robotics
providers.description: Avea Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics software company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building teleoperation software that lets operators control robots from anywhere in the world with ultra-low latency. Its product, Sentinel, provides real-time remote control, immersive viewing, haptic feedback, and multi-stream video so operators can remotely intervene and keep robots running continuously. The platform supports industrial robotic arms, humanoid robots, and custom systems, and targets use cases such as data collection for Physical AI training, remote real-world robot deployment, and supervised autonomy with human oversight. Integration is handled during onboarding by sharing a robot's URDF and joint control API rather than through a public developer API. As an early-stage startup, Avea Robotics publishes a website, Notion-hosted documentation, and a Substack blog, but does not yet expose a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a self-serve developer platform.

providers.name: Byanat
providers.description: Byanat is an Oman-based, award-winning AI company offering a unified platform for optimizing digital infrastructure across telecommunications networks and data centers. The platform pairs system-wide visibility with custom-tailored automation to scale operations, ensure compliance, and promote sustainability, an approach the company frames as "Infrastructure 4.0." Its product families span mobile network solutions (site management, degradation detection, auto-discovery, performance analytics), data centre solutions (predictive analytics, capacity forecasting, energy management, infrastructure monitoring), and an API and integration layer for cross-platform connectivity and AI-powered workflow automation. Byanat is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference; its API and integration capability is delivered as a managed product.

providers.name: Pax Historia
providers.description: Pax Historia is an alternate-history sandbox game backed by Y Combinator, where players explore branching "what if" scenarios and reshape the course of history through open-ended, simulation-driven play. It is a consumer-facing game product reached at paxhistoria.co with a single "Get Started" entry point; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer platform, API, SDKs, documentation, pricing page, or other machine-readable API surface. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead surfaced from the Y Combinator portfolio and enriched here with verified identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Espressive
providers.description: Espressive is an enterprise conversational-AI company whose flagship product, Barista, is a GenAI-based virtual support agent that automates the resolution of employee questions, issues, and requests across IT service management (ITSM), HR, and other internal help desks. Barista connects natural-language employee requests to automation by integrating with any REST-API-enabled third-party system (ServiceNow, Jira, Slack, Teams, Okta, Workday, Microsoft 365) via its Integration Designer and Barista Integration Marketplace, and reports employee adoption rates of 80-85% with 50-70% reductions in help-desk call volume. Espressive was acquired by Resolve (resolve.io) in September 2025 and folded into Resolve's agentic automation and orchestration platform; the standalone www.espressive.com surface now redirects to resolve.io. Espressive exposes no public developer API of its own -- Barista is a consumer of customer REST APIs, and product/developer documentation sits behind the Espressive support portal.

providers.name: Mecka AI
providers.description: Mecka AI is the data and deployment layer for physical AI — it captures, structures, and evaluates real-world human and robot activity into datasets that robotics and embodied-AI teams can train on. Rather than building robots, Mecka positions itself as the integrator of the robotics ecosystem, plugging into hardware makers, frontier model labs, and commercial partners and owning the last-mile data, annotation, QA, and evaluation layer between them. Its Egoverse dataset captures large-scale first-person (egocentric) human activity across tasks and environments, and a companion iOS app lets teams collect task-specific data at scale. Mecka is backed by Forerunner Ventures and raised a $60M Series A in 2026. As of this pass Mecka publishes a marketing site, an iOS data-collection app, and the Egoverse data platform, but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pyka
providers.description: Pyka is an Alameda, California company that designs and manufactures large, dual-use heavy-lift autonomous electric aircraft for commercial and defense operations. Its flagship products are the Pelican 2 autonomous crop-protection aircraft for aerial application and the DropShip long-range heavy-lift cargo UAS. Pyka builds a fully integrated, vertically owned autonomy stack — an Autonomy Engine (real-time OS, sensor fusion, flight control, and path planning), a Mission Control operator suite (simulation, communications, and operator interface), and custom aerospace-grade hardware. The company is backed by DCVC and Obvious Ventures. Pyka does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint. Surfaced via VC portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: Sensmore
providers.description: Sensmore (sensmore GmbH) is a German industrial-automation and embodied-AI company that turns robotics research into field-proven systems for heavy machinery in raw material operations. Its platform connects machines, sites, and data across mining, aggregates/construction, and defense, spanning products including Site Intelligence (live site operations), Machine Assist (driver assistance and collision warning), Eye (visual monitoring), Live Mapping (real-time site mapping), and Loader Automation (autonomous vehicle systems), with claims of reducing downtime by up to 30% while improving safety and resource efficiency. Sensmore was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation; its web presence is a marketing and corporate site.

providers.name: Sunrise
providers.description: Sunrise Robotics builds intelligent, two-armed autonomous robotic cells for manufacturing. The AI-driven system combines built-in perception and environmental awareness with autonomous execution to transform existing production processes, increase capacity, and free human workers for higher-value tasks. Cells deploy quickly (needing only a three-phase outlet), are flexible across manufacturing applications, and are built to ISO 10218 / TS 15066 safety standards. The company is backed by Seedcamp and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: teaBOT
providers.description: teaBOT is a Toronto-based hardware startup (Y Combinator, Summer 2015) that builds an automated loose-leaf tea-making robot offered to offices, showrooms, and lounges as an amenity-as-a-service. For a flat monthly fee, teams use the companion teaBOT app to explore premium teas and dispense a custom-blended cup in under 30 seconds, which companies such as Google, HubSpot, and McKinsey use as a workplace recruiting and retention perk. Founded by robotics PhD Rehman Merali, teaBOT runs a physical-product and mobile-app business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Truvio
providers.description: Truvio is a unified software portfolio company providing intelligent, AI-driven automation solutions for Microsoft Dynamics 365 across finance, operations, Business Central, and commerce. Its practitioner-built solutions span Accounts Payable automation (ExFlow), Banking & Treasury automation (SKSoft), eCommerce and Product Information Management (DynamicWeb), and Project & Production Management (Axtension), embedding expertise directly into Dynamics 365 to help organizations close the ERP value gap. Backed by Insight Partners. No public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Chef Robotics
providers.description: Chef Robotics is a San Francisco, California physical-AI company building AI-enabled robots for high-mix food production. Its core product is an NSF-certified food-assembly robot that picks, scoops, and deposits a wide range of ingredients — fresh, cooked, IQF, sauces, leafy greens, mixed vegetables, and discrete piece items — into trays, burritos, wraps, pizza bases, and other containers on conveyor lines. The robots are powered by ChefOS, a proprietary Generalized Food Manipulation Model trained on tens of millions of real-world servings and tens of thousands of hours of production data, combining vision, decision-making, and robot control across a See / Think / Act stack with continuous Fleet Learning. Chef Robotics sells via a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that bundles hardware, software updates, 24/7 monitoring, and customer success. Deployed customers include Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice, and Chef Bombay, with the fleet having produced 98+ million servings across the US, Canada, and Europe. The company is venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins, Avataar Ventures-led $43M Series A, Bloomberg Beta, Construct Capital) and serves frozen meals, fresh meals, co-manufacturing, D2C meal delivery, medically tailored meals, meatpacking, airline catering, and foodservice verticals. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for ChefOS — the platform is operated as a closed, fleet-managed service on Chef-owned hardware deployed inside customer facilities.

providers.name: Generalist AI
providers.description: Generalist AI, Inc. is a frontier AI research and product-driven company building general intelligence for the physical world — training robots that work autonomously across factories, warehouses, laboratories, restaurants, farms, homes, and beyond. Its flagship model, GEN-1, is a general-purpose embodied foundation model trained from scratch that reaches mastery of simple physical tasks, going beyond world models and vision-language-action (VLA) approaches. Backed by Spark Capital, the company publishes its research through a blog and open-sources vision and robotics tooling on GitHub. Generalist AI exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: iRobot
providers.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

providers.name: Peer Robotics
providers.description: Peer Robotics builds collaborative autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for manufacturing and warehouse material movement, designed to learn directly from humans to lower the cost and complexity of traditional automation. Its lineup includes the Peer 3000 collaborative mobile robot and the RM250 and RM500 AMRs (250kg and 500kg payloads) that handle pallets, trolleys, bin delivery, and machine tending through an intuitive human-robot dashboard interface. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a hardware and robotics product line rather than a public developer API surface; no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or GitHub repositories were found during enrichment probing.

providers.name: Vayu Robotics
providers.description: Vayu Robotics is a Palo Alto, California robotics company building AI foundation models and sensing for autonomous mobile robots. Its stack spans Vayu Drive, an end-to-end learned, sim-first foundation model for mobility; Vayu Sense, a plenoptic sensor with embodied AI for high-resolution depth perception; a Vayu Sense Development Kit bundled with NVIDIA Orin; and Vayu One, a low-cost autonomous delivery robot for last- and middle-mile delivery. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company was acquired by Serve Robotics in September 2025. Enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Cosmic Robotics
providers.description: Cosmic Robotics, Inc. designs and operates autonomous construction equipment that takes on the hardest, most dangerous jobs on a construction site, coordinated as a fleet by a single software layer. Its first market is utility-scale solar energy, with expansion planned into data center construction. The flagship Cosmic-1A is a purpose-built robotic platform for solar panel installation, and Constellation is the coordination and control layer that plans, dispatches, and monitors the robot fleet across a jobsite. Founded in 2023 and based in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco, the company is backed by Y Combinator. Cosmic Robotics is currently a hardware and fleet-software company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and any agent-facing surfaces (such as its published llms.txt) as the API Evangelist network enrichment pipeline monitors it for a future API.

providers.name: Lemnos Labs
providers.description: Lemnos Labs, Inc. is an early-stage deeptech venture capital firm that invests at the earliest phases of hardware company formation, helping founders better understand their customer, anticipate problems, and leverage their assets. Lemnos contributes engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and financial capital alongside the check, and deliberately keeps a minimal public presence — its site is a single page that lists only the active portfolio. That portfolio spans robotics and autonomy (Built Robotics, Fort Robotics, Path Robotics, Scythe Robotics, Simbe Robotics, Petra), agricultural technology (FarmWise, Ceres Imaging), autonomous cargo aviation (Elroy Air), space data and precise positioning (Spire, Swift Navigation), simulation (Duality), video analytics (Lumeo), and physical security (Rhombus). Lemnos itself publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital entity whose value to the network is its portfolio graph — several of its companies are meaningful API providers in their own right.

providers.name: Twolabs
providers.description: Twolabs is a San Francisco robotics startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building Tobi, a modular humanoid robot platform for builders to collect data, train skills, and deploy autonomous robots. The two-founder company vertically integrates hardware and AI in-house, streamlining robot training into a Record, Upload, Train, Deploy workflow, and is initially focused on caregiving applications in senior-care facilities such as feeding, dressing, medication reminders, mobility support, and companionship. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Unmannd
providers.description: Unmannd (Unmannd Autonomy Pvt Ltd) is an India-based defense technology company backed by Accel and Speciale Invest, engineering autonomous drones under the banner of aerial dominance. Its TITAN 30 is an autonomous defense-logistics drone with a 30 kg max payload, 60 km/h cruise speed, 20,000 ft operational ceiling, and 30 km max range; its FURY counter-UAS interceptor was announced as launching in Q1 2026. Unmannd is a hardware/defense company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Veo Robotics
providers.description: Veo Robotics built FreeMove, a 3D depth-sensing computer vision safety system that lets standard industrial robots work safely alongside people by monitoring workcells and dynamically restricting or resuming robot motion. Backed by GV and Lux Capital, the company's assets - including FreeMove and related intellectual property - were acquired by Symbotic in July 2024, and veobot.com now redirects to symbotic.com. Veo Robotics published no public API surface; this profile records the company in the API Evangelist network graph.

providers.name: Bash Shell
providers.description: GNU Bash (Bourne Again SHell) is the default Unix shell and command-line interpreter on most Linux distributions and macOS. Developed by Brian Fox for the GNU Project as a free replacement for the Bourne shell, Bash provides a rich scripting language with variables, control structures, functions, I/O redirection, job control, and process management. Bash scripts are the foundational automation tool for system administration, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps tooling, and software build systems.

providers.name: Boxbot
providers.description: Boxbot builds next-generation supply chain automation, making logistics operations more productive, intelligent, and resilient through automated, high-density dynamic storage that unlocks new AI-driven capabilities. Its platform is designed for mission-control fulfillment facilities: real-time space allocation packs variable-sized items densely, hands-free load/unload moves items onto and off proprietary storage trays linked to standard conveyors with no pick or load stations, and a modular, gantry-based architecture delivers a robust, fault-tolerant design with no single point of failure. Boxbot is a hardware/robotics company backed by Playground Global; it publishes a marketing presence but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Monumental
providers.description: Monumental builds autonomous construction robots and the software that runs them. Its robots lay bricks and blockwork on real building sites, coordinated by Monumental's software platform (Atrium) and fleet operations (Fleet). The venture-backed company operates across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and has raised multiple funding rounds (including a reported $32M raise and Series B rounds in the US and UK). Monumental was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation - this record captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Akara Robotics
providers.description: Akara Robotics (akara.ai) is a healthcare automation company building an integrated hardware-plus-AI platform for hospitals across Europe and the United States. Its AI Room Sensor passively captures surgical event data in the operating room as a hospital data layer, an AI platform turns that operational data into real-time staff coordination and actionable insights, and Violet, its clinically validated autonomous robot, uses high-intensity UV light to disinfect surfaces up to six times faster than manual cleaning. The company emphasizes hardware-level data deidentification for privacy compliance, single-provider delivery of the full system, no upfront capital cost, and installation in under an hour. Akara publishes a marketing and careers site but no public developer API, documentation, or OpenAPI surface at this time.

providers.name: Lincoln Electric Holdings
providers.description: Lincoln Electric Holdings is a global manufacturer of arc welding products, robotic welding systems, plasma and oxyfuel cutting equipment, and brazing and soldering alloys. The company also offers connected welding solutions and equipment monitoring software for industrial environments.

providers.name: Shotwellai
providers.description: Shotwell AI is a Y Combinator-backed startup building an observability and annotation layer for robotics training data. Its pipeline ingests raw teleoperation video, robot logs, and multimodal sensor streams, then uses models to watch every frame, segment continuous motion into discrete actions, and label each action against a customer's task definition and SOP rubric. Every label is quality-scored and returned in hours rather than weeks, producing dense, frame-accurate, training-ready datasets for robot manipulation, deformable/folding tasks, teleoperation episode QA, and vision-language-action (VLA) foundation-model post-training. As of enrichment the company exposes only a marketing website and a sales contact (hello@shotwell.ai); no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: AliciaBots
providers.description: AliciaBots is a maritime robotics company, backed by Techstars, that builds autonomous robot teams for cleaning and inspecting ship hulls. Its flagship Roverclean robot operates independently to remove marine growth and monitor hull condition in real time without interrupting a vessel's voyage, using self-learning adaptive systems, precision cleaning, and remote monitoring and control to improve fuel efficiency and help operators meet IMO regulatory standards. AliciaBots does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks the company as a network lead.

providers.name: Andrenam
providers.description: Andrenam is a defense technology company building an AI-powered maritime sensing network for undersea surveillance. It develops mass-manufacturable, low-cost buoy-based autonomous sonar systems that deploy from manned and unmanned vessels to detect, track, and identify real-time maritime traffic using cloud and edge AI, then dispatch resources to priority areas. Its product line spans deployment, AI-enhanced detection, and integration with naval command-and-control systems, targeting government and military maritime-domain-awareness customers. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: COSY
providers.description: COSY (CosyRobo) is a retail-technology robotics company that builds autonomous inventory robots for physical stores. Its flagship robot, SCOUT, roams store aisles using AI and machine vision to scan shelves, map products, audit stock levels, and check planogram compliance, feeding the results into a cloud-based management system so retailers can reduce out-of-stocks and improve on-shelf availability. Backed by 500 Global, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Dyna
providers.description: DYNA Robotics builds commercial-grade, general-purpose robots for real-world automation across factories, restaurants, and laundromats. Its flagship DYNA-1 is a dual-arm robotic system powered by a vision-language-action (VLA) foundation model, running 24/7 in production with a reported 99.4% success rate and human-level dexterity. The company positions itself as building embodied AGI through high-performance robots that adapt across environments and learn new skills rapidly with minimal custom engineering. Backed by CRV, DYNA closed a $120M Series A in 2025. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface has been published to date; this profile tracks the company as an AI/robotics lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: emergen
providers.description: emergen (智昌科技集团股份有限公司, Zhichang Technology Group) is a Chinese industrial intelligence company founded by Dr. Gan Zhongxue, an expert in intelligent manufacturing. Built around its proprietary "ternary control" technology and cluster (swarm) robotics, the company positions itself as "AI + Control," delivering integrated "industrial agent" solutions that install a control "brain" into individual machines, production lines, and whole factories. Its portfolio spans robot controllers, ubiquitous controllers, industrial and collaborative robots, life-science robots, GVision 2D/3D machine vision, the GSC-AI100 sense-compute-control AI controller, a swarm-intelligence network controller, a micro-control cloud platform, and the "Jiangxin" family of industrial large models (design, production, service, and management). emergen serves automotive, electronics, equipment manufacturing, steel, metallurgy, textile, furniture, and shipbuilding sectors, plus Robotics-as-a-Service. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass no public developer/API surface was found.

providers.name: finern
providers.description: Finern (Finern Automation) is a China-based industrial automation company that designs and builds fully automated production lines and intelligent measurement systems for manufacturing. It serves five sectors — automotive, electronics, new energy (battery/EV), healthcare/pharmaceutical equipment, and consumer goods — with automated assembly, testing, and inspection systems. The company reports 600+ personnel, 30,000+ square meters of facilities, 100+ global clients, 8 international sites, and 4 R&D centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Finern publishes a corporate marketing website but does not currently expose any public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface (no /.well-known/*, llms.txt, or OpenAPI found on probe).

providers.name: Generalist
providers.description: Generalist (Generalist AI) is a frontier AI research and product company building general intelligence for the physical world — embodied foundation models that train general-purpose robots to perform real-world physical tasks with human-level dexterity. Founded in 2024 by researchers drawn from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Boston Dynamics (contributors to PaLM-E, RT-2, Gemini Robotics, Atlas, Spot, and the scaling of ChatGPT and GPT-4), the company has released GEN-0 and GEN-1 — large multimodal embodied models that emit robot actions in real time across factories, warehouses, laboratories, restaurants, farms, homes, and space applications. GEN-1 is positioned as the first general physical AI model to cross a commercial-viability threshold. Generalist raised $400M in 2026 at roughly a $2B valuation ($500M+ total). It operates from the San Francisco Bay Area and Boston and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Hammoq
providers.description: HAMMOQ is an AI-powered resale and recommerce platform that streamlines the processing and listing of secondhand goods for resellers, liquidators, thrift and retail organizations. Its Listing Solution turns photographs into marketplace-ready listings: machine vision identifies each item's attributes and category, generative AI writes SEO-optimized titles and descriptions, and virtual assistants quality-check each listing before it is published across resale marketplaces such as eBay, Poshmark, Mercari, Amazon and Etsy. HAMMOQ also offers Sorting and Photography solutions and an Infinity AI Chrome extension that autofills item specifications during listing. The company raised a $24M round to tackle the growing retail-returns and used-goods market. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Sierra Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; HAMMOQ publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification at this time.

providers.name: Orchard Robotics
providers.description: Orchard Robotics (Orchard AI, "The AI Farming Company") is an agricultural technology startup founded in 2022 that builds AI-powered camera systems and farm-management software for precision fruit and vine growing. Its FruitScope platform mounts AI-enabled cameras on any farm vehicle to collect precise per-tree and per-vine data — fruit count, size, color, and growth rate — which is stored in FruitScope Vault and surfaced through FruitScope OS for crop decision-making, with a Vineyard Robotics division serving grape growers. Backed by General Catalyst, the company has raised roughly $22M. As of this profile Orchard Robotics publishes a marketing and careers website but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Presto Automation
providers.description: Presto Automation (now operating as Presto Phoenix, Inc.) is a Silicon Valley-based voice AI and automation provider for restaurant drive-thrus and quick-service restaurant (QSR) chains. Its flagship product, Presto Voice, is an AI-driven drive-thru ordering assistant that automates order taking using in-house Natural Language Understanding (NLU) and large language models combined with automated speech recognition (ASR) and text-to-speech (TTS), with optional human-in-the-loop supervision. Presto offers a full spectrum of operating modes (supervised AI, pure AI, agent-led, and unsupervised AI) and has expanded into AI-native phone ordering for QSRs. Presto Voice integrates into existing drive-thru hardware, confirmation boards, headsets, and POS platforms through partnerships with vendors such as Oracle, PAR, and Qu, and draws on AI partnerships with OpenAI and ElevenLabs. Presto does not publish a public or partner-facing developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; integrations are arranged directly with the company through vendor and POS partnerships, so no API products are listed here.

providers.name: Rhoda Ai
providers.description: Rhoda AI develops robotic intelligence for real-world industrial and commercial environments, building general-purpose foundation models that adapt to the variability of physical work through its Direct Video Action model. Its robots handle tasks across automotive, manufacturing, logistics, and ecommerce, including returns processing, component handling, and material breakdown. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of Mayfield and currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Smacktechnologies
providers.description: Smack Technologies is a frontier AI lab dedicated to national security, building domain-specific multimodal models trained via deep reinforcement learning in synthetic warfare environments to deliver decision dominance to the U.S. Department of War, its allies and partners. The company ships two product suites — Omega, a command-level AI stack pairing frontier models with customer-specific applications for strategic decision-making, and Alpha, an edge-level stack of lightweight models on proprietary hardware for tactical platforms and autonomous systems. Founded by MARSOC veterans Andrew Markoff and Clint Alanis and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Smack has raised $32M across Seed and Series A rounds led by Felicis. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs — a defense-domain vendor with no external developer surface.

providers.name: Fantasmo
providers.description: Fantasmo builds CPS (Camera Positioning System), a computer-vision positioning technology it positions as a "camera-powered GPS replacement" delivering hyper-accurate localization that works indoors and in dense urban environments where satellite GPS degrades, using only a device camera and a data connection rather than additional infrastructure. Its target applications span micromobility (scooter/bike tracking and theft prevention), robotics navigation, mobile augmented-reality experiences, and automotive lane-level positioning. Fantasmo was a Techstars-backed startup and was acquired by Niantic in 2022; the public fantasmo.io site remains online but exposes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at this time. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web presence and live DNS/TLS/HTTP probes.

providers.name: Fortive
providers.description: Fortive Corporation is a Fortune 500 diversified industrial technology conglomerate headquartered in Everett, Washington. The company operates across two main segments, Advanced Healthcare Solutions and Intelligent Operating Solutions, providing essential technologies for medical device safety, radiation protection, workflow automation, hazard detection, and predictive maintenance through its operating companies. This repository captures any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Fortive at the parent company level. Most APIs and developer resources are maintained by Fortive's individual operating companies.

providers.name: Inviscid AI
providers.description: Inviscid AI is a San Francisco-based startup (Y Combinator W2026) building physics-informed AI for real-time cooling and airflow simulation of buildings and industrial facilities. Its platform combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with physics-informed neural networks to run thermal digital twins up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD, ingesting live data from building management systems, meters, and IoT sensors to autonomously recommend HVAC setpoints and optimize airflow. Target facilities include data centers, offices, hospitals, and cold storage, where the company claims 30%+ energy savings and sub-90-day ROI. As of mid-2026 Inviscid AI is a pre-product-launch company with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending an external API.

providers.name: RoboDock
providers.description: RoboDock is an autonomous robotics company (Y Combinator W2026) building the robotics layer that powers autonomous EV and AV depots, starting with charging and inspections. Its robots automate depot operations for electric and autonomous vehicle fleets, handling vision-guided plug insertion with verified connection, automated post-trip vehicle inspection, and closed-loop learning that improves efficiency with each charge event. The company targets live EV and AV depots, ports, and logistics yards where charging and core depot operations are still performed manually multiple times per day across mixed fleets. RoboDock is a hardware and robotics business rather than an API provider; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation. Founded by Zinny Weli (CEO, ex-Zipline and Amazon robotics) and Celine Wang (CTO, ex-Plus autonomous systems).

providers.name: Forge Robotics
providers.description: Forge Robotics is a Galway, Ireland and San Francisco based robotics company building modular autonomous factories for metal fabrication. Its shipping container sized, software configurable units combine a vision system, sub millimeter 3D scanning, and robotic intelligence to autonomously handle, position, weld, laser engrave, and finish metal assemblies, turning conventional human programmed industrial welding robot arms into autonomous members of the workforce. The company targets the skilled welder shortage in US manufacturing with continuously operating, snap together production modules. Forge Robotics was co founded by Eoin Cobbe (CEO) and Robert Cormican (CTO) and is a Y Combinator backed pre seed startup. As of this profile the company exposes a marketing and product website only, with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Physical Intelligence
providers.description: Physical Intelligence (often styled "Pi" or "π") is a San Francisco-based research company building general-purpose foundation models for robotics with the stated goal of producing learning algorithms that can control any robot to do any task. The company has published a continuing line of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: π0 (October 2024, first generalist multi-task multi-robot policy), π0-FAST (autoregressive variant via Real-time Action Chunking / FAST tokenization), π0.5 (April 2025, open-world generalization), π*0.6 (November 2025, reinforcement-learning from experience), and π0.7 (April 2026, steerable model with emergent capabilities). Physical Intelligence releases significant work as open source: the openpi repository (~12K stars) is the canonical home for π0 weights and code, with companion repos including real-time-chunking-kinetix, pi-data-sharing, aloha, augmax, and rlds_dataset_builder. The company does not yet offer a hosted commercial API; access to the platform is via open-weight models and research collaborations.

providers.name: Pony.ai
providers.description: Pony.ai is a global autonomous-mobility company founded in Silicon Valley in 2016 and dual-headquartered in Guangzhou and Fremont. Its core technology is the Pony "virtual driver", a Level 4 autonomous driving stack deployed across three business lines: Robotaxi (PonyPilot+ ride-hailing service operating in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, plus pilots in California and Arizona), Robotruck (autonomous heavy-duty trucking in China), and Personally Owned Vehicle (POV) intelligent driving software for production passenger cars. The company is publicly listed on NASDAQ under PONY and reports more than 32 million kilometres of autonomous road testing. Pony.ai does not publish a traditional public developer API; its public GitHub presence includes infrastructure tooling such as pony_aim (experiment tracker) and bazel-buildfarm rather than the AV stack itself. This profile captures the company surface and any developer-relevant artifacts.

providers.name: Seasats
providers.description: Seasats designs and manufactures autonomous uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs) for ocean intelligence, maritime domain awareness, and defense missions. Its platform lines include the hand-deployable Lightfish (6-month endurance), the fast-response Quickfish (35+ knots with an integrated drone bay), and the heavy-payload Heavyfish. Vessels carry modular payloads, run persistent autonomous surveys, and integrate with existing command-and-control (C2) architectures. Seasats is a Techstars-backed company. As of this enrichment pass Seasats publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; its integration story is C2 interoperability, not a web API.

providers.name: Tuza
providers.description: Tuza is a banking automation platform that orchestrates AI agents, customers and workflows to eliminate the manual processes that slow banks down. Originally launched in the UK at tuza.co.uk as a card-payment fee comparison and switching service for merchants, the company has repositioned as Tuza AI, delivering agentic automation for banks. It is an early-stage, venture-backed fintech (backed by Northzone) building a product that connects AI agents with core banking operations and customer-facing workflows. As of this profile Tuza publishes a marketing and careers site only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface has been released yet, so this record captures verified company identity plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Wing
providers.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities. Wing was the first company to receive an FAA Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate for drone delivery (2019) and is an approved LAANC USS in the United States and an approved drone airspace authorization provider for CASA in Australia. Wing's commercial surface is split across two main platforms — the Wing Delivery Platform, a partner-only API and UI suite that lets retailers, restaurants, and logistics providers embed drone delivery into their own order flows (Walmart, DoorDash, Papa Johns, and others), and OpenSky, a consumer drone airspace authorization app and partner API. Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

providers.name: XtalPi
providers.description: XtalPi is an AI-and-quantum-physics drug discovery and materials research platform company with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and major operations in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under stock code 2228.HK. The company combines a hybrid AI plus quantum mechanics (QM) discovery engine with large-scale robotic laboratory automation to accelerate molecular research and development for pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials customers, including engagements with Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and Novartis. XtalPi's offering spans proprietary software platforms — PatSight for patent extraction, XFEP for free-energy perturbation binding-affinity prediction, XMolGen for generative chemistry, and XtalGazer for solid-state research — and intelligent automation hardware including the XmartChem intelligent synthesis workstation and ChemPlus desktop solid dispenser. Its drug discovery services cover hit discovery, hit/lead optimization, biology capabilities, focused library synthesis, and the PepiX peptide platform, complemented by sister brands Ailux (biology) and AiFChem (chemistry). XtalPi's products are delivered as enterprise collaborations, licensed software, and CRO-style services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: Aqrose Technology
providers.description: Aqrose Technology (阿丘科技) is an industrial AI machine-vision platform provider founded in Beijing in 2017 out of the Tsinghua University AI Lab, now dual-headquartered in Beijing and Singapore with offices in Suzhou, Shenzhen, Hsinchu, Berlin, Tokyo, and Seoul. The company builds AI tools, models, and turnkey systems for manufacturing quality control, safety inspection, and process optimization, with 20,000+ AI deployments across 1,200+ clients in 50+ industrial sectors. Its product line spans the AIDI defect-inspection platform, the AQVision low-code AI vision development toolkit, the AIDG toolkit, the SV2000 smart vision hardware, an AI Review System (ARS), a robot inspection system, and the AQ-VLM industrial vision-language model, serving EV batteries, automotive, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, electronics, photovoltaics, food and beverage, and packaging. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Atlas Motion Systems
providers.description: Atlas Motion Systems (atlasmotion.com) designs and builds brushless DC (BLDC) motors and actuators for defense and robotics applications, engineered around a customer's specific program and manufactured at scale. The public web presence is a single-page marketing site (hero plus a contact page); it is a hardware company that does not publish a developer portal, public API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. This profile was seeded as a Homebrew-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable identity and live domain-security probe data only. Enrichment found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Cerrion
providers.description: Cerrion builds enterprise-grade video AI agents for manufacturing. Its platform connects to existing or provided factory cameras to monitor production lines in real time, using pre-trained visual triggers to automatically detect and respond to quality defects, safety hazards, process deviations, and equipment issues. The closed-loop system can slow or stop machines, raise alarms, and escalate alerts while giving operators root-cause insight, helping manufacturers resolve problems up to 50% faster and cut downtime and scrap. Cerrion is deployed in live production across glass, food & beverage, tableware, sawmilling/timber, and CPG environments (customers include Unilever, Riedel, Schott Zwiesel, Stölzle Lausitz, Sisecam, and Verallia). Zurich-based and backed by Creandum, Y Combinator, Goat Capital, 10x Founders, and Session VC. No public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Fabrion
providers.description: Fabrion builds an AI Operating System for industrial manufacturers, applying artificial intelligence to manufacturing operations and the industrial sector. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of 8vc and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass Fabrion publishes a marketing website with AI Lab, Careers, and Contact pages, but exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, packages, MCP server, or other machine-readable developer artifacts. No developer, docs, or api subdomains resolve and no /.well-known/, llms.txt, pricing, or blog surfaces were found. This remains a lead awaiting a real API surface to enrich against.

providers.name: FIMI Technology
providers.description: FIMI Technology Ltd. (Beijing FIMI Technology Co., Ltd. / Shenzhen FIMI Robot Technology Co., Ltd.) is a consumer aerial-imaging hardware manufacturer founded in May 2014 as a member of the Xiaomi ecosystem. FIMI designs and sells affordable camera drones, handheld gimbal cameras, and smartphone gimbals, with a product lineup that includes the X8 series (X8 SE, X8 Pro, X8 Tele, X8T enterprise), the compact Mini 3, the Manta VTOL fixed-wing drone, and the PALM series gimbal cameras. The company holds hundreds of patents across flight control, wireless transmission links, mechatronic design, gimbal image-stabilization, and computer vision. FIMI is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. This is a consumer-electronics company with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces.
