Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: MOLG
providers.description: MOLG (molg.ai) is a circular manufacturing company tackling electronic waste. It operates autonomous robotic microfactories that disassemble complex devices like laptops and servers to recover components and materials for reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. MOLG also partners with manufacturers on design-for-circularity (modular snap/press-fit/latch assembly instead of screws and adhesives) and offers OriginMark, a traceability platform for tracking devices, components, and materials across their lifecycle to calculate embodied carbon and supply-chain transparency. As of this enrichment pass MOLG publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: One Robot
providers.description: One Robot is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building world-model-based simulation environments for robotics teams. Its core product learns physics and visual appearance directly from real robot data, producing simulation environments that are both visually and physically realistic so teams can train and evaluate robot manipulation policies without excessive reliance on physical robot time and real-world data collection. One Robot specializes in contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects (such as textile and box folding), and precise assembly tasks. As an early-stage two-person company it currently offers task-specific simulation collaboration rather than a public developer platform or API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network for future enrichment as any developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Seeing Systems
providers.description: Seeing Systems is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) defense technology company building autonomous, modular strike drones and AI-powered swarm coordination software at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics. Its product line includes Bandit, a cost-effective FPV drone for training and expendable missions with 30+ km of range; Banshee, an autonomous modular platform built for contested, jamming-resistant environments with 40+ km of range; and Aerie AI, swarm coordination software for multi-platform operations that lowers operator cognitive load. The company works directly with military and defense partners — including UK Royal Marine Commandos and NATO forces — rather than publishing a public developer platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of the latest enrichment pass Seeing Systems exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: VICTUS Technologies
providers.description: VICTUS Technologies builds contested-autonomy software for autonomous systems operating in GPS-denied and jamming-heavy environments. Its PhantomNAV platform delivers precise state estimation from the gravity and inertial sensors already embedded in drones, aircraft, submarines, satellites, and ships - no new hardware required - and integrates with Palantir Foundry's AIP infrastructure. VICTUS is backed by Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a marketing and platform site but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Jadu
providers.description: Jadu is a General Catalyst-backed company tracked in the API Evangelist network. Its public site at jadu.io presents JADU as AI-powered crypto trading automation built on the Hyperliquid decentralized exchange. As of this enrichment pass the site is a single-page marketing shell with no public developer surface: no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, Postman collection, changelog, pricing page, status page, GitHub organization, or /.well-known discovery documents were found (the host returns its index page for every path, so probed well-known and llms.txt hits are SPA catch-alls, not real documents). This profile therefore carries identity and a domain-security probe only; no API artifacts could be honestly derived because the provider publishes no machine-readable API surface to ground them.

providers.name: 6river
providers.description: 6 River Systems (6RS) is a warehouse fulfillment automation company founded in 2015 in Waltham, Massachusetts. Its flagship product is "Chuck," a collaborative autonomous mobile robot (AMR) that works alongside human associates to guide and optimize picking, sorting, and replenishment in distribution centers. The platform is WMS-agnostic and integrates with existing warehouse-management systems as an intelligent execution layer via a private/partner REST API for host data exchange; it does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or consumer SDKs. Norwest Venture Partners was an early investor; the company was acquired by Shopify in 2019 and by Ocado Group in 2023. The public marketing site at 6river.com currently serves a parked lander stub.

providers.name: AICE
providers.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aktoria Robotics
providers.description: Aktoria Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics company (Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch) building a teleoperation and remote-operation layer for robots under the banner "Human as API for Robots." Its platform lets operators run any robot anywhere in the world, remotely collecting operational data from robot fleets 24 hours a day, monitoring and intervening in deployed fleets, and moving hardware through a train-to-deploy-to-monitor lifecycle. Founded in 2026 by Shreenabh Agrawal (robotics, Carnegie Mellon University) and Jaskaran Singh Walia (previously a researcher at Microsoft, MIT, CMU, Cambridge, and NUS), the company is at the pre-product-launch stage and does not yet publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: DevOps
providers.description: DevOps is a cultural and technical movement that combines software development and IT operations to shorten the development lifecycle and deliver high-quality software continuously. It emphasizes automation, collaboration, monitoring, and infrastructure as code to bridge the gap between building software and running it in production. DevOps spans tooling categories including version control, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, observability, and security integration.

providers.name: DevSecOps
providers.description: Development, Security, and Operations methodology that integrates security practices within the DevOps process, emphasizing security automation and collaboration throughout the software development lifecycle. DevSecOps treats security as code, favors continuous monitoring and proactive testing, and delivers compliance and security capabilities as services consumable by development teams. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

providers.name: Embark Trucks
providers.description: Embark Trucks was an autonomous-trucking company founded in 2016 and backed by Y Combinator, building a self-driving software stack (the Embark Driver) for Class 8 semi-trucks operating on interstate highway freight lanes. The company went public via a SPAC merger with Northern Star Investment Corp II in late 2021, but wound down operations in November 2023 after failing to secure additional funding; its autonomous-driving technology and engineering assets were subsequently acquired by Applied Intuition. Embark never operated a public developer platform, REST API, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile is an identity record rather than a live API. Its only surviving public technical surface is the embarktrucks GitHub organization, which hosts open-source robotics and autonomous-vehicle tooling (ROS drivers, LIDAR/camera integrations, and the webviz visualization libraries) rather than first-party API client SDKs.

providers.name: Experiential Labs
providers.description: Experiential Labs is an applied AI research laboratory (Y Combinator Summer 2026, San Francisco) building world models that let AI agents simulate reality with high fidelity. Founded by Kion Fallah (former staff research scientist at Waabi) and Silen Naihin (AutoGPT and agent-benchmark contributor, co-founder of Stackwise), the company adapts techniques from autonomous-vehicle development to reconstruct environments at high accuracy and pursue recursive self-improvement and continual learning across domains. Its public work is open source on GitHub, including the world-model-harness (world-model-as-a-harness for simulating AI agent environments), OpenCLaaS (Continual Learning as a Service), and autoresearch-distillation. The company does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Gigacatalyst
providers.description: Gigacatalyst is a Y Combinator-backed enterprise AI platform that turns customer requirements into configured software demos, POCs, UAT environments, and implementation workspaces by writing real configurations through a customer's existing product APIs. It embeds an AI customization layer directly into SaaS applications so that sales, solutions-engineering, and customer-success teams can build the missing features and workflows they need using natural language, while inheriting the host product's authentication and role-based access controls, sandboxed execution, and AI model restrictions. Gigacatalyst is an API consumer: it operates on top of other providers' APIs rather than publishing its own public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: INDEX Robotics
providers.description: INDEX Robotics is a South Korean humanoid robotics startup based in Seongnam (Bundang) building high-precision actuators and upper-body humanoid robots for high-mix, low-volume industrial work. Its core products are the IA Series, a family of high-precision actuators purpose-built for humanoid joints, and INDEX01, a compact upper-body humanoid prototype that deliberately foregoes a mobile base so it can slot into constrained factory workspaces for logistics handling, machining support, and precision assembly. The company treats joint precision, responsiveness under sustained repetitive motion, and long-run performance consistency as the core unsolved problems in humanoid commercialization. In February 2026 INDEX Robotics closed a $1M (KRW 1.5B) seed round led by Futureplay with Bass Ventures and 500 Global co-investing. This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Medra
providers.description: Medra builds an AI-powered robotic platform for autonomous laboratory work in the life sciences. Its "Physical AI Scientist" combines robotic hardware, computer vision, and scientific reasoning AI to design, execute, and continuously optimize experiments — gene editing, RNA/nucleic-acid work, antibody design, and cell-based assays — the way a human scientist would. Units are deployed at partner sites including Genentech and Addition Therapeutics, with a DARPA collaboration on its AI Experimentalist reasoning layer. Founded by Michelle Lee and headquartered in San Francisco, Medra raised a $52M Series A (Dec 2025) from investors including Lux Capital and Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Medra publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: NODA AI
providers.description: NODA AI is a defense-technology company building autonomous force orchestration for the frontlines. Founded in 2024 in Austin, Texas by Global War on Terrorism veterans, it develops URZA, an AI-native strategic orchestration platform that acts as a tactics repository and reasoning engine for real-time task brokering across vendor-agnostic, mixed-fleet autonomous assets, integrated with 30+ OEM vehicles and control systems from subsurface to space; and LARIA, a synthetic weapons-and-tactics training environment that uses digital-twin modeling to develop and test autonomous plays. In February 2026 the company raised a $25M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners to serve the U.S. Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and the UK Ministry of Defense. NODA AI is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Bloomberg Beta. It publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs; its GitHub organization holds no public repositories.

providers.name: Orby AI
providers.description: Orby AI is an enterprise generative process automation company that uses Large Action Models, neuro-symbolic reasoning, and agentic process discovery to observe how people work and then automate repetitive back-office and desktop workflows across applications. Founded by former DeepMind and Google researchers, Orby was backed by Wing Venture Capital and NEA before being acquired by Uniphore in August 2025, where its technology now powers the Uniphore Business AI Cloud. Orby publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; its capabilities are delivered as an enterprise platform accessed via demo and sales engagement.

providers.name: Philon
providers.description: Philon is a Y Combinator-backed robotics research company building open-source, general-purpose humanoid robots capable of performing unsafe, repetitive, or boring tasks. Philon develops foundational AI models for embodied agents, including Holo 1.0, a generalist vision-language-action model that navigates virtual 3D worlds and completes hour-long objectives, alongside research on generative memory, focused attention for massive context windows, and latent steering of action experts. The company publishes its models and research code openly on GitHub.

providers.name: Pickle Robot Company
providers.description: Pickle Robot Company builds Physical AI robots for supply chain automation, focused on autonomously unloading non-palletized goods (floor-loaded boxes and parcels) from trucks and shipping containers at warehouse speed. Its Dill Autonomy Engine (DAE) combines classical optimal control with generative AI and machine vision so fleets improve continuously across deployments, with operational dashboards reporting picks-per-hour, unload times, and package-mix analysis. Customers include UPS and Cintas. Headquartered in the Boston, Massachusetts area, Pickle Robot is a DCVC portfolio company backed by investors including Teradyne Robotics Ventures, Toyota Ventures, Catapult Ventures, Hyperplane, and VersionOne. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK; its GitHub organization hosts robotics tooling (mostly ROS/SLAM forks) rather than API client libraries.

providers.name: NPco
providers.description: NPco (NP Company) is an AI-native physics-simulation startup building AI-powered simulation for aerospace, defense, and energy engineering. Backed by Partech, it positions itself around accelerating physics simulation with AI. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a marketing site (careers plus a contact@npco.ai address) with no public developer portal, API, documentation, or SDKs surfaced. This profile remains a lead in the Industrial, Energy & IoT sector pending any future developer/API surface.

providers.name: AMI Labs
providers.description: AMI Labs is a frontier AI research lab building intelligent systems that understand the real world. The lab develops world models trained with self-supervised learning on continuous, high-dimensional sensor data (cameras and other sensors), aiming for AI with persistent memory, reasoning and planning, and controllable, safety-oriented behavior. Targeted applications span industrial process control, automation, wearable devices, robotics, and healthcare. AMI Labs launched officially in March 2026 with a $1.03B funding round and operates from Paris, New York, Montreal, and Singapore. It is backed by HV Capital, Obvious Ventures, and Wing Venture Capital. The lab operates as a research organization and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Arlo Industries
providers.description: Arlo Industries is a San Francisco defense hardware company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building a passive sensing network for detecting and tracking drones and aerial threats without traditional radar. Its product, Mentat, uses a distributed mesh architecture of low-cost sensors that cooperatively detect and track targets in 3D while remaining invisible to the threats they monitor. The company frames its approach around "asymmetric economics" — sensor deployment cost grows linearly while tracking accuracy grows exponentially — making the system more scalable than conventional radar installations. Arlo has demonstrated its technology with Ukrainian military operators on active frontlines and maintains partnerships across the US, Ukraine, and Northern Europe. As an early-stage hardware startup it publishes no public API, developer program, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Aurora Innovation
providers.description: Aurora Innovation is a Pittsburgh-headquartered autonomous-vehicle company publicly traded on NASDAQ as AUR. Its core product is the Aurora Driver, a self-driving system designed as a single platform deployable across vehicle classes - first commercialized in long-haul Class 8 trucking through Aurora Horizon, with Aurora Connect intended for ride-hailing applications. The Aurora Driver is integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous and PACCAR Peterbilt 579/Kenworth T680 trucks, uses Aurora's proprietary FirstLight FMCW lidar with 450+ metre range, and benefits from a NVIDIA-powered compute platform and Continental hardware partnership. Aurora launched commercial driverless freight operations in Texas in 2025 between Fort Worth, El Paso, Dallas, and Houston, with freight customers including Werner, Hirschbach, Uber Freight, FedEx, Schneider, Ryder, and Toyota Motor North America. Aurora does not publish a public developer API; the public surface is product, safety, and investor material.

providers.name: Blue River Technology
providers.description: Blue River Technology is a Santa Clara, California agricultural robotics company and John Deere subsidiary that builds intelligent farm machinery using computer vision, machine learning, and robotics. Its flagship product, See & Spray, uses onboard cameras and deep-learning models to distinguish crops from weeds in real time and target herbicide only where it is needed, cutting chemical use while improving field health. The company combines Silicon Valley software engineering with deep agricultural-equipment expertise across computer vision, full-stack software, robotics and mechatronics, product management, and field testing. Blue River Technology does not currently publish a public developer portal, API, or SDK; this profile tracks the company as a Khosla Ventures portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Calibrate Ventures
providers.description: Calibrate Ventures is a Pasadena, California venture capital firm backing visionary technical founders scaling deep tech to transform industries such as transportation and logistics, food and agriculture, healthcare, manufacturing, security, and warehousing. The firm invests in AI, computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and automation startups, partnering with founders to turn a technical breakthrough into scalable commercial advantage and drawing on decades of combined investment and company-building experience. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent company in the API Evangelist network and enriched from the firm's public web presence.

providers.name: Collaborative Robotics
providers.description: Collaborative Robotics (Cobot) is a Physical AI company founded by Brad Porter building AI-powered collaborative robots that work safely alongside people. Its flagship robot, Proxie, is a human-capable mobile manipulator designed to address labor shortages across warehousing, manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare. The company uses ScoutMap to analyze facility operations and identify automation opportunities, then deploys robots that learn real-world workflow patterns. Backed by General Catalyst, Collaborative Robotics is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it is a hardware / Physical AI provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Coolant
providers.description: Coolant (Coolant Climate, Inc.) is a climate-technology startup building AI-powered forest monitoring and carbon measurement from consumer-grade drone imagery. Its "3D spatial intelligence" platform reconstructs high-resolution 3D forest models from ordinary drone footage (DJI Mini, Mavic) and applies computer vision to measure biomass, tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), tree counts, species, and growth rates — delivering LiDAR-grade accuracy at a fraction of the cost. The company positions this as the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) layer for scalable, verifiable carbon removal, reforestation success tracking, and conservation planning. Coolant raised a $4.3M seed round from General Catalyst and Floodgate in October 2025. As of this profile the company operates a marketing site, a demo web application, and a technical blog, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: digitalsurgery
providers.description: Digital Surgery (originally Touch Surgery / Kinosis) is a London-based surgical artificial intelligence company backed by Balderton Capital and acquired by Medtronic in 2020, where it now operates as part of Medtronic's Covidien surgical business. It builds the Touch Surgery ecosystem of surgical simulation and training tools and Touch Surgery Enterprise, an AI-powered platform for recording, analyzing, and reviewing surgical video in the operating room. The company does not publish a public developer program or API; digitalsurgery.com now redirects to Medtronic's Digital Surgery product page. This profile remains a network stub awaiting a real developer surface.

providers.name: Firnas Aero
providers.description: Firnas Aero is a Saudi Arabian deep-tech startup building autonomous Drone-in-a-Box (DiaB) systems for aerial surveillance, industrial inspection, and environmental assessment. Its turnkey platform pairs self-charging, robotic battery-swapping drone stations with cloud-based remote management over 5G, Ethernet, or Wi-Fi, and applies machine-learning and deep-learning models for anomaly detection, Foreign Object Debris (FOD) detection, hazard identification, and geo-location. Based at KRTP HQ in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, the company serves infrastructure, energy, and security clients including Red Sea Global, NEOM, and the Saudi Electricity Company, and is backed by 500 Global. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Fortastra
providers.description: Fortastra is a spacecraft manufacturer building low-cost, maneuverable orbital defense systems designed for scalability and autonomous operation. Its spacecraft protect space-based infrastructure with autonomous navigation that detects, analyzes, and responds to orbital anomalies without relying on distant ground-based sensors. The company's open software architecture spans sensing, maneuvering, coordination, and response functions, and its hardware is validated through component testing, simulation, and orbital deployment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: Fyto
providers.description: Fyto is a Bay Area agricultural cleantech and robotics company, founded in 2019 by Jason Prapas with MIT origins, that builds automated cultivation systems for lemna — fast-growing aquatic "superplants" in the duckweed family. Its ReCover process, GrowGrid raised growbeds, and autonomous Harvester machine capture excess nutrients from dairy and livestock operations and convert them into high-protein animal feed, cutting nitrate pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions without arable land, synthetic fertilizer, or manual labor. Backed by GV, Fyto is scaling regenerative farming from California's San Joaquin Valley. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation is currently published.

providers.name: Generalist AI
providers.description: Generalist AI is a frontier AI research and product company founded in 2024 that is building general intelligence for the physical world. Rather than manufacturing robots, Generalist builds the embodied foundation models — the "brain" — that run across many robot types and hardware configurations, with an emphasis on dexterity and autonomy. Its founding team of researchers, roboticists, and operators comes from Google DeepMind, Boston Dynamics, and OpenAI, with prior work on PaLM-E, RT-2, Gemini Robotics, Atlas, Spot, and the scaling of large language models. The company's GEN-1 model (April 2026) is described as the first general-purpose model to reach mastery of simple physical tasks, running with full autonomy. Generalist operates from the Bay Area (San Mateo / San Francisco) and Boston, and has raised more than $500M — including a $400M round at a roughly $2B valuation backed by Nvidia, Bezos Expeditions, Radical Ventures, 8VC, Union Square Ventures, Norwest Venture Partners, Hanabi Capital, and boldstart ventures. Generalist AI currently publishes no public API or developer program; this profile captures its company identity and web presence for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GITAI
providers.description: GITAI is a space robotics company building safe and affordable robotic labor for space. It develops robotic arms, spacecraft platforms, autonomous "Inchworm" robots, and lunar rovers for on-orbit servicing, satellite assembly and maintenance, and lunar and orbital infrastructure construction, working with customers and agencies such as NASA and JAXA. GITAI operates as a B2B and government contractor and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, SDK, or developer documentation; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with the publicly observable web, blog, and domain-security surface only.

providers.name: MightyFly
providers.description: MightyFly is an autonomous air-logistics company building hybrid-electric eVTOL cargo aircraft for expedited, long-range, same-day deliveries. Its autonomous aircraft carry up to 500 pounds, travel up to 1,000 miles at roughly 150 MPH, and cut delivery emissions by around 64% versus traditional ground and air freight. MightyFly targets B2B logistics and defense delivery partnerships rather than offering a public developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or public specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Mobileye
providers.description: Mobileye is an Israel-headquartered ADAS and autonomous-driving technology company, majority-owned by Intel and publicly traded on NASDAQ as MBLY. Its flagship platform is the EyeQ family of purpose-built automotive systems-on-chip (EyeQ4, EyeQ5, EyeQ6L, EyeQ6H, EyeQ Ultra), shipped in over 175 million vehicles worldwide through partnerships with most major OEMs. Mobileye's solution portfolio spans entry-level ADAS, Mobileye SuperVision (eyes-on, hands-off highway and urban driving), Mobileye Chauffeur (eyes-off conditional autonomy), and Mobileye Drive (Level 4 full autonomy in robotaxi and goods-delivery applications). The company pioneered Responsibility- Sensitive Safety (RSS), a mathematical framework for AV decision safety contributed to IEEE standards work, and operates Road Experience Management (REM), a crowdsourced HD-mapping system that harvests anonymized road data from millions of consumer vehicles to build and update the Mobileye Roadbook. Mobileye does not publish a traditional public developer API; OEM and integration relationships are private B2B engagements.

providers.name: Movel AI
providers.description: Movel AI is a Singapore-based robotics deployment software company, founded in 2016, that makes it faster and cheaper to get autonomous mobile robots up and running in real-world environments. Its platform pairs deep learning, sensor fusion, and probabilistic planning so robots can perceive their surroundings and plan tasks on their own. Core products are the Movel Fleet Management System (FMS) for real-time monitoring and control of multi-robot fleets and Movel RNS (Robotic Navigation System) for precise single-robot navigation of complex spaces, applied across logistics, manufacturing, construction, and healthcare. The company is backed by Silicon Solution Ventures, 500 Global, AviTech, SGInnovate, Seeds Capital, and Enterprise Singapore. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Movel AI publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Nuro
providers.description: Nuro is a Mountain View-based autonomy company that has pivoted from its original autonomous-goods-delivery vehicle program (R1, R2, R3) to a licensable, vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving stack. The Nuro Driver is an AI-first Level 4 self-driving system, validated through 5+ years of driverless deployments and more than 1.7 million autonomous miles with zero at-fault incidents, paired with the Nuro Toolkit suite of supporting technology. Partners and customers include Uber and Lucid (premium robotaxi program with production-intent vehicles announced for CES 2026), Mercedes- Benz, Toyota, Kroger, Domino's, and Walmart, with NVIDIA participation in recent funding rounds. Nuro has offices in Mountain View, San Francisco, Santa Clara, Las Vegas, Houston, Toronto, Washington DC, Shenzhen, Tokyo, and an upcoming Munich expansion. Nuro does not publish a public developer API; the Driver and Toolkit are commercialized through B2B licensing rather than a self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Odyssey Ai
providers.description: Odyssey is an AI research lab building general-purpose world models — causal, multimodal systems that understand and simulate physical environments, generating long-form interactive video simulations from text or image prompts rather than text. Its research includes Odyssey-2 (a flagship world model producing multi-minute interactive simulations), Starchild-1 (a real-time multimodal world model), Agora-1 (a multi-agent world simulator), and PROWL-1 (a reinforcement-learning framework for adversarial environment exploration). Odyssey positions world models as foundational AI for robotics, gaming, healthcare, education, and 3D visual asset generation, and raised a $310M Series B. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC. At the time of this profile Odyssey publishes research, writing, and interactive demos but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Plena Health
providers.description: Plena Health is an AI operating system for specialty medical practices, founded in 2025 and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch. Plena automates the complex administrative workflows a clinic's staff shouldn't have to do — referrals, fax intake, patient calls, scheduling, prior authorization, procedure compliance, and collections — end to end, running in the background across the EHRs, clearinghouses, and other systems a practice already uses, rather than requiring the practice to adopt new software. Founded by Eyad Abdalla (CEO) and Ahmed Al Mudarris (CTO) and based in San Francisco, the company reports operating across six specialties in eight states. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Plena publishes only a marketing site (a single-page React application) with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Quantum Systems
providers.description: Quantum-Systems GmbH is a Gilching/Munich, Germany-based dual-use drone manufacturer founded in 2015 by former Bundeswehr helicopter pilot Florian Seibel. The company designs, builds, and operates small electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for reconnaissance, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition (RSTA), surveying, and mapping. Its flagship platforms include the Trinity Pro (mapping/surveying VTOL with up to 90-minute endurance), the Vector tactical reconnaissance drone (the de facto main small UAS supplier to the German Bundeswehr and, with 619+ systems delivered as of April 2025, one of the most-used Western reconnaissance drones in Ukraine), the Reliant long-range Group 2 ISR/RSTA platform built for the U.S. market with 10+ hours endurance and hot-swappable MOD-compliant payload bays (EO/IR, SIGINT, EW, CRPA), and the Ukraine-manufactured Sparta drone carrier that delivers two FPV drones to a 200 km combat radius. All platforms are operated through QBase 3D, Quantum-Systems' proprietary Windows-based mission planning, control, and post-processing software with integrated ESRI terrain data and direct export to Pix4D, Agisoft, Propeller, and Trimble Business Center. The Vector tactical line is built on Auterion's flight stack. Backed by HV Capital, DTCP, Thiel Capital, Project A, Airbus Ventures, and Omnes Capital, the company reached unicorn status in May 2025 as "Europe's first dual-use unicorn." Quantum-Systems supplies the militaries of Germany, the United States, Ukraine, Australia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Romania, and Spain. There is no public developer API, REST endpoint, SDK, or open-source release for QBase 3D or any Quantum-Systems platform; integration with Pix4D/Agisoft/Propeller/Trimble is via standard photogrammetry file exchange (GeoTIFF, RAW imagery, flight logs), not a programmable API.

providers.name: Reach Labs
providers.description: Reach Labs (operating as Reach Power Inc.) is a wireless power transmission company that delivers electrical energy through the air without physical connections, describing its mission as "doing for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented approach combines energy-transmission hardware, a custom delivery algorithm, and adaptive software controls to beam power to devices across varying distances and conditions. The company targets three primary sectors: defense and intelligence (powering sensors, autonomous vehicles, and drones in remote environments), manufacturing and logistics (energizing robotics and IoT devices in industrial settings), and public safety (enabling continuous drone operations for first responders). Reach was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable metadata surface.

providers.name: Remedy Robotics
providers.description: Remedy Robotics is a medical robotics company developing what it describes as the world's first endovascular robot capable of performing entire cardiovascular and stroke procedures under onsite, remote, or autonomous control. Its stated mission is to expand timely access to life-saving vascular interventions for patients who cannot reach specialized stroke and cardiac care in time. Remedy Robotics is a portfolio company of DCVC. As a clinical-stage medical device developer, the company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Skild AI
providers.description: Skild AI is a Pittsburgh-founded robotics AI company developing the Skild Brain, a general-purpose, omni-bodied physical AI system intended to control many different robot embodiments across many tasks without being tied to a specific hardware design. The company is initially targeting three application platforms: security and inspection robots that can navigate dangerous environments, mobile manipulation systems combining grasping and navigation, and autonomous packing with dexterous skills. Skild publishes a research blog discussing topics such as learning from humans and video data. The company is backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Felicis, SoftBank, Bezos Expeditions, and other investors. Skild AI does not currently publish a public API, SDK, model weights, or developer documentation; commercial engagement appears to run through direct partnerships and pilots.

providers.name: Tekever
providers.description: Tekever is a multinational defence technology company headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal, with operations in the United Kingdom (Bath and a planned large-scale drone production facility in Swindon), France (Toulouse and Cahors), and the United States (Fayetteville, North Carolina). Founded in 2001, the company specialises in AI-driven autonomy for civil and defence missions, with its core business centred on long-endurance Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) used for Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), maritime surveillance, and electronic warfare. Its flagship platforms include the AR3, a configurable medium-range tactical UAS (designated StormShroud in service with the UK Royal Air Force), the AR5, a SATCOM-enabled long-endurance maritime and land ISR aircraft, and the ARX, a next-generation system positioned as the company's game changer. These platforms are paired with ATLAS, Tekever's real-time intelligence-as-a-service platform that fuses sensor and satellite data into actionable mission intelligence. Tekever drones are operated by the UK Ministry of Defence, the British Army, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (with the UK having committed approximately £270 million in Tekever UAVs for Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion), the European Maritime Safety Agency under a €30 million contract, the French Ministry of Armed Forces (CNES/DGA), Portugal, and NATO. The company also develops satellite technology and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities to extend its intelligence services beyond the airborne domain. Tekever's revenue model is built on government and defence contracts, platform sales, and managed ISR-as-a-service offerings; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and engagement with the company is conducted through direct sales, government procurement, and partnership channels.

providers.name: Wayve
providers.description: Wayve is a London-based embodied AI company pioneering AV2.0, an end-to-end, mapless, vehicle-agnostic approach to autonomous driving built on large-scale self-supervised learning rather than hand-engineered HD maps and rule stacks. Wayve's core technology stack includes the Wayve AI Driver (the production driving stack licensed to automakers), GAIA generative world models that synthesize realistic driving video from text and serve as simulators for policy training, and LINGO, a vision-language-action research line that uses natural language to train and explain driving decisions. Backed by SoftBank, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Uber with a 1.5 billion USD funding round, Wayve is partnering with Nissan, Mercedes-Benz, and Stellantis on production programmes, and with Uber and Nissan on a Tokyo robotaxi launch. Wayve does not publish a public developer API; its public surface is research, press, and product positioning material.

providers.name: .Prompt.md
providers.description: Reusable prompt template files for AI coding assistants, defining task-specific instructions that can be executed from chat interfaces. Used for standardizing common development tasks like code review, refactoring, and test generation.

providers.name: 6 River Systems
providers.description: 6 River Systems is a warehouse fulfillment robotics company founded in 2015 in Waltham, Massachusetts by former Kiva Systems leaders Rylan Hamilton, Jerome Dubois, and CTO Chris Cacioppo. Its flagship product is "Chuck," a collaborative autonomous mobile robot (AMR) that works alongside human associates to guide and accelerate order picking, replenishment, and sortation in ecommerce and retail warehouses. The 6RS platform is a cloud-based execution layer that sits on top of a customer's WMS/ERP and exposes a RESTful JSON/HTTPS integration API for order, task, and operational-data exchange rather than a public self-serve developer portal. Shopify acquired 6 River Systems in 2019 for roughly $450M; Ocado Group acquired it from Shopify in May 2023, and the technology now sits within Ocado Intelligent Automation (Ocado Mobile Robot System / OMRS). Chuck has been deployed across 100-plus warehouses for 70-plus customers. Added to the API Evangelist network as a menlo-ventures portfolio lead.

providers.name: 6thSense
providers.description: 6thSense is a physical-AI hardware company building the touch layer for dexterous robots. It designs and manufactures wearable tactile-sensing data gloves that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and 3D hand pose — alongside custom tactile skin molded to robot hands. Its capture stack synchronizes eight aligned modalities (tactile and pressure proxies, egocentric video, depth/RGB-D, hand pose, motion and IMU dynamics, wrist and scene cameras, dense labels and commentary, and success/failure outcomes) into model-ready demonstration datasets used to train the next generation of dexterous, manipulation-capable robots. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (S26).

providers.name: 9 Mothers Corporation
providers.description: 9 Mothers Corporation is a defense technology company founded in 2024 and based in Austin, Texas, building AI-powered counter-drone (C-sUAS) point defense systems for the FPV drone era. Its flagship product, EDDA, is a small, low-power, autonomous-capable point-defense turret that engages Group 1 suicide drones at 10-100+ meter range to protect soldiers, vehicles, and critical assets. A Y Combinator Spring 2026 company with reported sales to the U.S. Department of War, its roadmap includes Vor (passive acoustic sensor), Atla (belt-fed shotgun system), and Gleipnir (counter-drone for larger platforms). This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Advanced Metal Research
providers.description: Advanced Metal Research is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in Los Angeles building machine intelligence for American welding. The company develops American-made robotic welding cells that pair computer vision with real-time seam tracking and post-weld inspection, turning welding from a scarce manual craft into a closed-loop manufacturing system that learns from every weld as it happens. Founded in 2025 by Julian Fried, Stephen Lin, and Angus Muffatti, it targets the projected shortage of skilled welding professionals across US industrial manufacturing. The company is early-stage and hardware-focused; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Aerodome
providers.description: Aerodome was a Drone-as-First-Responder (DFR) company founded in 2023 by former California police officer Rahul Sidhu (CEO) and Kenaniah Cerny (Chief Architect). It built a fully integrated, automated, and remotely operated software platform that let public-safety agencies dispatch autonomous drones directly from 911 calls, pairing DJI drone hardware, robotic battery-swap docking nests, and radar with Aerodome DFR software featuring augmented-reality street overlays, automated flight operations, computer-aided-dispatch integration, and live airspace awareness. The company reported average 86-second response times to 911 calls. Backed by a16z, CRV, and 2048 Ventures across a seed (Oct 2023) and $21.5M Series A (May 2024), Aerodome was acquired by Flock Safety in October 2024 for over $300 million; its technology and software now ship as the Flock Safety "Flock DFR" product line, and the aerodome.com domain redirects to that product page.

providers.name: AirKit
providers.description: AirKit (Airkit.ai) was a low-code platform for building customer-facing digital experiences and, later, AI-powered customer service agents, backed by Accel and Emergence Capital. The company was acquired by Salesforce (announced 2023) and its technology now underpins Salesforce Agentforce. As of this enrichment pass, www.airkit.com 301-redirects to salesforce.com/agentforce and the domain's CAA records point to salesforce.com, so AirKit no longer operates an independent developer surface, API, documentation, or portal of its own — all first-party discovery URLs resolve into Salesforce properties. This profile is retained as an acquired-company record; enrichment beyond domain-level DNS/TLS evidence is not applicable.

providers.name: AirMap
providers.description: AirMap was a drone airspace-management and unmanned traffic management (UTM) platform that provided airspace intelligence, flight planning, digital notice, and geofencing services for drones and their operators, exposed through a developer platform of airspace and flight APIs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the company appears defunct: airmap.com no longer serves a developer portal or API and now resolves to a parked Squarespace-hosted page with a mismatched TLS certificate, and the legacy developer.airmap.com / api.airmap.com / docs.airmap.com hosts no longer resolve. No live API surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Airplane
providers.description: Airplane was a Benchmark-backed developer platform for building internal tools, dashboards, and operational workflows by turning scripts into shareable tasks and UIs. It was acquired by Airtable in 2023 and the product was subsequently wound down. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct: the website www.airplane.dev no longer connects, the airplane.dev apex resolves to a domain-parking IP, and the airplanedev GitHub organization was archived on 2026-02-03 with no public repositories. No live API, developer portal, documentation host, SDK, or event surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Airware
providers.description: Airware was an enterprise commercial-drone (UAV) software and aerial-data-analytics company founded in 2011 by Jonathan Downey and headquartered in San Francisco. It began by building an operating system and autopilot for commercial drones, then pivoted to a cloud-based "Aerial Information Platform" that captured, processed, and analyzed drone imagery for enterprise verticals such as mining, quarrying, insurance, and construction. Airware acquired French drone-analytics firm Redbird in 2016 and raised roughly $118M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, GV (Google Ventures), Intel Capital, and Next World Capital. The company ceased operations in September 2018. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no live developer surface, API, or public specification is currently discoverable (the airware.com domain no longer resolves), so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

providers.name: Aitme
providers.description: Aitme was a Berlin-based deep-tech robotics company that built a platform for automated food preparation, deploying robotic kitchen and canteen systems that cooked and assembled meals autonomously for foodservice and workplace-catering settings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company has since been acquired and exposes no public developer surface: no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or hosted domain could be located during enrichment. This profile is retained as an honest catalog record with no fabricated API artifacts.

providers.name: American Aerospace Advisors
providers.description: American Aerospace Technologies, Inc., doing business as American Aerospace Advisors, is a defense and critical-infrastructure monitoring company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. It provides end-to-end airborne intelligence systems that combine unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), airborne sensors, analytics, and communications to deliver near-real-time data through a cloud-based intelligence gateway. Its flagship AiRanger medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aircraft and InstiMaps sensor technology support pipeline and linear-asset patrol, beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) flight services, sensor integration, and aviation policy consulting. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Anon
providers.description: Anon is an enterprise AI agent platform that builds production-ready AI agents for companies. Its offerings include computer-use agents that automate long-running browser workflows, hosted web agents that perform tasks across multiple systems, and an agent authentication toolkit that gives developers tools to authenticate agents across third-party services. Originally positioned as an automated authentication layer for the gen-AI age, Anon has raised $14M from Forerunner Ventures, Union Square Ventures, and Abstract Ventures. As of this profile the company does not publish a public self-serve API, SDK, developer portal, or MCP server; engagements are handled directly (hello@anon.com).

providers.name: Atrisa
providers.description: Atrisa (formerly Refortifai) is a Y Combinator (P26) startup building AI agents for analog circuit design. The product is a chat-based assistant engineer that lets hardware and analog design teams ask it, in natural language, to create a design, debug a circuit, or run simulations. Atrisa is designed to fit into existing workflows: teams bring their own toolkit, PDKs (process design kits), and design documents, which Atrisa reads, understands, and adopts to produce schematic-level outputs and iterate on analog designs. As an early-stage company it currently ships a hosted web application rather than a public developer API, so this profile captures its identity, domain-security posture, and public surface pending any future API release.

providers.name: Axon
providers.description: Axon is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building real-time predictive intelligence on a brain-inspired architecture. Its approach centers on small, efficient "world models" that learn continuously on-device rather than depending on large models or the cloud, giving an edge-first design lower latency and lower cost. The initial focus is high-frequency trading and capital markets, where real-time prediction is decisive, with future applications targeted at wearables, edge devices, and robotics. Axon is backed by Northzone, Concept Ventures, a16z Speedrun, and EWOR. As of this profile the company is pre-product with no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal; this repository tracks it in the API Evangelist network for enrichment as its developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Bear Flag Robotics
providers.description: Bear Flag Robotics is an autonomous-tractor company that retrofits existing farm tractors with sensors, onboard compute, and path-planning software to enable driverless field operations such as tillage and row-crop work. Founded in 2017 and backed by Y Combinator and True Ventures, the company was acquired by John Deere in August 2021 and now advances Deere's autonomy roadmap. It is a hardware and agricultural-robotics business with no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or GitHub surface; its website redirects to John Deere.

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: Bumblebee Spaces
providers.description: Bumblebee Spaces is a San Francisco smart-home robotics company that builds app-controlled motorized storage systems for compact urban living. Its ceiling-mounted robotic units lift beds, closets, and storage bins up and out of the way, reclaiming floor space in small apartments, while a built-in camera and mobile app track and retrieve stored belongings on demand. The company sells and installs hardware plus a companion consumer mobile application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Canaan Partners, the profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Carmera *
providers.description: CARMERA was a New York City based road-intelligence and HD mapping company that provided "change-as-a-service" map maintenance for autonomous driving, mobility-as-a-service and consumer navigation. It used consumer-grade cameras mounted on commercial fleet vehicles as crowdsourced visual probes to detect permanent road inventory change (signs, signals, lane markings) and temporary closure events (construction), then regenerated both HD and SD maps in near real time. Its commercial offering was described as detection APIs that identify map-impacting events plus vector APIs that deliver map updates, layered over a customer-supplied or CARMERA-supplied base map. The company was backed by GV and was acquired in July 2021 by Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota), the advanced mobility subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. Its APIs were sold under enterprise agreements and were never published as a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass the carmera.com domain no longer resolves and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API artifact survives.

providers.name: Cencorp
providers.description: Cencorp (Zhuhai) Industrial Technology Co., Ltd. is a process-automation equipment manufacturer that designs and builds high-end laser processing, dispensing, automated optical inspection (AOI), and system-integration & automation systems for the consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor, and new-energy industries. Formed in 2020 and combining the acquired Finland-based Cencorp automation business with operations headquartered in Zhuhai, China, the company runs 12 offices worldwide with 400+ R&D engineers and 300+ patents, and is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this is a physical automation-equipment business.

providers.name: chowbotics
providers.description: Chowbotics was a food-robotics company known for "Sally," a fresh-food and salad vending robot that assembled customized bowls on demand for cafeterias, hospitals, campuses, and grocery locations. The company was acquired by DoorDash in early 2021 and no longer operates as a standalone business; its domain (chowbotics.com) now redirects to DoorDash (get.doordash.com). As of this enrichment pass Chowbotics publishes no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this remains an identity-only record in the API Evangelist network rather than an active API provider profile.

providers.name: Citadel
providers.description: Citadel (also branded Citadel Defense / Drone Citadel) is a counter-unmanned-aircraft-system (C-UAS) company founded in 2016 that built an automated, modular drone-defense solution using proprietary machine-learning algorithms to detect, classify, and defeat unauthorized drones. It raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series A in 2017 and was subsequently acquired by BlueHalo. The company operates no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, and its standalone domains (citadeldefense.com, dronecitadel.com) are now parked or no longer resolve.

providers.name: Cloudpipes
providers.description: Cloudpipes was a Sofia (Bulgaria) and London-based iPaaS (integration platform as a service) that provided a cloud-based integration and workflow-automation platform for connecting SaaS applications and automating business processes without code. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups / 500 Istanbul), BrightCap Ventures and LAUNCHub Ventures, the company was acquired by Vista-backed Quickbase (Quick Base) in August 2019 and its standalone product and developer surface were subsequently wound down. This API Evangelist profile is a historical/portfolio record: the cloudpipes.com origin is offline (Cloudflare 522) and no live API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts remain available to harvest.

providers.name: Concurrent Real-Time
providers.description: Concurrent Real-Time, Inc. is a provider of high-performance real-time computing systems, software, and solutions, headquartered in Pompano Beach, Florida. Its portfolio centers on RedHawk Linux, a real-time operating system based on Linux; iHawk multiprocessor computer platforms; the NightStar suite of development, debugging, and analysis tools; and SIMulation Workbench, a real-time simulation framework used for hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and model-based design. Concurrent Real-Time serves aerospace, defense, automotive, transportation, financial, and industrial simulation markets. The company traces its lineage to the real-time division of Concurrent Computer Corporation and is backed by Battery Ventures. It operates as a systems and embedded-software vendor rather than a public web-API provider, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Congruent
providers.description: Congruent builds AI-native radar hardware and simulation tooling for self-driving cars and end-to-end autonomy. The company pairs a radar architecture that exposes raw sensor data with a world-model-based generative simulator, producing both real and synthetic raw radar returns to train autonomy stacks. Radar is the only depth sensor cheap enough to scale to every vehicle while still working in rain, fog, snow, and dust, where camera and lidar systems degrade. Congruent is an early-stage Y Combinator (W26) company founded in 2025 by Clement Barthes and Evan Scope Crafts, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this profile the company operates a single marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or specification.

providers.name: Cruise
providers.description: Cruise was an autonomous-vehicle (robotaxi) company founded in 2013 and majority-owned by General Motors, building self-driving technology and operating driverless ride-hail services in San Francisco and other U.S. cities. Backed by GM, Honda, SoftBank Vision Fund, Spark Capital, Y Combinator and others, Cruise suspended operations after a 2023 incident and, in December 2024, GM announced it would end robotaxi development and fold the Cruise team into GM's own autonomous and driver-assistance programs. As of 2026 the getcruise.com domain 301-redirects to GM's autonomous-driving pages. Cruise never published a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Curious Ai
providers.description: The Curious AI Company was a Helsinki, Finland-based artificial intelligence research company founded in 2015 by Harri Valpola (previously founder of ZenRobotics) along with Antti Rasmus, Mathias Berglund, Tapani Raiko, and Timo Haanpaa. The company pursued artificial general intelligence, real-world computer vision for robots, and interactive, autonomous, and semi-supervised machine learning, and is best known for foundational research on Ladder Networks for semi-supervised deep learning. It raised roughly 4.7M USD from investors including DCVC, Lifeline Ventures, and Invus, and was acquired by Apple in January 2021. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer platform, API, documentation, or SDKs. This record is retained as a DCVC portfolio identity profile; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: CYGIA
providers.description: CYGIA (Zhuhai CYGIA Automation Equipment Co.) is an intelligent-factory equipment and solution provider founded in 2006 and headquartered in Zhuhai, China. It develops, manufactures, and services intelligent automation and automated-test equipment for consumer electronics, semiconductor and integrated-circuit, automotive, medical, and new-energy industries. Once backed by Qiming Venture Partners, CYGIA became a subsidiary of publicly traded CYG (Changyuan Group, Shanghai Stock Exchange 600525.SH) in 2015. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface for CYGIA, which is a hardware/automation-equipment manufacturer rather than an API provider.

providers.name: DeepMap
providers.description: DeepMap was a high-definition mapping and localization software company for autonomous vehicles, building HD maps, real-time localization, and map-update infrastructure that let self-driving cars know precisely where they were. Backed by a16z and Accel, DeepMap was acquired by NVIDIA in 2021 and folded into NVIDIA's autonomous-vehicle platform; the deepmap.ai domain now resolves to NVIDIA's self-driving solutions page. No independent DeepMap developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists post-acquisition. This profile is retained as a network/portfolio record.

providers.name: DeepWay 深向
providers.description: DeepWay (深向科技 / Shenxiang Technology) is a Chinese intelligent new-energy heavy-truck company, backed by Baidu and Qiming Venture Partners, that designs and manufactures electric autonomous freight trucks it calls RoboTrucks. Its vehicle line includes the Xingchen II (深向星辰 II) and Xingtu (深向星途) electric heavy trucks paired with the Tianji (天玑) driver-assistance and autonomous driving stack, an AI-based fleet management platform, and a vehicle-owner mobile app. DeepWay reports 7,500+ activated L2 vehicles, a 30%+ subscription rate, and 300M+ km of assisted-driving operation, and follows a roadmap from L2 assistance (2023) to L4 platooning (2025) to single-vehicle L4 autonomy (2028). Its business model progresses from vehicle sales to subscription services to large-scale autonomous logistics capacity. As of this enrichment pass DeepWay publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification — this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Degla Inc
providers.description: Degla is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) startup building an autonomous aerial intelligence layer that turns natural language into multi-drone mission execution. Operators describe an objective in plain language and Degla plans the mission, assigns aircraft, defines coverage patterns, and deploys a fleet that adapts in real time — with no waypoints, flight plans, or specialized training required. The platform targets search and rescue, emergency response, infrastructure inspection, and other critical field operations. Founded in 2026 by Aziz Hanafi and based in Boston, the company is in early access and has not yet published a public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: DiDi Autonomous
providers.description: DiDi Autonomous Driving (滴滴自动驾驶) is the autonomous-driving subsidiary of Chinese mobility giant DiDi. Founded as an internal research unit in 2016 and spun out as an independent company in 2019, it develops Level 4 self-driving technology and operates robotaxi services integrated into the DiDi ride-hailing platform in Chinese cities including Shanghai and Guangzhou. In 2020 SoftBank Vision Fund led a roughly $500M funding round into the unit. As a hardware- and fleet-oriented autonomous mobility operator it does not currently publish a public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Drishti Technologies
providers.description: Drishti Technologies was a Mountain View, California company (founded 2016 by Prasad Akella, Krishnendu Chaudhury, and Ashish Gupta) that applied AI-powered computer vision and video analytics to manual assembly lines in manufacturing. Its platform digitized human actions on the production floor to enable time-and-motion studies at scale, quality traceability, and continuous improvement, with products including Drishti Trace (video capture and traceability) and Drishti Flow (line analytics). The company was acquired by Apple in September 2023 and no longer operates an independent public website, developer portal, or API surface — its domains (drishti.com, drishti.ai) no longer resolve to a live product.

providers.name: Earendil Robotics
providers.description: Earendil Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company registered in England and Wales that builds AI-powered situational-awareness and counter-drone systems for tactical units. Its product line includes IVAS, an edge-AI vision-augmentation system fusing night vision, thermal imaging, and laser ranging for total-darkness operation; Aeglos, an autonomous high-speed (300+ km/h) interceptor drone for counter-UAS defense with autonomous target locking and all-weather thermal tracking; and Holo, an ultra-lightweight dual-mode tactical sight combining high-resolution thermal imaging with a fiber-optic reticle. As of this profile the company exposes only a public marketing website and a contact form, with no published developer surface, API, SDKs, documentation, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Eden Robotics
providers.description: Eden Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed robotics company building autonomous robots for industrial operations, delivered on a robots-as-a-service model that starts at roughly $10 per hour with no setup fees. The offering is positioned as plug-and-play, requiring no on-site engineers or specialized robotics hires, and is powered by the company's Theta OS platform. As of this profile the company publishes a single marketing and sales-contact website and does not expose a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this record captures the verified company identity and domain-security posture and will be upgraded if and when a developer surface is published.

providers.name: Eigentech
providers.description: Eigentech (eigentech.ai) is an artificial intelligence technology company, reported to have been founded around 2016 and headquartered in Hangzhou, China, that applies AI and machine learning to business and industrial domains. Its platform is positioned to help enterprises improve operational efficiency, optimize workflows, and strengthen data-driven decision-making by embedding AI into existing business processes. Eigentech is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for the enrichment pipeline. NOTE - as of the latest enrichment pass the company website (https://eigentech.ai) does not resolve and no public developer, documentation, or API surface could be reached, so no API artifacts could be harvested without fabrication.

providers.name: Eka Robotics
providers.description: Eka Robotics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts robotics-AI company founded in 2025 that is building intelligence for the physical world in its native language: force. Its Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model combines vision, force sensing, and action to give robots generality, performance, and safety for close human-robot interaction. The team pioneers self-supervised robot learning, large-scale robot learning, world models, reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer, drawing talent from MIT, Berkeley, Harvard, DeepMind, and Boston Dynamics. Co-founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal (Improbable AI Lab), the company is an early-stage research-and-hardware venture and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with the company's public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: EraDrive
providers.description: EraDrive is a space technology company building compact, AI-powered self-driving modules that give spacecraft onboard autonomy — vision-based navigation, control, collision avoidance, and situational awareness computed at the edge. A Stanford Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) spinoff founded by Sumant Sharma (CEO), Justin Kruger (CTO), and Prof. Simone D'Amico (CSO), EraDrive integrates flight-proven autonomy software with existing satellite infrastructure for space traffic management, on-orbit servicing and logistics, and advanced remote sensing across commercial and defense missions. The company closed an oversubscribed $5.3M seed round in December 2025, co-led by Haystack Ventures with participation from Point Nine, Harpoon Ventures, Brave Capital, 2100 VC, and Entropy Industrial Capital. As an early-stage hardware/software company, EraDrive currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Fern Bot
providers.description: Fern (operating as Ishiki Labs) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) physical-AI startup building high-fidelity, custom robot world models that let robotics companies evaluate and train their robot policies at scale in software. Fern provides plug-and-play reinforcement-learning environments generated from a foundational world model: robotics teams seed varied starting scenes from their production environments, test and improve policies entirely in simulation, and Fern generates RL heads on top of existing policies to raise speed and success rates — a continual-learning flywheel where production robots improve every week. Founded in 2025 by CEO Amit Yadav (ex-Meta LLaMA / Reality Labs research scientist) and CTO Robert Xu (ex-Meta Reality Labs and Citadel Securities). As of this profile Fern publishes a marketing site, a whitepaper, and case studies but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Figure
providers.description: Figure is a Sunnyvale, California humanoid robotics company building general-purpose bipedal robots for the home and the workplace. Its current flagship product is Figure 03, marketed as an everyday general-purpose humanoid robot, succeeding Figure 01 and Figure 02. Figure develops Helix, an in-house Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that unifies perception, language understanding, and learned control to drive a full upper humanoid body at 35 degrees of freedom and 200 Hz, with capabilities including novel-object manipulation from natural-language commands and multi-robot task coordination. Figure has run commercial pilots with partners such as BMW and previously collaborated with OpenAI on language models. The company's revenue model is robot sales/leasing and enterprise deployments; Helix is a proprietary on-board model and there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Figure or Helix.

providers.name: FireVisor
providers.description: FireVisor is an AI-based manufacturing analytics platform that helps manufacturers leverage their production data beyond traditional defect detection and process control methods. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore (with a secondary office in Toronto, Canada), FireVisor works toward "self-aware factories powered by artificial intelligence," applying machine learning to manufacturing and industrial-automation data. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this profile the public firevisor.com site returns a 404 from its load balancer and exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Fleetzero
providers.description: Fleetzero is a Houston-based maritime technology company, founded in 2021 and led by U.S. Navy veterans and shipping-industry experts, building battery-electric energy and robotics systems to decarbonize ocean shipping at cost parity with fossil fuels. Its Leviathan modular marine energy storage system, 3.8 MWh marine battery containers, and 55 MWh battery barges provide propulsion power and mobile charging infrastructure for cargo vessels. Backed by Obvious Ventures, Fleetzero was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it currently publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Flirtey
providers.description: Flirtey was a drone-delivery technology company founded in 2013 by Matthew Sweeny and Tom Bass, backed by Y Combinator. It pioneered autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle delivery, conducting the first FAA-approved drone delivery in the United States in 2016 (Nevada) and running early delivery trials with partners including Domino's (the first pizza delivered by drone, in New Zealand) and 7-Eleven. Flirtey developed the Flirtey Eagle delivery drone and portable landing/loading systems aimed at medical, food, and retail last-mile logistics. The company is now defunct: it did not maintain a public developer program or API, and the flirtey.com domain has since been sold and now redirects to an unrelated business (us-stemcell.com). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Fulfil
providers.description: Fulfil (Fulfil Solutions) is an automation company that builds robotic online-grocery fulfillment systems. Its ShopBot robots perform zero-labor pick-and-pack across all grocery temperatures and categories (ambient, refrigerated, frozen, and produce), providing item-level data and control with claimed 99% order accuracy and roughly 50% lower operating costs. The company operates automated micro-fulfillment facilities and partners with grocery and delivery operators. Backed by DCVC, Fulfil was surfaced as a portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing website but no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Futurtec
providers.description: Futurtec (鑫君特) is a Chinese medical-device company founded in 2015 and recognized as a national high-tech enterprise, focused on orthopedic surgical robotics. Its flagship ORTHBOT surgical system combines navigation with automatic robotic execution — intelligent needle placement, non-invasive positioning, dual-camera navigation, and visual force-feedback pressure protection — and holds Chinese regulatory approval (Feb 2021) and EU MDR CE certification (May 2023). The company reports 251+ patents filed or granted, including 84+ invention patents and 25+ PCT applications. As of this enrichment pass, Futurtec publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or software surface: it is a clinical hardware manufacturer, so the enrichment pipeline found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: galbot
providers.description: Galbot (银河通用机器人, "Galaxy Universal Robotics") is the official site of a general-purpose, embodied-AI robotics company. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and profiled here for API and developer-surface enrichment.
